American Civil War: Union cavalrymen defeat Confederate forces at Toms Brook, Virginia during Sheridan's Shenandoah Valley campaign.
American Civil War: The Union garrison of Glasgow, Missouri surrenders to Confederate forces.
American Civil War: The Battle of Cedar Creek ends the last Confederate threat to Washington, DC.
American Civil War: A Union attack on the Confederate capital of Richmond is repulsed.
Gregor Mendel presents his laws of heredity
Uruguayan War: The Siege of Paysandú ends as the Brazilians and Coloradans capture Paysandú, Uruguay.
American Civil War: Fort Fisher in North Carolina falls to the Union, thus cutting off the last major seaport of the Confederacy.
American Civil War: Columbia, South Carolina, is burned as Confederate forces flee from advancing Union forces.
American Civil War: A day after Union forces capture Richmond, Virginia, U.S. President Abraham Lincoln visits the Confederate capital.
William H. Seward, the U.S. Secretary of State, and his family are attacked at home by Lewis Powell.
Astronomer Angelo Secchi demonstrates the Secchi disk, which measures water clarity, aboard Pope Pius IX's yacht, the L'Immaculata Concezion.
Union cavalry troopers corner and shoot dead John Wilkes Booth, assassin of President Abraham Lincoln, in Virginia.
The Empire of Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay sign the Treaty of the Triple Alliance.
American Civil War: Nathan Bedford Forrest surrenders his forces at Gainesville, Alabama.
American Civil War: In Kentucky, Union soldiers ambush and mortally wound Confederate raider William Quantrill, who lingers until his death on June 6.
In the market square of Springfield, Missouri, Wild Bill Hickok shoots and kills Davis Tutt in what is regarded as the first western showdown.
Welsh settlers arrive at Chubut in Argentina.
Treaty of Sinchula is signed whereby Bhutan cedes the areas east of the Teesta River to the British East India Company.
Shaw University, the first historically black university in the southern United States, is founded in Raleigh, North Carolina.
Georgia ratifies the 13th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.
Bedrich Smetana's comic opera The Bartered Bride premieres in Prague.
The Fenians defeat Canadian forces at Ridgeway and Fort Erie, but the raids end soon after.
Austro-Prussian War is decided at the Battle of Königgrätz, enabling Prussia to exclude Austria from German affairs.
Reconstruction: Tennessee becomes the first U.S. state to be readmitted to Congress following the American Civil War.
The Kingstree jail fire kills 22 freedmen in Reconstruction-era South Carolina.
Queen Victoria gives Royal Assent to the British North America Act which establishes Canada on July 1.
Alaska is purchased from Russia for $7.2 million, about two cents/acre ($4.19/km2), by United States Secretary of State William H. Seward.
Coronation of Franz Joseph as King of Hungary following the Austro-Hungarian compromise (Ausgleich).
Maximilian I of the Second Mexican Empire is executed by a firing squad in Querétaro, Querétaro.
An earthquake strikes the Virgin Islands, triggering the largest tsunami witnessed in the Caribbean and killing dozens.
Pro-Imperial forces capture Osaka Castle from the Tokugawa shogunate and burn it to the ground.
The University of California is founded in Oakland, California when the Organic Act is signed into law.
Former shōgun Tokugawa Yoshinobu surrenders Edo Castle to Imperial forces, marking the end of the Tokugawa shogunate.
Boshin War: The Battle of Utsunomiya Castle ends as former Tokugawa shogunate forces withdraw northward.
The United States Senate fails to convict President Andrew Johnson by one vote.
Impeachment of Andrew Johnson: President Andrew Johnson is acquitted by one vote in the United States Senate.
The Treaty of Bosque Redondo is signed, allowing the Navajo to return to their lands in Arizona and New Mexico.
The 14th Amendment to the United States Constitution is certified, establishing African American citizenship and guaranteeing due process of law.
French astronomer Pierre Janssen discovers helium.
The Imperial Russian steam frigate Alexander Nevsky is shipwrecked off Jutland while carrying Grand Duke Alexei Alexandrovich of Russia.
The Uspenski Cathedral, designed by Aleksey Gornostayev, is inaugurated in Helsinki, Finland.
Paraguayan War: Brazilian troops defeat the Paraguayan Army at the Battle of Avay.
The largest alluvial gold nugget in history, called the "Welcome Stranger", is found in Moliagul, Victoria, Australia.
Mendeleev publishes the periodic table (6 March)
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi born at Porbandar (2 October)
In Egypt, the Suez Canal, linking the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea, is inaugurated.
In Dumbarton, Scotland, the clipper Cutty Sark is launched.
Thomas Nast publishes a political cartoon  symbolizing the Democratic Party with a donkey ("A Live Jackass Kicking a Dead Lion") for Harper's Weekly.
In Montana, U.S. cavalrymen kill 173 Native Americans, mostly women and children, in what becomes known as the Marias Massacre.
Reconstruction Era: Virginia is readmitted to the Union.
US president Ulysses S. Grant signs a joint resolution of Congress establishing the U.S. Weather Bureau.
The Manitoba Act is given the Royal Assent, paving the way for Manitoba to become a province of Canada on July 15.
The first game of rugby in New Zealand is played in Nelson between Nelson College and the Nelson Rugby Football Club.
Reconstruction Era of the United States: Georgia becomes the last of the former Confederate states to be readmitted to the Union.
Franco-Prussian War: The Battle of Sedan is fought, resulting in a decisive Prussian victory.
Franco-Prussian War: Battle of Sedan: Prussian forces take Napoleon III of France and 100,000 of his soldiers prisoner.
Franco-Prussian War: The Siege of Metz begins, resulting in a decisive Prussian victory on October 23.
During an expedition to the Wyoming Territory, Henry D. Washburn observes and names the Old Faithful Geyser.
Franco-Prussian War: The siege of Paris begins. The city held out for over four months before surrendering.
By plebiscite, the citizens of the Papal States accept annexation by the Kingdom of Italy.
Franco-Prussian War: Marshal Bazaine surrenders to Prussian forces at the conclusion of the Siege of Metz along with 140,000 French soldiers.
Joseph H. Rainey of South Carolina becomes the second black U.S. congressman.
In the Battle of Bapaume, an engagement in the Franco-Prussian War, General Louis Faidherbe's forces bring about a Prussian retreat.
Franco-Prussian War: The Siege of Paris ends in French defeat and an armistice.
Sinmiyangyo: Captain McLane Tilton leads 109 US Marines in a naval attack on Han River forts on Kanghwa Island, Korea.
The Connecticut Valley Railroad opens between Old Saybrook, Connecticut and Hartford, Connecticut in the United States.
Bishop John Coleridge Patteson, first bishop of Melanesia, is martyred on Nukapu, now in the Solomon Islands.
Yohannes IV is crowned Emperor of Ethiopia in Axum, the first imperial coronation in that city in over 200 years.
Challenger expedition: HMS Challenger, commanded by Captain George Nares, sails from Portsmouth, England.
A group of Modoc warriors defeats the United States Army in the First Battle of the Stronghold, part of the Modoc War.
Bulgarian revolutionary leader Vasil Levski is executed by hanging in Sofia by the Ottoman authorities.
Der Krach: The Vienna stock exchange crash begins the Panic of 1873 and heralds the Long Depression.
Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis receive a U.S. patent for blue jeans with copper rivets.
At Adair, Iowa, Jesse James and the James–Younger Gang pull off the first successful train robbery in the American Old West.
The Clay Street Hill Railroad begins operating the first cable car in San Francisco's famous cable car system.
Austrian explorers Julius von Payer and Karl Weyprecht discover the archipelago of Franz Josef Land in the Arctic Sea.
Cetshwayo ascends to the throne as king of the Zulu nation following the death of his father Mpande.
Chief Kintpuash and companions are hanged for their part in the Modoc War of northern California.
The Treaty of Pangkor is signed between the British and Sultan Abdullah of Perak, paving the way for further British colonization of Malaya.
Modest Mussorgsky's opera Boris Godunov premieres in Mariinsky Theatre in St.Petersburg.
The first group of Dorsland trekkers under the leadership of Gert Alberts leaves Pretoria.
Aires de Ornelas e Vasconcelos is appointed the Archbishop of the Portuguese colonial enclave of Goa, India.
Patrick Francis Healy becomes the first African-American inaugurated as president of a predominantly white university, Georgetown University.
A cartoon by Thomas Nast in Harper's Weekly, is considered the first important use of an elephant as a symbol for the United States Republican Party.
Guangxu Emperor of Qing dynasty China begins his reign, under Empress Dowager Cixi's regency.
The Herzegovinian rebellion against the Ottoman Empire begins.
The 1864 play Heath Cobblers by Aleksis Kivi premieres in Oulu, Finland.
Alexander Graham Bell patents the telephone (7 March)
The first National League baseball game is played at the Jefferson Street Grounds in Philadelphia.
A performance of Wagner's Das Rheingold opens the first Ring cycle at the first Bayreuth Festival.
Crazy Horse and his warriors fight their last battle against the United States Cavalry at Wolf Mountain, Montana Territory.
American Indian Wars: Sitting Bull leads his band of Lakota into Canada to avoid harassment by the United States Army under Colonel Nelson Miles.
American Indian Wars: Battle of the Big Hole: A small band of Nez Percé Indians clash with the United States Army.
American astronomer Asaph Hall discovers Phobos, one of Mars's moons.
Anna Sewell's animal welfare novel Black Beauty is published.
Russo-Turkish War (1877–78): Sofia is liberated from Ottoman rule.
Yale Daily News becomes the first independent daily college newspaper in the United States.
John Tunstall is murdered by outlaw Jesse Evans, sparking the Lincoln County War in Lincoln County, New Mexico.
The Russo-Turkish War ends with Bulgaria regaining its independence from the Ottoman Empire according to the Treaty of San Stefano.
Hödel assassination attempt by anarchist Max Hödel targeting the German Kaiser, Wilhelm I.
Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera H.M.S. Pinafore opens at the Opera Comique in London.
Nobiling assassination attempt by anarchist Karl Nobiling targeting the German Kaiser, Wilhelm I.
Over 640 die when the crowded pleasure boat Princess Alice collides with the Bywell Castle in the River Thames.
Karl Benz, working in Mannheim, Germany, files for a patent on his first reliable two-stroke gas engine. He was granted the patent in 1879.
Thomas Edison demonstrates a practical electric lamp (October)
England's cricket team, led by Lord Harris, is attacked in a riot during a match in Sydney.
Sandford Fleming first proposes the adoption of Universal Standard Time at a meeting of the Royal Canadian Institute.
War of the Pacific: The Battle of Topáter, the first battle of the war, is fought between Chile and the joint forces of Bolivia and Peru.
Anglo-Zulu War: Battle of Kambula: British forces defeat 20,000 Zulus.
Bolivia declares war on Chile, and Chile declares war on Peru, starting the War of the Pacific.
The first group of 463 Indian indentured laborers arrives in Fiji aboard the Leonidas.
War of the Pacific: Two Chilean ships blocking the harbor of Iquique (then belonging to Peru) battle two Peruvian vessels in the Battle of Iquique.
Russia and the United Kingdom sign the Treaty of Gandamak establishing an Afghan state.
Napoléon Eugène, the last dynastic Bonaparte, is killed in the Anglo-Zulu War.
Anglo-Zulu War: Cetshwayo, last king of the Zulus, is captured by the British.
War of the Pacific: The Chilean Navy defeats the Peruvian Navy in the Battle of Angamos.
Thomas Edison applies for a patent for his design for an incandescent light bulb.
the fictional character of Nora Helmer is first portrayed by Betty Hennings at a showing of A Doll's House at the Royal Danish Theatre.
Tay Bridge disaster: The central part of the Tay Rail Bridge in Dundee, Scotland, United Kingdom collapses as a train passes over it, killing 75.
Thomas Edison demonstrates incandescent lighting to the public for the first time, in Menlo Park, New Jersey.
War of the Pacific: The Battle of Arica, the assault and capture of Morro de Arica (Arica Cape), ends the Campaña del Desierto (Desert Campaign).
Australian bushranger Ned Kelly is captured at Glenrowan.
Second Anglo-Afghan War: Battle of Maiwand: Afghan forces led by Mohammad Ayub Khan defeat the British Army in battle near Maiwand, Afghanistan.
The army of Mohammad Ayub Khan is routed by the British at the Battle of Kandahar, ending the Second Anglo-Afghan War.
The Basuto Gun War breaks out after the Basuto launch a rebellion against the Cape Colony.
Outbreak of the First Boer War between the Boer South African Republic and the British Empire.
Billy the Kid escapes from the Lincoln County jail in Mesilla, New Mexico.
Carol I is crowned the King of the Romanian Kingdom.
Charles J. Guiteau shoots and fatally wounds U.S. President James A. Garfield (who will die of complications from his wounds on September 19).
American outlaw Billy the Kid is shot and killed by Sheriff Pat Garrett in the Maxwell House at Fort Sumner, New Mexico.
U.S. President Chester A. Arthur is sworn in upon the death of James A. Garfield the previous day.
First known conversation in modern Hebrew by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and friends.
Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday participate in the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona.
Robert Koch announces the discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis.
Thomas Henry Burke and Lord Frederick Cavendish are stabbed to death by Fenian assassins in Phoenix Park, Dublin.
The Triple Alliance between the German Empire, Austria-Hungary and the Kingdom of Italy is formed.
The Anglo-French Convention of 1882 marks the territorial boundaries between Guinea and Sierra Leone.
Premiere of Richard Wagner's opera Parsifal at Bayreuth.
A British force repels an Egyptian force led by Ahmed Urabi in the battle of Qassasin during the Anglo-Egyptian War.
Thomas Edison's first commercial hydroelectric power plant, the Vulcan Street Plant, begins operation.
The great fire destroys a large part of Oulu's city center in Oulu Province, Finland.
Transit of Venus, second and last of the 19th century.
Wales and England contest the first Home Nations (now Six Nations) rugby union match.
Tonkin Campaign: French forces capture the Sơn Tây citadel.
The arrival at Plymouth of Tāwhiao, King of Maoris, to claim the protection of Queen Victoria.
The cornerstone for the Statue of Liberty is laid on Bedloe's Island (now Liberty Island) in New York Harbor.
George Eastman receives a U.S. Government patent on his new paper-strip photographic film.
Sino-French War: French troops under General Oscar de Négrier defeat a numerically superior Qing force at Núi Bop in northern Vietnam.
A British force defeats a large Dervish army at the Battle of Abu Klea in the Sudan.
Troops loyal to The Mahdi conquer Khartoum, killing the Governor-General Charles George Gordon.
Sino-French War: Chinese victory in the Battle of Phu Lam Tao near Hưng Hóa, northern Vietnam.
Cree and Assiniboine warriors win the Battle of Cut Knife, their largest victory over Canadian forces during the North-West Rebellion.
Louis Pasteur successfully tests his vaccine against rabies on Joseph Meister, a boy who was bitten by a rabid dog.
Gottlieb Daimler patents the world's first motorcycle with an internal combustion engine, the Reitwagen.
Five Chinese people were lynched outside of Pierce City in the Idaho Territory of the United States.
Ethiopian forces under Ras Alula defeat Mahdist Sudanese forces in the battle of Kufit.
Canadian rebel leader of the Métis and "Father of Manitoba" Louis Riel is executed for treason.
Itō Hirobumi, a samurai, becomes the first Prime Minister of Japan.
Indian National Congress founded (28 December)
A fire devastates much of Vancouver, British Columbia.
The New-York Tribune becomes the first newspaper to use a linotype machine, eliminating typesetting by hand.
Karl Benz officially unveils the Benz Patent-Motorwagen, the first purpose-built automobile.
The United States Senate allows the Navy to lease Pearl Harbor as a naval base.
The Dawes Act is enacted, authorizing the U.S. President to divide Native American tribal land into individual allotments.
On Easter Sunday, Pope Leo XIII authorizes the establishment of the Catholic University of America.
Herman Hollerith applies for US patent #395,781 for the 'Art of Compiling Statistics', which was his punched card calculator.
The Rocky Mountains Park Act becomes law in Canada, creating the nation's first national park, Banff National Park.
The founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, joins Sindh-Madrasa-tul-Islam, Karachi.
Granny, a sea anemone, died in Edinburgh after nearly 60 years in captivity. Her death was reported in The Scotsman and The New York Times.
With the passage of the Lei Áurea ("Golden Law"), the Empire of Brazil abolishes slavery.
The White Rajahs territories become the British protectorate of Sarawak.
The stratovolcano Mount Bandai erupts, killing approximately 500 people in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.
George Eastman registers the trademark Kodak and receives a patent for his camera that uses roll film.
Jack the Ripper kills his third and fourth victims, Elizabeth Stride and Catherine Eddowes.
Louis Le Prince films the first motion picture, Roundhay Garden Scene.
Herman Hollerith is issued US patent #395,791 for the 'Art of Applying Statistics' — his punched card calculator.
Archduke Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria, heir to the Austro-Hungarian crown, is found dead with his mistress Baroness Mary Vetsera in the Mayerling.
The Ahmadiyya Muslim Community is established by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in Qadian, British India.
Menelik II, Emperor of Ethiopia, signs the Treaty of Wuchale, giving Italy control over Eritrea.
An attack upon a U.S. Army paymaster and escort results in the theft of over $28,000 and the award of two Medals of Honor.
The Great Seattle Fire destroys all of downtown Seattle.
North Dakota and South Dakota are admitted as the 39th and 40th U.S. states.
Eritrea is consolidated into a colony by the Italian government as Italian Eritrea.
The United States Census Bureau begins using Herman Hollerith's tabulating machine to count census returns.
The U.S. Congress passes the Sherman Antitrust Act.
Idaho is admitted as the 43rd U.S. state.
In Buenos Aires, Argentina the Revolución del Parque takes place, forcing President Miguel Ángel Juárez Celman's resignation.
At Auburn Prison in New York, murderer William Kemmler becomes the first person to be executed by electric chair.
Cornwallis Valley Railway begins operation between Kentville and Kingsport, Nova Scotia.
Liliʻuokalani is proclaimed the last monarch and only queen regnant of the Kingdom of Hawaii.
History of Portugal: The first attempt at a Portuguese republican revolution breaks out in the northern city of Porto.
SS Utopia collides with HMS Anson in the Bay of Gibraltar and sinks, killing 562 of the 880 passengers on board.
Pope Leo XIII defends workers' rights and property rights in the encyclical Rerum novarum, the beginning of modern Catholic social teaching.
History of cinema: The first public display of Thomas Edison's prototype kinetoscope.
In San Francisco, John Muir organizes the Sierra Club.
The Chicago "L" elevated rail system begins operation.
The Limelight Department, one of the world's first film studios, is officially established in Melbourne, Australia.
Thomas Edison receives a patent for a two-way telegraph.
U.S. Marines land in Honolulu, Hawaii from the USS Boston to prevent the queen from abrogating the Bayonet Constitution.
The Tati Concessions Land, formerly part of Matabeleland, is formally annexed to the Bechuanaland Protectorate, now Botswana.
Thomas A. Edison finishes construction of the first motion picture studio, the Black Maria in West Orange, New Jersey.
Verdi's last opera, Falstaff, premieres at La Scala, Milan.
Katharine Lee Bates writes "America the Beautiful" after admiring the view from the top of Pikes Peak near Colorado Springs, Colorado.
Swami Vivekananda speaks at the Parliament of the World's Religions, Chicago (11 September)
The Battle of Bembezi took place and was the most decisive battle won by the British in the First Matabele War of 1893.
Abdur Rahman Khan accepts the Durand Line as the border between the Emirate of Afghanistan and the British Raj.
13 November stabbing is committed by Léon Léauthier during the Ère des attentats. This is an influential event in the birth of modern terrorism.
The Cripple Creek miner's strike, led by the Western Federation of Miners, begins in Cripple Creek, Colorado, United States.
Coxey's Army, the first significant American protest march, arrives in Washington, D.C.
The Manchester Ship Canal in the United Kingdom is officially opened by Queen Victoria, who later knights its designer Sir Edward Leader Williams.
Governor Davis H. Waite orders the Colorado state militia to protect and support the miners engaged in the Cripple Creek miners' strike.
The International Olympic Committee is founded at the Sorbonne in Paris, at the initiative of Baron Pierre de Coubertin.
The Empire of Japan and Qing China declare war on each other after a week of fighting over Korea, formally inaugurating the First Sino-Japanese War.
Over 400 people die in the Great Hinckley Fire, a forest fire in Hinckley, Minnesota.
Buffalo Bill, 15 of his Native Americans, and Annie Oakley were filmed by Thomas Edison in his Black Maria Studio in West Orange, New Jersey.
Nicholas II becomes the new (and last) Tsar of Russia after his father, Alexander III, dies.
H. H. Holmes, one of the first modern serial killers, is arrested in Boston, Massachusetts.
The Dreyfus affair begins in France, when Alfred Dreyfus is wrongly convicted of treason.
Dreyfus affair: French army officer Alfred Dreyfus is stripped of his rank and sentenced to life imprisonment on Devil's Island.
Fountains Valley, Pretoria, the oldest nature reserve in Africa, is proclaimed by President Paul Kruger.
The Republic of Formosa is formed, with Tang Jingsong as its president.
Rontgen discovers X-rays (8 November)
Wilhelm Röntgen publishes a paper detailing his discovery of a new type of radiation, which later will be known as x-rays.
La bohème premieres in Turin at the Teatro Regio (Turin), conducted by the young Arturo Toscanini.
In Athens, the opening of the first modern Olympic Games is celebrated, 1,500 years after the original games are banned by Roman emperor Theodosius I.
Summer Olympics: The Olympic marathon is run ending with the victory of Greek athlete Spyridon Louis.
While on a pilgrimage of Shah Abdol-Azim Shrine in Ray, Tehran, Naser al-Din Shah of Qajar Persia, was assassinated by Mirza Reza Kermani.
Nicholas II is crowned as the last Tsar of Imperial Russia.
Guglielmo Marconi applies for a patent for his wireless telegraph.
William Jennings Bryan delivers his Cross of Gold speech advocating bimetallism at the 1896 Democratic National Convention in Chicago.
J. J. Thomson discovers the electron
Shinhan Bank, the oldest bank in South Korea, opens in Seoul.
Anglo-Afghan War: The Siege of Malakand ends when a relief column is able to reach the British garrison in the Malakand states.
Marie and Pierre Curie discover polonium and radium
Émile Zola's J'accuse…! exposes the Dreyfus affair.
Dreyfus affair: Émile Zola is brought to trial for libel for publishing J'Accuse...!
Spanish–American War: In the Battle of Guantánamo Bay, U.S. Marines begin the American invasion of Spanish-held Cuba.
Philippine Declaration of Independence: General Emilio Aguinaldo declares the Philippines' independence from Spain.
The first solo circumnavigation of the globe is completed by Joshua Slocum from Briar Island, Nova Scotia.
A Spanish squadron, led by Pascual Cervera y Topete, is defeated by an American squadron under William T. Sampson in the Battle of Santiago de Cuba.
US president William McKinley signs the Newlands Resolution, annexing Hawaii as a territory of the United States.
Carl Gustav Witt discovers 433 Eros, the first near-Earth asteroid to be found.
Hannibal Goodwin patents celluloid photographic film.
The steam ship SS Mohegan sinks near the Lizard peninsula, Cornwall, killing 106.
Negrese nationalists revolt against Spanish rule and establish the short-lived Republic of Negros.
Marie and Pierre Curie announce the isolation of radium.
RMS Oceanic, the largest ship afloat since SS Great Eastern, is launched.
The Malolos Constitution is inaugurated, establishing the First Philippine Republic. Emilio Aguinaldo is sworn in as its first president.
Phoebe, a satellite of Saturn, becomes the first to be discovered with photographs, taken in August 1898, by William Henry Pickering.
Philippine–American War: Malolos, capital of the First Philippine Republic, is captured by American forces.
The St. Andrew's Ambulance Association is granted a royal charter by Queen Victoria.
Pearl Hart, a female outlaw of the Old West, robs a stage coach 30 miles southeast of Globe, Arizona.
Philippine-American War:  the American Asiatic Squadron destroys a Filipino battery at the Battle of Olongapo.
The Boers begin their 118-day siege of British-held Ladysmith during the Second Boer War.
Max Planck introduces the quantum idea
American statesman and diplomat John Hay announces the Open Door Policy to promote trade with China.
Second Boer War: Having already besieged the fortress at Ladysmith, Boer forces attack it, but are driven back by British defenders.
To combat Czech nationalism, Emperor Franz Joseph decrees German will be language of the Austro-Hungarian Armed Forces.
Giacomo Puccini's Tosca opens in Rome.
The United States Senate accepts the Anglo-German treaty of 1899 in which the United Kingdom renounces its claims to the Samoan islands.
Second Boer War: Boers stop a British attempt to break the Siege of Ladysmith in the Battle of Spion Kop.
Second Boer War: British troops fail in their third attempt to lift the Siege of Ladysmith.
Second Boer War: Imperial forces suffer their worst single-day loss of life on Bloody Sunday, the first day of the Battle of Paardeberg.
Mayor of New York City Robert Anderson Van Wyck breaks ground for a new underground "Rapid Transit Railroad" that would link Manhattan and Brooklyn.
Archaeologists in Knossos, Crete, discover the first clay tablet with hieroglyphic writing in a script later called Linear B.
One day after its enactment by the Congress, President William McKinley signs the Foraker Act into law, giving Puerto Rico limited self-rule.
Hawaii becomes a territory of the United States, with Sanford B. Dole as governor.
The Scofield Mine disaster kills over 200 men in Scofield, Utah in what is to date the fifth-worst mining accident in United States history.
The second German Naval Law calls for the Imperial German Navy to be doubled in size, resulting in an Anglo-German naval arms race.
The Governor of Shanxi province in North China orders the execution of 45 foreign Christian missionaries and local church members, including children.
Armies of the Eight-Nation Alliance capture Tientsin during the Boxer Rebellion.
Kaiser Wilhelm II makes a speech comparing Germans to Huns; for years afterwards, "Hun" would be a disparaging name for Germans.
In Italy, King Umberto I of Italy is assassinated by the anarchist Gaetano Bresci. His son, Victor Emmanuel III, 31 years old, succeeds to the throne.
Battle of Peking: The Eight-Nation Alliance occupies Beijing, China, in a campaign to end the bloody Boxer Rebellion in China.
Max Planck discovers Planck's law of black-body radiation.
President William McKinley is re-elected, along with his vice-presidential running mate, Governor Theodore Roosevelt of New York.
Second Boer War: The Battle of Leliefontein takes place, during which the Royal Canadian Dragoons win three Victoria Crosses.
The first great Texas oil gusher is discovered at Spindletop in Beaumont, Texas.
Edward VII is proclaimed King of the United Kingdom after the death of his mother, Queen Victoria.
Anton Chekhov's Three Sisters premieres at Moscow Art Theatre in Russia.
William McKinley is inaugurated President of the United States for the second time; Theodore Roosevelt is vice president.
O. Henry is released from prison in Columbus, Ohio, after serving three years for embezzlement from a bank.
Peter O'Connor sets the first World Athletics recognised long jump world record of 24 ft 11.75 in (7.6137 m), a record that would stand for 20 years.
Kiowa land in Oklahoma is opened for white settlement, effectively dissolving the contiguous reservation.
The first claimed powered flight, by Gustave Whitehead in his Number 21.
Vice President of the United States Theodore Roosevelt utters the famous phrase, "Speak softly and carry a big stick" at the Minnesota State Fair.
Guglielmo Marconi transmits the first transatlantic radio signal from Poldhu, Cornwall, England to St. John's, Newfoundland.
Guglielmo Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal (the letter "S" [•••] in Morse Code), at Signal Hill in St John's, Newfoundland.
The first American college football bowl game, the Rose Bowl between Michigan and Stanford, is held in Pasadena, California.
Second Boer War: Australian soldiers Harry "Breaker" Morant and Peter Handcock are executed in Pretoria after being convicted of war crimes.
The 7.5 Mw Guatemala earthquake shakes Guatemala with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), killing between 800 and 2,000.
Pierre and Marie Curie refine radium chloride.
The U.S. Congress passes the Spooner Act, authorizing President Theodore Roosevelt to acquire rights from Colombia for the Panama Canal.
Peruvian explorer and farmer Agustín Lizárraga discovers Machu Picchu, the "Lost City of the Incas".
Edward VII and Alexandra of Denmark are crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.
Hallam Tennyson, 2nd Baron Tennyson, son of the poet Alfred Tennyson, becomes the second Governor-General of Australia.
El Yunque National Forest in Puerto Rico becomes part of the United States National Forest System as the Luquillo Forest Reserve.
The Kishinev pogrom in Kishinev (Bessarabia) begins, forcing tens of thousands of Jews to later seek refuge in Palestine and the Western world.
A landslide kills 70 people in Frank, in the District of Alberta, Canada.
Românul de la Pind, the longest-running newspaper by and about Aromanians until World War II, is founded.
A group of Serbian officers storms the royal palace and assassinates King Alexander I of Serbia and his wife, Queen Draga.
Benito Mussolini, at the time a radical Socialist, is arrested by Bern police for advocating a violent general strike.
Macedonian rebels in Kruševo proclaim the Kruševo Republic, which exists for only ten days before Ottoman Turks lay waste to the town.
German engineer Karl Jatho allegedly flies his self-made, motored gliding airplane four months before the first flight of the Wright brothers.
The Russian Social Democratic Labour Party splits into two groups: The Bolsheviks (Russian for "majority") and Mensheviks (Russian for "minority").
The Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty is signed by the United States and Panama, giving the United States exclusive rights over the Panama Canal Zone.
The Wright brothers make the first controlled powered, heavier-than-air flight in the Wright Flyer at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
The distress signal "CQD" is established only to be replaced two years later by "SOS".
Anton Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard receives its premiere performance at the Moscow Art Theatre.
Japanese forces launch a surprise attack against Russian-controlled Port Arthur, marking the start of the Russo-Japanese war.
Russo-Japanese War: Battle of Hsimucheng: Units of the Imperial Japanese Army defeat units of the Imperial Russian Army in a strategic confrontation.
Einstein's miracle year: special relativity, E = mc^2, photoelectric effect
Russian Revolution of 1905: Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich of Russia is assassinated in the Moscow Kremlin by Socialist Revolutionary Ivan Kalyayev.
Eleftherios Venizelos calls for Crete's union with Greece, and begins what is to be known as the Theriso revolt.
Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany declares his support for Moroccan independence in Tangier, beginning the First Moroccan Crisis.
In India, an earthquake hits the Kangra Valley, killing 20,000, and destroying most buildings in Kangra, McLeod Ganj and Dharamshala.
Norway's parliament dissolves its union with Sweden. The vote was confirmed by a national plebiscite on August 13 of that year.
The 7.2 Mw Calabria earthquake shakes southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing between 557 and 2,500 people.
Partition of Bengal (16 October); Swadeshi movement begins
Irish nationalist Arthur Griffith founds Sinn Féin as a political party with the main aim of establishing a dual monarchy in Ireland.
A workers' uprising occurs in Kyiv, Ukraine (then part of the Russian Empire), and establishes the Shuliavka Republic.
In rugby union, the "Match of the Century" is played between Wales and New Zealand at Cardiff Arms Park.
SS Valencia runs aground on rocks on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, killing more than 130.
Édouard de Laveleye forms the Belgian Olympic Committee in Brussels.
The 1906 Intercalated Games open in Athens.
The attempted regicide of Spanish King Alfonso XIII and Queen Victoria Eugenie on their wedding day instead kills 24.
Cunard Line's RMS Lusitania is launched from the John Brown Shipyard, Glasgow (Clydebank), Scotland.
Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania millionaire Harry Thaw shoots and kills prominent architect Stanford White.
Persian Constitutional Revolution: Mozaffar ad-Din Shah Qajar, King of Iran, agrees to convert the government to a constitutional monarchy.
All-India Muslim League founded (30 December)
Charles Curtis of Kansas becomes the first Native American U.S. Senator.
Belgian chemist Leo Baekeland announces the creation of Bakelite, the world's first synthetic plastic.
The Workers' Federation of Chile declares a general strike in solidarity with a rail workers' strike.
Most resistance societies in Santiago return to work, bringing an end to the 1907 Chilean general strike.
The start of the first Scout camp on Brownsea Island, the origin of the worldwide Scouting movement.
The first Boy Scout encampment concludes at Brownsea Island in southern England.
Indian Territory and Oklahoma Territory join to form Oklahoma, which is admitted as the 46th U.S. state.
A coal mine explosion at Monongah, West Virginia, kills 362 workers.
The Chilean Army commits a massacre of at least 2,000 striking saltpeter miners in Iquique, Chile.
The Alpha Kappa Alpha sorority becomes the first Greek-letter organization founded and established by African American college women.
Members of the Portuguese Republican Party fail in their attempted coup d'état against the administrative dictatorship of Prime Minister João Franco.
Lisbon Regicide: King Carlos I of Portugal and Infante Luis Filipe are shot dead in Lisbon.
SMS Blücher, the last armored cruiser to be built by the Imperial German Navy, is launched.
Hauser Dam, a steel dam on the Missouri River in Montana, fails, sending a surge of water 25 to 30 feet (7.6 to 9.1 m) high downstream.
The Chicago Cubs defeat the Detroit Tigers, 2–0, clinching the 1908 World Series; this would be their last until winning the 2016 World Series.
The 7.1 Mw Messina earthquake shakes Southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing between about 80,000.
Bakelite, the first plastic, is made
Explorer Aeneas Mackintosh of the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition escaped death by fleeing across ice floes.
Newly formed automaker General Motors (GM) buys into the Oakland Motor Car Company, which later becomes GM's long-running Pontiac division.
Richard Strauss's opera Elektra receives its debut performance at the Dresden State Opera.
United States troops leave Cuba, with the exception of Guantanamo Bay Naval Base, after being there since the Spanish–American War.
Kinemacolor, the first successful color motion picture process, is first shown to the general public at the Palace Theatre in London.
Muslims in the Ottoman Empire begin a massacre of Armenians in Adana.
Sultan of Ottoman Empire Abdul Hamid II is overthrown, and is succeeded by his brother, Mehmed V.
Alfred Deakin becomes Prime Minister of Australia for the third time.
Two United States warships are sent to Nicaragua after 500 revolutionaries (including two Americans) are executed by order of José Santos Zelaya.
SMS Zrínyi, one of the last pre-dreadnought battleships built by the Austro-Hungarian Navy, is launched.
Frenchman Louis Paulhan wins the 1910 London to Manchester air race, the first long-distance aeroplane race in the United Kingdom.
Charles Rolls, a co-founder of Rolls-Royce Limited, becomes the first man to make a non-stop double crossing of the English Channel by plane.
The first Father's Day is celebrated in Spokane, Washington.
The Ottoman Empire captures the city of Shkodër, putting down the Albanian Revolt of 1910.
British ocean liner RMS Olympic is launched.
HMS Niobe arrives in Halifax Harbour to become the first ship of the Royal Canadian Navy.
The first air freight shipment (from Dayton, Ohio, to Columbus, Ohio) is undertaken by the Wright brothers and department store owner Max Morehouse.
Johan Alfred Ander becomes the last person to be executed in Sweden.
An underground explosion at the Hulton Bank Colliery No. 3 Pit in Over Hulton, Westhoughton, England, kills 344 miners.
Delhi Durbar; capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi
Rutherford proposes the nucleus of the atom
A gun battle in the East End of London leaves two dead. It sparked a political row over the involvement of then-Home Secretary Winston Churchill.
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake destroys the city of Almaty in Russian Turkestan.
Kappa Alpha Psi, the world's third-oldest and largest black fraternity, is founded at Indiana University.
Roald Amundsen's South Pole expedition makes landfall on the eastern edge of the Ross Ice Shelf.
Mexican Revolution: Mexicali is captured by the Mexican Liberal Party, igniting the Magonista rebellion of 1911.
The destroyer USS Terry makes the first airplane rescue at sea saving the life of Douglas McCurdy 16 kilometres (10 miles) from Havana, Cuba.
The Second Canton Uprising takes place in Guangzhou, Qing China, but is suppressed.
George V and Mary of Teck are crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.
Mexican Revolution: Government forces bring an end to the Magonista rebellion of 1911 in the Second Battle of Tijuana.
Hiram Bingham III re-discovers Machu Picchu, "the Lost City of the Incas".
The Australasian Antarctic Expedition began as the SY Aurora departed London.
Ishi, considered the last Native American to make contact with European Americans, emerges from the wilderness of northeastern California.
The White Star Line's RMS Olympic collides with the British warship HMS Hawke.
An accidental bomb explosion triggers the Wuchang Uprising against the Qing dynasty, beginning the Xinhai Revolution.
The Xinhai Revolution spreads to Guangzhou, where the Qing general Fengshan is assassinated by the Chinese Assassination Corps.
After declaring war on the Ottoman Empire on September 29, 1911, Italy annexes Tripoli and Cyrenaica.
Jana Gana Mana, the national anthem of India, is first sung in the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress.
The Scout Association is incorporated throughout the British Empire by royal charter.
German geophysicist Alfred Wegener first presents his theory of continental drift.
British polar explorer Captain Robert Falcon Scott reaches the South Pole, one month after Roald Amundsen.
Marie-Adélaïde, the eldest of six daughters of Guillaume IV, becomes the first reigning Grand Duchess of Luxembourg.
Sultan Abd al-Hafid signs the Treaty of Fez, making Morocco a French protectorate.
The Cunard liner RMS Carpathia brings 705 survivors from the RMS Titanic to New York City.
The eruption of Novarupta in Alaska begins. It is the largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century.
Henrique Mitchell de Paiva Couceiro leads an unsuccessful royalist attack against the First Portuguese Republic in Chaves.
Arthur Rose Eldred is awarded the first Eagle Scout award of the Boy Scouts of America.
First Balkan War: The day after the Battle of Sarantaporo, Greek troops liberate the city of Kozani.
First Balkan War: The Greek navy completes the capture of the island of Lemnos for use as a forward base against the Dardanelles.
Bulgaria defeats the Ottoman Empire in the Battle of Lule Burgas, the bloodiest battle of the First Balkan War, which opens her way to Constantinople.
Woodrow Wilson is elected the 28th President of the United States, defeating incumbent William Howard Taft.
The Deutsche Opernhaus (now Deutsche Oper Berlin) opens in the Berlin neighborhood of Charlottenburg, with a production of Beethoven's Fidelio.
First Balkan War: King George I of Greece makes a triumphal entry into Thessaloniki after its liberation from 482 years of Ottoman rule.
Spain declares a protectorate over the north shore of Morocco.
Albania declares its independence from the Ottoman Empire.
First Balkan War: The Royal Hellenic Navy defeats the Ottoman Navy at the Battle of Elli.
The first municipally owned streetcars take to the streets in San Francisco.
First Balkan War: Greece completes its capture of the eastern Aegean island of Chios, as the last Ottoman forces on the island surrender.
The Sixteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution is ratified, authorizing the Federal government to impose and collect an income tax.
Greek military aviators Michael Moutoussis and Aristeidis Moraitinis perform the first naval air mission in history, with a Farman MF.7 hydroplane.
President Woodrow Wilson addresses American Civil War veterans at the Great Reunion of 1913.
Second Balkan War: Delegates from Bulgaria, Romania, Serbia, Montenegro, and Greece sign the Treaty of Bucharest, ending the war.
Queen Wilhelmina opens the Peace Palace in The Hague.
The United Mine Workers of America launch a strike which eventually escalated into the Colorado Coalfield War.
Ford Motor Company introduces the first moving vehicle assembly line.
A rail workers' strike in Chile escalates into a general strike, organized by the Regional Workers' Federation of Chile.
Crete, having obtained self rule from Turkey after the First Balkan War, is annexed by Greece.
The Karluk, flagship of the Canadian Arctic Expedition, sinks after being crushed by ice.
HMHS Britannic, sister to the RMS Titanic, is launched at Harland and Wolff shipyard in Belfast.
The House of Commons of the United Kingdom passes the Home Rule Bill for devolution in Ireland.
Mexican Revolution: Pancho Villa takes Zacatecas from Victoriano Huerta.
The Illinois Monument is dedicated at Cheatham Hill in what is now the Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park.
The funeral of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie takes place in Vienna, six days after their assassinations in Sarajevo.
Felix Ysagun Manalo registers the Iglesia ni Cristo (Church of Christ) as Iglesia ni Kristo with the government of the Philippines.
First World War begins (28 July)
World War I: In the culmination of the July Crisis, Austria-Hungary declares war on the Kingdom of Serbia and begins the Great War.
World War I: The German Empire declares war on the Russian Empire.
World War I: The First Russian Army, led by Paul von Rennenkampf, enters East Prussia.
World War I: The Royal Navy defeats the German fleet in the Battle of Heligoland Bight.
World War I: Start of the Battle of St. Quentin in which the French Fifth Army counter-attacked the invading Germans at Saint-Quentin, Aisne.
World War I: Start of the Battle of Grand Couronné, a German assault against French positions on high ground near the city of Nancy.
World War I: Private Thomas Highgate becomes the first British soldier to be executed for desertion during the war.
HMAS AE1, the Royal Australian Navy's first submarine, is lost at sea with all hands near East New Britain, Papua New Guinea.
Andrew Fisher becomes Prime Minister of Australia for the third time.
World War I: The First Battle of Ypres begins.
World War I: The new British battleship HMS Audacious is sunk by a minefield laid by the armed German merchant-cruiser Berlin.
World War I: The Russian Empire declares war on the Ottoman Empire and the Dardanelles is subsequently closed.
World War I: France and the British Empire declare war on the Ottoman Empire.
Mexican Revolution: The last of U.S. forces withdraw from Veracruz, occupied seven months earlier in response to the Tampico Affair.
World War I: Following a war-induced closure in July, the New York Stock Exchange re-opens for bond trading.
World War I: Admiral Franz von Hipper commands a raid on Scarborough, Hartlepool and Whitby.
Einstein publishes general relativity (November)
Gandhiji returns to India from South Africa (9 January)
Russia defeats Ottoman Turkey in the Battle of Sarikamish during the Caucasus Campaign of World War I.
World War I: Germany is the first to make large-scale use of poison gas in warfare in the Battle of Bolimów against Russia.
World War I: During the Battle of Gallipoli, three battleships are sunk during a failed British and French naval attack on the Dardanelles.
World War I: The use of poison gas in World War I escalates when chlorine gas is released as a chemical weapon in the Second Battle of Ypres.
World War I: Italy secretly signs the Treaty of London pledging to join the Allied Powers.
The May 14 Revolt takes place in Lisbon, Portugal.
HMS Princess Irene explodes and sinks off Sheerness, Kent, with the loss of 352 lives.
Colombo Town Guard officer Henry Pedris is executed in British Ceylon for allegedly inciting persecution of Muslims.
RFC Captain Lanoe Hawker becomes the first British pursuit aviator to earn the Victoria Cross.
The British capture Nasiriyah from the Ottomans during the Mesopotamian campaign.
Patrick Pearse gives his famous speech "Ireland unfree shall never be at peace" at O'Donovan Rossa's funeral in Dublin.
World War I: The German 12th Army occupies Warsaw during the Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive and the Great Retreat of 1915.
World War I: Battle of Sari Bair: The Allies mount a diversionary attack timed to coincide with a major Allied landing of reinforcements at Suvla Bay.
World War I: The Second Battle of Champagne begins.
World War I: Radoje Ljutovac becomes the first soldier in history to shoot down an enemy aircraft with ground-to-air fire.
Yuan Shikai declares the establishment of the Empire of China and proclaims himself Emperor.
Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the Muslim League
World War I: Imperial Russia begins the Erzurum Offensive, leading to the defeat of the Ottoman Empire's Third Army.
In Brushaber v. Union Pacific Railroad Co., the Supreme Court of the United States declares the federal income tax constitutional.
World War I: The British government passes the Military Service Act that introduces conscription in the United Kingdom.
The Centre Block of the Parliament buildings in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada burns down with the loss of seven lives.
World War I: In the Battle of Verdun, a German unit captures Fort Douaumont, keystone of the French defences, without a fight.
Sailing in the lifeboat James Caird, Ernest Shackleton arrives at South Georgia after a journey of 800 nautical miles from Elephant Island.
A seventeen-year-old farmworker, Jesse Washington, is lynched in Waco, Texas, USA, after being convicted of rape and murder.
World War I: Battle of Jutland: The British Grand Fleet engages the High Seas Fleet in the largest naval battle of the war, which proves indecisive.
World War I:   Battle of Delville Wood begins as an action within the Battle of the Somme, lasting until 3 September 1916.
In Seattle, Washington, William Boeing and George Conrad Westervelt incorporate Pacific Aero Products (later renamed Boeing).
World War I: Battle of Fromelles: British and Australian troops attack German trenches as part of the Battle of the Somme.
Preparedness Day Bombing: In San Francisco, a bomb explodes on Market Street during a parade, killing ten and injuring 40.
World War I: Austrian sabotage causes the sinking of the Italian battleship Leonardo da Vinci in Taranto.
Ernest Shackleton completes the rescue of all of his men stranded on Elephant Island in Antarctica.
The Kingdom of Poland is proclaimed by the Act of 5th November of the emperors of Germany and Austria-Hungary.
World War I: Prime Minister of Australia Billy Hughes is expelled from the Labor Party over his support for conscription.
World War I: The Central Powers capture Bucharest.
World War I: The Battle of Rafa is fought near the Egyptian border with Palestine.
The Congress of the United States passes the Immigration Act of 1917 over President Woodrow Wilson's veto.
World War I: Mesopotamian campaign: Baghdad falls to Anglo-Indian forces commanded by General Frederick Stanley Maude.
World War I: Canadian forces successfully complete the taking of Vimy Ridge from the Germans.
In the leadup to the Battle of Aqaba, T. E. Lawrence and his Arab forces defeat a battalion of  Ottomans at Abu al-Lissan.
World War I: The Allies reach the Yser Canal at the Battle of Passchendaele.
World War I: The Battle of Passchendaele begins near Ypres in West Flanders, Belgium.
Ten suffragists, members of the Silent Sentinels, are arrested while picketing the White House in favor of women's suffrage in the United States.
The "Miracle of the Sun" is witnessed by an estimated 70,000 people in the Cova da Iria in Portugal.
Old Style date of the October Revolution in Russia.
Tikhon is elected the Patriarch of Moscow and of the Russian Orthodox Church.
Russian Revolution (7 November)
World War I: The Third Battle of Gaza ends, with British forces capturing Gaza from the Ottoman Empire.
P. E. Svinhufvud becomes the chairman of his first senate, technically the first Prime Minister of Finland.
World War I: Russia and the Central Powers sign an armistice at Brest-Litovsk, and peace talks leading to the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk begin.
World War I: USS Jacob Jones is the first American destroyer to be sunk by enemy action when it is torpedoed by German submarine SM U-53.
Halifax Explosion: A munitions explosion near Halifax, Nova Scotia kills more than 1,900 people in the largest artificial explosion up to that time.
Finland declares independence from the Russian Empire.
World War I: British General Edmund Allenby enters Jerusalem on foot and declares martial law.
Father Edward J. Flanagan founds Boys Town as a farm village for wayward boys.
Cheka, the first Soviet secret police force, is founded.
U.S. President Woodrow Wilson announces his "Fourteen Points" as conditions for ending World War I.
Finnish Civil War: The first serious battles take place between the Red Guards and the White Guard.
The Gregorian calendar is introduced in Russia by decree of the Council of People's Commissars effective February 14 (New Style).
Finnish Civil War: A group of Red Guards hangs a red lantern atop the tower of Helsinki Workers' Hall to symbolically mark the start of the war.
Finnish Civil War: The Red Guard rebels seize control of the capital, Helsinki; members of the Senate of Finland go underground.
Ukrainian–Soviet War: The Bolshevik Red Army, on its way to besiege Kyiv, is met by a small group of military students at the Battle of Kruty.
Finnish Civil War: The Suinula massacre, which changes the nature of the war in a more hostile direction, takes place in Kangasala.
The Twin Peaks Tunnel in San Francisco, California begins service as the longest streetcar tunnel in the world at 11,920 feet (3,630 meters) long.
The Council of Lithuania unanimously adopts the Act of Independence, declaring Lithuania an independent state.
World War I: German forces capture Tallinn to virtually complete the occupation of Estonia.
Beginning of the bloody March Events in Baku and other locations of Baku Governorate.
World War I: German fighter ace Manfred von Richthofen, better known as "The Red Baron", is shot down and killed over Vaux-sur-Somme in France.
Cape Town Mayor, Sir Harry Hands, inaugurates the two-minute silence.
The Finnish Civil War ends when the Whites take over Fort Ino, a Russian coastal artillery base on the Karelian Isthmus, from Russian troops.
First airmail service in Canada from Montreal to Toronto.
World War I: The Battle of Hamel, a successful attack by the Australian Corps against German positions near the town of Le Hamel on the Western Front.
The Left SR uprising in Russia starts with the assassination of German ambassador Wilhelm von Mirbach by Cheka members.
World War I: Bapaume taken by the New Zealand Division in the Hundred Days Offensive.
The battle of Megiddo begins in which British forces attack the right flank of the Ottoman army during World War I.
World War I: British forces capture Haifa, Acre, and Es Salt from the Ottoman Empire.
World War I: The end of the Battle of Megiddo, the climax of the British Army's Sinai and Palestine campaign under General Edmund Allenby.
Ukrainian War of Independence: Insurgent forces led by Nestor Makhno defeats the Central Powers at the battle of Dibrivka.
World War I: Corporal Alvin C. York kills 28 German soldiers and captures 132, for which he was awarded the Medal of Honor.
The 7.1 Mw San Fermín earthquake shakes Puerto Rico. The quake and resulting tsunami kill up to 116 people.
World War I: A new Polish government in western Galicia is established, triggering the Polish–Ukrainian War.
First World War ends (11 November)
World War I: Germany signs an armistice agreement with the Allies in a railroad car in the forest of Compiègne.
World War I: Allied troops occupy Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire.
Transylvania unites with Romania, following the incorporation of Bessarabia (March 27) and Bukovina (November 28) and thus concluding the Great Union.
Darwin Rebellion: Up to 1,000 demonstrators march on Government House in Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia.
The German Workers' Party, which would become the Nazi Party, is founded in Munich.
Montenegrin guerrilla fighters rebel against the planned annexation of Montenegro by Serbia, but fail.
Great Molasses Flood: A wave of molasses released from an exploding storage tank sweeps through Boston, Massachusetts, killing 21 and injuring 150.
Act Zluky is signed, unifying the Ukrainian People's Republic and the West Ukrainian National Republic.
The First Regional Congress of Peasants, Workers and Insurgents is held by the Makhnovshchina at Velykomykhailivka.
The Order of the White Rose of Finland is established by Baron Gustaf Mannerheim, the regent of Finland.
Charlie Chaplin, Mary Pickford, Douglas Fairbanks, and D. W. Griffith launch United Artists.
In Milan, Italy, Benito Mussolini founds his Fascist political movement.
Mexican Revolution leader Emiliano Zapata is ambushed and shot dead by government forces in Morelos.
The Third Regional Congress of Peasants, Workers and Insurgents is held by the Makhnovshchina at Huliaipole.
Jallianwala Bagh massacre at Amritsar (13 April)
Uruguay becomes a signatory to the Buenos Aires copyright treaty.
The NC-4 aircraft arrives in Lisbon after completing the first transatlantic flight.
Anarchists simultaneously set off bombs in eight separate U.S. cities.
Sette Giugno: Nationalist riots break out in Valletta, the capital of Malta. British soldiers fire into the crowd, killing four people.
Sir Barton wins the Belmont Stakes, becoming the first horse to win the U.S. Triple Crown.
John Alcock and Arthur Whitten Brown depart from St. John's, Newfoundland on the first nonstop transatlantic flight.
The British airship R34 lands in Norfolk, England, completing the first airship return journey across the Atlantic in 182 hours of flight.
The dirigible Wingfoot Air Express crashes into the Illinois Trust and Savings Building in Chicago, killing 12 people.
The Chicago Race Riot erupts after a racial incident occurred on a South Side beach, leading to 38 fatalities and 537 injuries over a five-day period.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, who founded the Republic of Turkey, gathers a congress in Sivas to make decisions as to the future of Anatolia and Thrace.
In the Netherlands, a law granting full voting rights to women is granted royal assent by Queen Wilhelmina.
The Elaine massacre in Arkansas commences.
Cincinnati Reds pitcher Adolfo Luque becomes the first Latin American player to appear in a World Series.
The Cincinnati Reds win the World Series, resulting in the Black Sox Scandal.
The Fourth Regional Congress of Peasants, Workers and Insurgents is held by the Makhnovshchina at Oleksandrivsk.
The U.S. Congress passes the Volstead Act over President Woodrow Wilson's veto, paving the way for Prohibition to begin the following January.
The Industrial Workers of the World attack an Armistice Day parade in Centralia, Washington, ultimately resulting in the deaths of five people.
Ukrainian War of Independence: Ukrainian Bolsheviks attempt to assassinate Nestor Makhno as part of the Polonsky conspiracy.
Babe Ruth of the Boston Red Sox is sold to the New York Yankees by owner Harry Frazee, allegedly establishing the Curse of the Bambino superstition.
League of Nations Covenant automatically enters into force after the Treaty of Versailles is ratified by Germany.
The United States Senate votes against joining the League of Nations.
Polish–Soviet War: The Polish army under General Edward Rydz-Śmigły celebrates its capture of Kiev with a victory parade on Khreshchatyk.
Aftermath of World War I: The Parliament of Poland establishes Silesian Voivodeship before the Polish-German plebiscite.
Non-Cooperation Movement begins (1 August)
World War I: Ottoman sultan Mehmed VI's representatives sign the Treaty of Sèvres that divides up the Ottoman Empire between the Allies.
Polish–Soviet War: The Battle of Warsaw begins and will last till August 25. The Red Army is defeated.
The Tambov Rebellion breaks out, in response to the Bolshevik policy of Prodrazvyorstka.
The Louisiana hurricane dissipates over Kansas after forcing around 4,500 people to evacuate and causing $1.45 million in damages.
Ukrainian War of Independence: The Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic agree to a truce with the Makhnovshchina.
Ukrainian War of Independence: Mikhail Frunze orders the Red Army to immediately cease hostilities with the Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine.
The Ocoee massacre commences in Orange County, Florida on the day of the 1920 United States presidential election.
Irish War of Independence: Kilmichael Ambush: The Irish Republican Army ambush a convoy of British Auxiliaries and kill seventeen.
World premiere of the science fiction play R.U.R. by the Czech writer Karel Čapek in a theater in Hradec Králové.
Greco-Turkish War: The First Battle of İnönü, the first battle of the war, begins near Eskişehir in Anatolia.
Georgian capital Tbilisi falls to the invading Russian forces after heavy fighting and the Russians declare the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic.
Emir Abdullah establishes the first centralised government in the newly created British protectorate of Transjordan.
Mikhail Tukhachevsky orders the use of chemical weapons against the Tambov Rebellion, bringing an end to the peasant uprising.
Serbian King Alexander I proclaims the new constitution of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, known thereafter as the Vidovdan Constitution.
World War I: U.S. President Warren G. Harding signs the Knox–Porter Resolution formally ending the war between the United States and Germany.
Rif War: The Spanish Army suffers its worst military defeat in modern times to the Berbers of the Rif region of Spanish Morocco.
Researchers at the University of Toronto, led by biochemist Frederick Banting, prove that the hormone insulin regulates blood sugar.
Bolshevik–Makhnovist conflict: Mikhail Frunze declares victory over the Makhnovshchina.
Tannu Uriankhai, later Tuvan People's Republic is established as a completely independent country (which is supported by Soviet Russia).
Russian Civil War: The Red Army dissolves the Makhnovshchina after driving the Revolutionary Insurgent Army out of Ukraine.
Margaret Gorman, a 16-year-old, wins the Atlantic City Pageant's Golden Mermaid trophy; pageant officials later dubbed her the first Miss America.
President Warren G. Harding delivers the first speech by a sitting U.S. president against lynching in the Deep South.
The Tomb of the Unknowns is dedicated by U.S. President Warren G. Harding at Arlington National Cemetery.
The Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed in London by British and Irish representatives.
The uprising called the "pork mutiny" starts in the region between Kuolajärvi and Savukoski in Finland.
Chauri Chaura incident; Gandhiji suspends Non-Cooperation (5 February)
In India, Mohandas Gandhi is sentenced to six years in prison for civil disobedience, of which he serves only two.
The Soviet government creates the South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast within the Georgian SSR.
British Army Field Marshal Sir Henry Wilson is killed by the Irish Republican Army helping to spark the Irish Civil War.
The Irish Civil War begins with the shelling of the Four Courts in Dublin by Free State forces.
Johnny Weissmuller swims the 100 meters freestyle in 58.6 seconds, breaking the world swimming record and the 'minute barrier'.
The League of Nations awards mandates of Togoland to France and Tanganyika to the United Kingdom.
A typhoon hits Shantou, Republic of China, killing more than 50,000 people.
Enver Pasha dies in a skirmish between the Bolshevik Red Army and Basmachi troops, to whom he had defected earlier.
Battle of Dumlupınar: The final battle in the Greco-Turkish War (Turkish War of Independence).
A referendum in Rhodesia rejects the country's annexation to the South African Union.
Italian fascists led by Benito Mussolini march on Rome and take over the Italian government.
Abolition of the Ottoman sultanate: The last sultan of the Ottoman Empire, Mehmed VI, abdicates.
The United States Supreme Court upholds mandatory vaccinations for public school students in Zucht v. King.
The Parliament of Northern Ireland votes to remain a part of the United Kingdom and not unify with Southern Ireland.
Britain's Railways are grouped into the Big Four: LNER, GWR, SR, and LMS.
Lithuanian residents of the Memel Territory rebel against the League of Nations' decision to leave the area as a mandated region under French control.
Occupation of the Ruhr: Troops from France and Belgium occupy the Ruhr area to force Germany to make its World War I reparation payments.
During the Irish Civil War the Irish Free State Army executes 10 members of the anti-treaty Irish Republican Army
Howard Carter unseals the burial chamber of Pharaoh Tutankhamun.
The Duke of York (the future King George VI) weds Lady Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon at Westminster Abbey.
U.S. Vice President Calvin Coolidge becomes president upon the death of President Warren G. Harding.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of the Republic of Turkey, founds the Republican People's Party.
The German Rentenmark is introduced in Germany to counter hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic.
Adolf Hitler is arrested in Munich for high treason for his role in the Beer Hall Putsch.
Thousands of Irish Republicans end the 1923 Irish hunger strikes, five  die from starvation.
Ramsay MacDonald becomes the first Labour Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
The 1924 Winter Olympics opens in Chamonix, in the French Alps, inaugurating the Winter Olympic Games.
Six days after his death, Vladimir Lenin's body is carried into a specially erected mausoleum.
The first state execution in the United States by gas chamber takes place in Nevada.
A.E.K., a major Greek multi-sport club, is established in Athens by Greek refugees from Constantinople.
J. Edgar Hoover is appointed first Director of the United States' Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and remains so until his death in 1972.
British Mount Everest expedition: British mountaineers Andrew Irvine and George Mallory go missing.
The Georgian opposition stages the August Uprising against the Soviet Union.
The Uzbek SSR is founded in the Soviet Union.
Adolf Hitler is released from Landsberg Prison.
The Government of Turkey expels Patriarch Constantine VI from Istanbul.
Serum run to Nome: Dog sleds reach Nome, Alaska with diphtheria serum, inspiring the Iditarod race.
The 1925 Tri-State tornado hits the Midwestern states of Missouri, Illinois, and Indiana, killing 695 people.
Mrs Dalloway, one of Virginia Woolf's earliest and best-known novels, is published.
The first modern performance of Claudio Monteverdi's opera Il ritorno d'Ulisse in patria occurred in Paris.
Scopes Trial: John T. Scopes is indicted for teaching human evolution in Tennessee.
The original Chrysler Corporation is founded by Walter Chrysler from the remains of the Maxwell Motor Company.
Scopes Trial: In Dayton, Tennessee, high school biology teacher John T. Scopes is found guilty of teaching human evolution in class and fined $100.
A train robbery takes place in Kakori, near Lucknow, India, by the Indian independence revolutionaries, against the British government.
Rif War: Spanish forces including troops from the Foreign Legion under Colonel Francisco Franco landing at Al Hoceima, Morocco.
Secret agent Sidney Reilly, the first "super-spy" of the 20th century, is executed by the OGPU, the secret police of the Soviet Union.
Roman Catholic papal encyclical Quas primas introduces the Feast of Christ the King.
Al-Baqi cemetery, former site of the mausoleum of four Shi'a Imams, is leveled to the ground by Wahhabis.
The 28 May 1926 coup d'état: Ditadura Nacional is established in Portugal to suppress the unrest of the First Republic.
King Roger, an opera about Roger II of Sicily by Karol Szymanowski, is premiered at the Grand Theatre in Warsaw.
Mercedes-Benz is formed by Gottlieb Daimler and Karl Benz merging their two companies.
Germany is admitted to the League of Nations.
A hurricane devastates Miami, Florida, killing 372 people.
Football stadium San Siro is inaugurated in Milan, Italy
Antanas Smetona assumes power in Lithuania as the 1926 coup d'état is successful.
Simon Commission appointed; boycott follows
Teddy Wakelam gives the first live radio commentary of a football match, between Arsenal F.C. and Sheffield United at Highbury.
A revolt against the military dictatorship of Portugal breaks out at Porto.
In New York City, Samuel Roxy Rothafel opens the Roxy Theatre.
Shanghai massacre of 1927: Chiang Kai-shek orders the Chinese Communist Party members executed in Shanghai, ending the First United Front.
Mae West is sentenced to ten days in jail for obscenity for her play Sex.
Carabineros de Chile (Chilean national police force and gendarmerie) are created.
The Ford Motor Company ceases manufacture of the Ford Model T and begins to retool plants to make the Ford Model A.
The Peace Bridge opens between Fort Erie, Ontario and Buffalo, New York.
Patriarch Sergius of Moscow proclaims the declaration of loyalty of the Russian Orthodox Church to the Soviet Union.
Leon Trotsky is expelled from the Soviet Communist Party, leaving Joseph Stalin in undisputed control of the Soviet Union.
The Holland Tunnel opens to traffic as the first Hudson River vehicle tunnel linking New Jersey to New York City.
Following 19 years of Ford Model T production, the Ford Motor Company unveils the Ford Model A as its new automobile.
Kern and Hammerstein's musical play Show Boat, considered to be the first true American musical play, opens at the Ziegfeld Theatre on Broadway.
Alexander Fleming notices penicillin (September)
Leon Trotsky is exiled to Alma-Ata.
C. V. Raman discovers the Raman effect (28 February)
Second Northern Expedition: The National Revolutionary Army captures Beijing, whose name is changed to Beiping ("Northern Peace").
Sliced bread is sold for the first time (on the inventor's 48th birthday) by the Chillicothe Baking Company of Chillicothe, Missouri.
The airship Graf Zeppelin completes its first trans-Atlantic flight, landing at Lakehurst, New Jersey, United States.
Indonesia Raya, now the national anthem of Indonesia, is first played during the Second Indonesian Youth Congress.
The Law on the Adoption and Implementation of the Turkish Alphabet, replaces the Arabic alphabet with the Latin alphabet.
Lala Lajpat Rai dies after a lathi charge (17 November)
Lahore Congress demands Purna Swaraj (December)
King Alexander of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes suspends his country's constitution, starting the January 6th Dictatorship.
Members of the Việt Nam Quốc Dân Đảng assassinate the labor recruiter Bazin, prompting a crackdown by French colonial authorities.
President Calvin Coolidge signs legislation establishing the 96,000 acres (390 km2) Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming.
Huey P. Long, Governor of Louisiana, is impeached by the Louisiana House of Representatives.
The inaugural Monaco Grand Prix takes place in the Principality of Monaco. William Grover-Williams wins driving a Bugatti Type 35.
A fire at the Cleveland Clinic in Cleveland, Ohio kills 123.
In Hollywood, the first Academy Awards ceremony takes place.
Margaret Bondfield is appointed Minister of Labour. She is the first woman appointed to the Cabinet of the United Kingdom.
Wall Street Crash begins the Great Depression (24 October)
Soviet General Secretary Joseph Stalin orders the "liquidation of the kulaks as a class".
The Communist Party of Vietnam is founded at a "Unification Conference" held in Kowloon, British Hong Kong.
While studying photographs taken in January, Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto.
Elm Farm Ollie becomes the first cow to fly in a fixed-wing aircraft and also the first cow to be milked in an aircraft.
Dandi March / Salt Satyagraha (12 March to 6 April)
At the end of the Salt March, Gandhi raises a lump of mud and salt and declares, "With this, I am shaking the foundations of the British Empire."
The United Kingdom, Japan and the United States sign the London Naval Treaty regulating submarine warfare and limiting shipbuilding.
The Independence Producers host the first night game in the history of Organized Baseball in Independence, Kansas.
The 1,046 feet (319 m) Chrysler Building in New York City, the tallest man-made structure at the time, opens to the public.
The inaugural FIFA World Cup begins in Uruguay.
In Montevideo, Uruguay wins the first FIFA World Cup by beating Argentina.
Patent number US1781541 is awarded to Albert Einstein and Leó Szilárd for their invention, the Einstein refrigerator.
Gandhi-Irwin Pact; Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru hanged (23 March)
Wiley Post and Harold Gatty take off from Roosevelt Field, Long Island in an attempt to circumnavigate the world in a single-engine plane.
Judge and Nazi Party member Werner Best drafts the Boxheim Documents, which described a violent takeover of the government by the NSDAP.
A secret society in the Imperial Japanese Army launches an abortive coup d'état attempt.
James Chadwick discovers the neutron
Finland and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression treaty.
Second Sino-Japanese War: The Chinese National Revolutionary Army begins the defense of Harbin.
Alt Llobregat insurrection suppressed in Central Catalonia, Spain.
Second Sino-Japanese War: Harbin, Manchuria, falls to Japan.
The Mäntsälä rebellion begins when members of the far-right Lapua Movement start shooting at the social democrats' event in Mäntsälä, Finland.
Dominion of Newfoundland: Ten thousand rioters seize the Colonial Building leading to the end of self-government.
In an attempted coup d'état, the Prime Minister of Japan, Inukai Tsuyoshi, is assassinated.
The American Friends of Lafayette is founded at Lafayette College in Easton, Pennsylvania
In the Netherlands, construction of the Afsluitdijk is completed and the Zuiderzee bay is converted to the freshwater IJsselmeer.
A bloodless revolution instigated by the People's Party ends the absolute power of King Prajadhipok of Siam (now Thailand).
The state of São Paulo revolts against the Brazilian Federal Government, starting the Constitutionalist Revolution.
Premiere of Walt Disney's Flowers and Trees, the first cartoon short to use Technicolor and the first Academy Award winning cartoon short.
The positron (antiparticle of the electron) is discovered by Carl D. Anderson.
A speech by Laureano Gómez leads to the escalation of the Leticia Incident.
The body of actress Peg Entwistle is discovered by police, two days after her suicide by jumping off of the Hollywoodland sign.
Last day of the Battle of Boquerón between Paraguay and Bolivia during the Chaco War.
George Lansbury became the leader of the opposition British Labour Party.
German-born Swiss physicist Albert Einstein is granted an American visa.
Anarchist insurrection of January 1933 breaks out in Barcelona, Spain.
Casas Viejas incident: 22 peasants killed by the Security and Assault Corps in Casas Viejas, Spain.
Mutiny on Royal Netherlands Navy warship HNLMS De Zeven Provinciën off the coast of Sumatra, Dutch East Indies.
Launch of the USS Ranger at Newport News, Virginia. It is the first purpose-built aircraft carrier to be commissioned by the US Navy.
The Parliament of Austria is suspended because of a quibble over procedure – Chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss initiates an authoritarian rule by decree.
Franklin D. Roosevelt is inaugurated as the 32nd President of the United States.
The Reichstag passes the Enabling Act of 1933, making Adolf Hitler dictator of Germany.
U.S. Navy airship USS Akron is wrecked off the New Jersey coast due to severe weather.
The Gestapo, the official secret police force of Nazi Germany, is established by Hermann Göring.
The Deutsche Studentenschaft attack Magnus Hirschfeld's Institut für Sexualwissenschaft, later burning many of its books.
Censorship: In Germany, the Nazis stage massive public book burnings.
The Walt Disney Company cartoon Three Little Pigs premieres at Radio City Music Hall, featuring the hit song "Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?"
New Deal: The U.S. Federal Securities Act is signed into law requiring the registration of securities with the Federal Trade Commission.
The first drive-in theater opens in Camden, New Jersey.
The first Major League Baseball All-Star Game is played in Chicago's Comiskey Park. The American League defeated the National League 4–2.
In a decree called the Gleichschaltung, Adolf Hitler abolishes all German political parties except the Nazis.
Nazi Germany uses a referendum to ratify its withdrawal from the League of Nations.
The first NFL Championship Game is played at Wrigley Field in Chicago between the New York Giants and Chicago Bears. The Bears win 23–21.
The 8.0 Mw Nepal–Bihar earthquake strikes Nepal and Bihar with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing an estimated 6,000–10,700 people.
The Balkan Entente is formed between Greece, Romania, Yugoslavia, and Turkey.
The Austrian Civil War ends with the defeat of the Social Democrats and the Republikanischer Schutzbund.
The Tydings–McDuffie Act is passed by the United States Congress, allowing the Philippines to become a self-governing commonwealth.
The U.S. Auto-Lite strike begins, culminating in a five-day melee between Ohio National Guard troops and 6,000 strikers and picketers.
A self coup by prime minister Kārlis Ulmanis succeeds in Latvia, suspending its constitution and dissolving its Saeima.
Near Callander, Ontario, Canada, the Dionne quintuplets are born to Oliva and Elzire Dionne; they will be the first quintuplets to survive infancy.
The Communications Act of 1934 establishes the United States' Federal Communications Commission (FCC).
The Night of the Long Knives ends after three days of killings.
Reichskanzler Adolf Hitler becomes Führer of Germany following the death of President Paul von Hindenburg.
The German referendum of 1934 approves Adolf Hitler's appointment as head of state with the title of Führer.
An Ustashe assassin kills King Alexander I of Yugoslavia and Louis Barthou, Foreign Minister of France, in Marseille.
Lieutenant Kijé, one of Sergei Prokofiev's best-known works, premiered.
Government of India Act, 1935
Benito Mussolini and French Foreign Minister Pierre Laval sign the Franco-Italian Agreement.
Amelia Earhart becomes the first person to fly solo from Hawaii to California.
Adolf Hitler orders the Luftwaffe to be re-formed, violating the provisions of the Treaty of Versailles.
Robert Watson-Watt carries out a demonstration near Daventry which leads directly to the development of radar in the United Kingdom.
A 7.7 Mw earthquake destroys Quetta in modern-day Pakistan killing 40,000.
Dr. Robert Smith takes his last drink, and Alcoholics Anonymous is founded in Akron, Ohio, United States, by him and Bill Wilson.
Chaco War ends: A truce is called between Bolivia and Paraguay who had been fighting since 1932.
A ceasefire is negotiated between Bolivia and Paraguay, ending the Chaco War.
Switzerland: A Royal Dutch Airlines plane en route from Milan to Frankfurt crashes into a Swiss mountain, killing thirteen.
The Dust Bowl heat wave reaches its peak, sending temperatures to 109 °F (43 °C) in Chicago and 104 °F (40 °C) in Milwaukee.
The Long March, a mammoth retreat undertaken by the armed forces of the Chinese Communist Party a year prior, ends.
The China Clipper inaugurates the first commercial transpacific air service, connecting Alameda, California with Manila.
The Lebensborn Project, a Nazi reproduction program, is founded by Heinrich Himmler.
Regina Jonas is ordained as the first female rabbi in the history of Judaism.
The first inductees into the Baseball Hall of Fame are announced.
Tupelo–Gainesville tornado outbreak: An F5 tornado kills 233 in Tupelo, Mississippi.
Italy formally annexes Ethiopia after taking the capital Addis Ababa on May 5.
Inventor Edwin Armstrong demonstrates FM broadcasting to an audience of engineers at the FCC in Washington, DC.
Spanish Civil War: The Popular Executive Committee of Valencia takes power in the Valencian Community.
In Catalonia, Spain, the Unified Socialist Party of Catalonia is founded through the merger of Socialist and Communist parties.
Spanish Civil War: Germany and Italy decide to intervene in the war in support for Francisco Franco and the Nationalist faction.
King Edward VIII, in one of his few official duties before he abdicates the throne, officially unveils the Canadian National Vimy Memorial.
The Olympics open in Berlin with a ceremony presided over by Adolf Hitler.
A fire wipes out Kursha-2 in the Meshchera Lowlands, Ryazan Oblast, Russia, killing 1,200 and leaving only 20 survivors.
Jesse Owens wins the 100 metre dash, defeating Ralph Metcalfe, at the Berlin Olympics.
Prime Minister of Greece Ioannis Metaxas suspends parliament and the Constitution and establishes the 4th of August Regime.
Rainey Bethea is hanged in Owensboro, Kentucky in the last known public execution in the United States.
The Great Purge of the Soviet Union begins when the first of the Moscow Trials is convened.
Nazi Germany begins its mass arrests of Jehovah's Witnesses, who are interned in concentration camps.
