Spanish Civil War: Largo Caballero forms a war cabinet to direct the republican war effort.
Raoul Villain, who assassinated the French Socialist Jean Jaurès, is himself killed by Spanish Republicans in Ibiza.
Spanish Civil War: The republican government flees from Madrid to Valencia, leading to the formation of the Madrid Defense Council in its stead.
Spanish Civil War: The Madrid Defense Council is formed to coordinate the Defense of Madrid against nationalist forces.
Australian cricketer Jack Fingleton becomes the first player to score centuries in four consecutive Test innings.
The beginning of Xi'an incident. As a result, Chiang Kai Shek is captured.
Spanish Civil War: Nationalists and Republicans both withdraw after suffering heavy losses, ending the Second Battle of the Corunna Road.
The Guiding Light debuts on NBC radio from Chicago. In 1952 it moves to CBS television, where it remains until September 18, 2009.
Spanish Civil War: Republican forces establish the Interprovincial Council of Santander, Palencia and Burgos in Cantabria.
Wallace H. Carothers receives a United States patent for nylon.
Spanish Civil War: Spanish Republican forces defeat the Italians at the Battle of Guadalajara.
Sir Frank Whittle ground-tests the first jet engine designed to power an aircraft, at Rugby, England.
Spanish Civil War: Guernica, Spain, is bombed by the German Condor Legion and the Italian Aviazione Legionaria.
South African medical researcher Max Theiler develops the yellow fever vaccine at the Rockefeller Foundation in New York City.
King George VI and Queen Elizabeth of the United Kingdom are crowned in Westminster Abbey.
In California, the Golden Gate Bridge opens to pedestrian traffic, creating a vital link between San Francisco and Marin County, California.
Great Purge: The Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin executes eight army leaders.
Pennsylvania becomes the first (and only) state of the United States to celebrate Flag Day officially as a state holiday.
Tongzhou mutiny: In Tongzhou, China, the East Hebei Army attacks Japanese troops and civilians.
Spanish Civil War: The Regional Defence Council of Aragon is dissolved by the Second Spanish Republic.
Spanish Civil War: the Basque Army surrenders to the Italian Corpo Truppe Volontarie following the Santoña Agreement.
Second Sino-Japanese War: The Chinese Eighth Route Army gains a minor, but morale-boosting victory in the Battle of Pingxingguan.
Rafael Trujillo orders the execution of Haitians living in the border region of the Dominican Republic.
Murder of 9 Catholic priests in Zhengding, China, who protected the local population from the advancing Japanese army.
The Duke and Duchess of Windsor tour Nazi Germany for 12 days and meet Adolf Hitler on 22 October.
Nazi Germany begins expulsions of 18,000 Polish Jews.
Stalinists execute Pastor Paul Hamberg and seven members of Azerbaijan's Lutheran community.
Second Italo-Ethiopian War: Italy leaves the League of Nations.
Second Sino-Japanese War: USS Panay incident: Japanese aircraft bomb and sink U.S. gunboat USS Panay on the Yangtze river in China.
Oil is discovered in Saudi Arabia.
Superman debuts in Action Comics #1 (cover dated June 1938).
United States President Franklin D. Roosevelt dedicates the Eternal Light Peace Memorial and lights the eternal flame at Gettysburg Battlefield.
World speed record for a steam locomotive is set in England, by the Mallard, which reaches a speed of 125.88 miles per hour (202.58 km/h).
Hawaii Clipper disappears between Guam and Manila as the first loss of an airliner in trans-Pacific China Clipper service.
Bulgaria signs a non-aggression pact with Greece and other states of Balkan Antanti (Turkey, Romania, Yugoslavia).
Archaeologists discover engraved gold and silver plates from King Darius the Great in Persepolis.
Otto Hahn discovers the nuclear fission of the heavy element uranium, the scientific and technological basis of nuclear energy.
The deadliest earthquake in Chilean history strikes Chillán, killing approximately 28,000 people.
Spanish Civil War: Catalonia Offensive: Troops loyal to nationalist General Francisco Franco and aided by Italy take Barcelona.
During a speech in the Reichstag, Adolf Hitler makes a prediction about the end of the Jewish race in Europe if another world war were to occur.
As part of British air raid precautions, the first of 2.5 million Anderson shelters is constructed in a garden in Islington, north London.
In Bombay, Mohandas Gandhi begins a hunger strike in protest at the autocratic rule in British India.
Benito Mussolini declares an Italian protectorate over Albania and forces King Zog I into exile.
The Canadian National War Memorial is unveiled by King George VI and Queen Elizabeth in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.
Shooting begins on Paramount Pictures' Dr. Cyclops, the first horror film photographed in three-strip Technicolor.
Albert Einstein and Leo Szilard write a letter to Franklin D. Roosevelt, urging him to begin the Manhattan Project to develop a nuclear weapon.
The Thirteen Roses: Thirteen female members of the Unified Socialist Youth are executed by Francoist forces in Madrid, Spain.
Second World War begins (1 September)
World War II: Germany and Slovakia invade Poland, beginning the European phase of World War II.
World War II: Following the start of the invasion of Poland the previous day, the Free City of Danzig (now Gdańsk, Poland) is annexed by Nazi Germany.
World War II: The Battle of Hel begins, the longest-defended pocket of Polish Army resistance during the German invasion of Poland.
Burmese national hero U Ottama dies in prison after a hunger strike to protest Britain's colonial government.
World War II: The Soviet invasion of Poland begins.
World War II: German submarine U-29 sinks the British aircraft carrier HMS Courageous.
World War II: The Polish government of Ignacy Mościcki flees to Romania.
World War II: The Battle of Kępa Oksywska concludes, with Polish losses reaching roughly 14% of all the forces engaged.
World War II: General Władysław Sikorski becomes prime minister of the Polish government-in-exile.
World War II: Germany annexes western Poland.
World War II: The German submarine U-47 sinks the British battleship HMS Royal Oak within her harbour at Scapa Flow, Scotland.
World War II: HMS Rawalpindi is sunk by the German battleships Scharnhorst and Gneisenau.
Winter War: The Red Army's advance on the Karelian Isthmus is stopped by Finns at the Mannerheim Line during the Battle of Taipale.
Winter War: The Battle of Tolvajärvi, also known as the first major Finnish victory in the Winter War, begins.
HMS Duchess sinks after a collision with HMS Barham off the coast of Scotland with the loss of 124 men.
World War II: Battle of the River Plate: The Admiral Graf Spee is scuttled by Captain Hans Langsdorff outside Montevideo.
The 7.8 Mw Erzincan earthquake shakes eastern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme). At least 32,700 people were killed.
Winter War: Finland holds off a Soviet attack in the Battle of Kelja.
Martin Kamen and Sam Ruben discover carbon-14.
Five people are killed in an arson attack on the offices of the communist newspaper Flamman in Luleå, Sweden.
Second Sino-Japanese War: Japan declares Nanking capital of a new Chinese puppet government, nominally controlled by Wang Jingwei.
Booker T. Washington becomes the first African American to be depicted on a United States postage stamp.
World War II: Royal Marines land in Namsos, Norway, preceding a larger force which will arrive two days later.
John Steinbeck is awarded the Pulitzer Prize for his novel The Grapes of Wrath.
World War II: In the Le Paradis massacre, 99 soldiers from a Royal Norfolk Regiment unit are shot after surrendering to German troops; two survive.
World War II: Belgium surrenders to Nazi Germany to end the Battle of Belgium.
King Haakon VII, Crown Prince Olav and the Norwegian government leave Tromsø and go into exile in London. They return exactly five years later.
World War II: The completion of Operation Alphabet, the evacuation of Allied forces from Narvik at the end of the Norwegian campaign.
World War II: Thirteen thousand British and French troops surrender to General Erwin Rommel at Saint-Valery-en-Caux.
World War II: Appeal of 18 June by Charles de Gaulle.
Henry Larsen begins the first successful west-to-east navigation of Northwest Passage from Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.
World War II: Operation Collar, the first British Commando raid on occupied France, by No 11 Independent Company.
Romania cedes Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina to the Soviet Union after facing an ultimatum.
California opens its first freeway, the Arroyo Seco Parkway.
The animated short A Wild Hare is released, introducing the character of Bugs Bunny.
World War II: Italian forces begin the invasion of British Somaliland.
World War II: The Soviet Union formally annexes Latvia.
Estonia is annexed by the Soviet Union.
World War II: Due to setbacks in the Battle of Britain and approaching autumn weather, Hitler postpones Operation Sea Lion.
Two Avro Ansons collide in mid-air over New South Wales, Australia, remain locked together, then land safely.
World War II: The McCollum memo proposes bringing the United States into the war in Europe by provoking the Japanese to attack the United States.
President Lluís Companys of Catalonia is executed by the Francoist government.
The first edition of the Ernest Hemingway novel For Whom the Bell Tolls is published.
World War II: Greece rejects Italy's ultimatum. Italy invades Greece through Albania a few hours later.
World War II: The British armed merchant cruiser HMS Jervis Bay is sunk by the German pocket battleship Admiral Scheer.
World War II: In the Battle of Taranto, the Royal Navy launches the first all-aircraft ship-to-ship naval attack in history.
World War II: The German auxiliary cruiser Atlantis captures top secret British mail from the Automedon, and sends it to Japan.
World War II: The Battle of Gabon ends as Free French Forces take Libreville, Gabon, and all of French Equatorial Africa from Vichy French forces.
Walt Disney's animated musical film Fantasia is first released at New York's Broadway Theatre, on the first night of a roadshow.
World War II: In response to the leveling of Coventry by the German Luftwaffe two days before, the Royal Air Force bombs Hamburg.
The Holocaust: In occupied Poland, the Nazis close off the Warsaw Ghetto from the outside world.
New York City's "Mad Bomber" George Metesky places his first bomb at a Manhattan office building used by Consolidated Edison.
World War II: Following the initial Italian invasion, Greek troops counterattack into Italian-occupied Albania and capture Korytsa.
World War II: Romania becomes a signatory of the Tripartite Pact, officially joining the Axis powers.
World War II: The First Slovak Republic becomes a signatory to the Tripartite Pact, officially joining the Axis powers.
World War II: At the Battle of Cape Spartivento, the Royal Navy engages the Regia Marina in the Mediterranean Sea.
In Romania, the ruling Iron Guard fascist party assassinates over 60 of arrested King Carol II of Romania's aides and other political dissidents.
Captain America Comics #1, containing the first appearance of the superhero Captain America, is published.
World War II: The Cardiff Blitz severely damages the cathedral in Cardiff, Wales.
United States President Franklin D. Roosevelt delivers his Four Freedoms speech in the State of the Union address.
World War II: The Greek army captures Kleisoura.
Franco-Thai War: Vichy French forces inflict a decisive defeat over the Royal Thai Navy.
A German officer is killed in Bucharest, Romania, sparking a rebellion and pogrom by the Iron Guard, killing 125 Jews and 30 soldiers.
World War II: British and Commonwealth troops capture Tobruk from Italian forces during Operation Compass.
Charles Lindbergh testifies before the U.S. Congress and recommends that the United States negotiate a neutrality pact with Adolf Hitler.
Pope Pius XII elevates the Apostolic Vicariate of the Hawaiian Islands to the dignity of a diocese. It becomes the Roman Catholic Diocese of Honolulu.
World War II: Allied forces begin the Battle of Keren to capture Keren, Eritrea.
World War II: Bombing of Genoa: The Cathedral of San Lorenzo in Genoa, Italy, is struck by a bomb which fails to detonate.
World War II: The United Kingdom launches Operation Claymore on the Lofoten Islands, the first large-scale British Commando raid.
World War II: Nazi Germany launches Operation 25 (the invasion of Kingdom of Yugoslavia) and Operation Marita (the invasion of Greece).
World War II: The Axis powers establish the Independent State of Croatia.
At California's March Field, Bob Hope performs his first USO show.
World War II: The House of Commons in London is damaged by the Luftwaffe in an air raid.
World War II: Battle of Crete: German paratroops invade Crete.
World War II: Manolis Glezos and Apostolos Santas climb the Athenian Acropolis and tear down the German flag.
Anglo-Iraqi War: The United Kingdom completes the re-occupation of Iraq and returns 'Abd al-Ilah to power as regent for Faisal II.
World War II: The Battle of Crete ends as Crete capitulates to Germany.
World War II: German paratroopers murder Greek civilians in the villages of Kondomari and Alikianos.
World War II: The Allies commence the Syria–Lebanon Campaign against the possessions of Vichy France in the Levant.
World War II: Nazi Germany invades the Soviet Union in Operation Barbarossa.
World War II: The Continuation War between the Soviet Union and Finland, supported by Nazi Germany, began.
Romanian authorities launch one of the most violent pogroms in Jewish history in the city of Iași, resulting in the murder of at least 13,266 Jews.
World War II: German troops capture the city of Białystok during Operation Barbarossa.
Nazi crimes against the Polish nation: Nazi troops massacre Polish scientists and writers in the captured Ukrainian city of Lviv.
World War II: The German army launches its offensive to encircle several Soviet armies near Smolensk.
World War II: Montenegrins begin the Trinaestojulski ustanak (Thirteenth of July Uprising), a popular revolt against the Axis powers.
Soviet leader Joseph Stalin consolidates the Commissariats of Home Affairs and National Security to form the NKVD and names Lavrentiy Beria its chief.
World War II: The Battle of Smolensk concludes with Germany capturing about 300,000 Soviet Red Army prisoners.
World War II: Winston Churchill and Franklin D. Roosevelt sign the Atlantic Charter of war stating postwar aims.
Germany and Romania sign the Tiraspol Agreement, rendering the region of Transnistria under control of the latter.
World War II: Tallinn, the capital of Estonia, is occupied by Nazi Germany following an occupation by the Soviet Union.
The Tighina Agreement, a treaty regarding administration issues of the Transnistria Governorate, is signed between Germany and Romania.
World War II: German forces begin the Siege of Leningrad.
The Holocaust in Lithuania: Lithuanian Nazis and local police begin a mass execution of 403 Jews in Nemenčinė.
During World War II, German forces, with the aid of local Ukrainian collaborators, begin the two-day Babi Yar massacre.
World War II: Thousands of civilians in German-occupied Serbia are murdered in the Kragujevac massacre.
World War II: The Kragujevac massacre against Serbian men and boys takes place.
World War II:  Camp X opens in Canada to begin training Allied secret agents for the war.
The Holocaust: Adolf Hitler declares the imminent extermination of the Jews at a meeting in the Reich Chancellery.
World War II: First battle of the American Volunteer Group, better known as the "Flying Tigers", in Kunming, China.
World War II: A Thai-Japanese Pact of Alliance is signed.
World War II: Operation Anthropoid, the plot to assassinate high-ranking Nazi officer Reinhard Heydrich, commences.
World War II: Manila is captured by Japanese forces, enabling them to control the Philippines.
World War II: Japanese forces attack Tarakan in Borneo, Netherlands Indies (Battle of Tarakan)
World War II: United States President Franklin D. Roosevelt creates the National War Labor Board.
World War II: First use of an aircraft ejection seat by a German test pilot in a Heinkel He 280 jet fighter.
The Holocaust: Nazi Germany begins deporting Jews from the Łódź Ghetto to Chełmno extermination camp.
The Jewish resistance organization, Fareynikte Partizaner Organizatsye, based in the Vilna Ghetto is established.
World War II: The Battle of Rabaul commences Japan's invasion of Australia's Territory of New Guinea.
World War II: The Allies bombard Bangkok, leading Thailand, then under Japanese control, to declare war against the United States and United Kingdom.
World War II: Allied forces are defeated by the Japanese at the Battle of Malaya and retreat to Singapore.
World War II: Josef Terboven, Reichskommissar of German-occupied Norway, appoints Vidkun Quisling the Minister President of the National Government.
The Osvald Group is responsible for the first, active event of anti-Nazi resistance in Norway, to protest the inauguration of Vidkun Quisling.
World War II: The Imperial Japanese Army begins the systematic extermination of perceived hostile elements among the Chinese in Singapore.
World War II: During the Battle of the Java Sea, an Allied strike force is defeated by a Japanese task force in the Java Sea in the Dutch East Indies.
World War II: Operation Biting launches its overnight raid on the German coastal radar station at Bruneval to retrieve a Würzburg installation.
World War II: Ten Japanese warplanes raid Broome, Western Australia, killing more than 100 people.
Holocaust: The first Jews from the Lvov Ghetto are gassed at the Belzec death camp in what is today eastern Poland.
World War II: Adolf Hitler issues Fuhrer Directive No. 41 summarizing Case Blue, including the German Sixth Army's planned assault on Stalingrad.
World War II: The Doolittle Raid on Japan: Tokyo, Yokohama, Kobe and Nagoya are bombed.
Pierre Laval becomes Prime Minister of Vichy France.
World War II: In German-occupied Poland, the Majdan-Tatarski ghetto is established, situated between the Lublin Ghetto and a Majdanek subcamp.
World War II: On Corregidor, the last American forces in the Philippines surrender to the Japanese.
World War II: The Thai Phayap Army invades the Shan States during the Burma Campaign.
World War II: The U.S. tanker SS Virginia is torpedoed in the mouth of the Mississippi River by the German submarine U-507.
World War II: In Operation Anthropoid, Reinhard Heydrich is fatally wounded in Prague; he dies of his injuries eight days later.
World War II: Imperial Japanese Navy midget submarines begin a series of attacks on Sydney, Australia.
World War II: The Imperial Japanese Navy submarines I-21 and I-24 shell the Australian cities of Sydney and Newcastle.
World War II: Erwin Rommel is promoted to Field Marshal after the Axis capture of Tobruk.
World War II: Germany's latest fighter aircraft, a Focke-Wulf Fw 190, is captured intact when it mistakenly lands at RAF Pembrey in Wales.
World War II: Nazi Germany starts its strategic summer offensive against the Soviet Union, codenamed Case Blue.
World War II: The 250-day Siege of Sevastopol in the Crimea ends when the city falls to Axis forces.
Anne Frank and her family go into hiding in the "Secret Annexe" above her father's office in an Amsterdam warehouse.
The Holocaust: Nazi Germany begins the deportation of 100,000 Jews from the occupied Netherlands to extermination camps.
World War II: The German offensives Operation Edelweiss and Operation Braunschweig begin on the Eastern Front.
World War II: Allied forces successfully halt the final Axis advance into Egypt.
Queen Wilhelmina of the Netherlands becomes the first reigning queen to address a joint session of the United States Congress.
Quit India Movement launched (8 August)
Dmitri Shostakovich's 7th symphony premieres in a besieged Leningrad.
World War II: In response to news of its coming liquidation, Dov Lopatyn leads an uprising in the Ghetto of Lakhva (present-day Belarus).
World War II: A Japanese floatplane drops incendiary bombs on Oregon.
World War II: The Matanikau action on Guadalcanal begins: U.S. Marines attack Japanese units along the Matanikau River.
World War II: Ocean Liner RMS Queen Mary accidentally rams and sinks HMS Curacoa, killing over 300 crewmen aboard Curacoa.
World War II: Off Guadalcanal, United States Navy ships intercept and defeat a Japanese force.
The Alaska Highway first connects Alaska to the North American railway network at Dawson Creek in Canada.
World War II: Matanikau Offensive begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends three days later with an American victory.
World War II: Battle of Stalingrad: General Friedrich Paulus sends Adolf Hitler a telegram saying that the German 6th Army is surrounded.
World War II: At Toulon, the French navy scuttles its ships and submarines to keep them out of Nazi hands.
World War II: During the Manhattan Project, a team led by Enrico Fermi initiates the first artificial self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction.
The Holocaust: Schutzstaffel chief Heinrich Himmler orders that Roma candidates for extermination be deported to Auschwitz.
World War II: Japanese air forces bomb Calcutta, India.
The Republic of China agrees to the Sino-British New Equal Treaty and the Sino-American New Equal Treaty.
World War II: Japan begins Operation Ke, the successful operation to evacuate its forces from Guadalcanal during the Guadalcanal campaign.
World War II: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill begin the Casablanca Conference to discuss strategy and study the next phase of the war.
World War II: Troops of the British Eighth Army capture Tripoli in Libya from the German–Italian Panzer Army.
World War II: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill conclude a conference in Casablanca.
World War II: The first day of the Battle of Rennell Island, USS Chicago (CA-29) is torpedoed and heavily damaged by Japanese bombers.
World War II: The Battle of Stalingrad comes to an end when Soviet troops accept the surrender of the last organized German troops in the city.
The Holocaust: In Berlin, the Gestapo arrest 1,800 Jewish men with German wives, leading to the Rosenstrasse protest.
Ioannis Rallis becomes collaborationist Prime Minister of Greece during the Axis Occupation.
World War II: Operation Vengeance, Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto is killed when his aircraft is shot down by U.S. fighters over Bougainville Island.
World War II: The British submarine HMS Seraph surfaces near Huelva to cast adrift a dead man dressed as a courier and carrying false invasion plans.
World War II: A Japanese submarine sinks AHS Centaur off the coast of Queensland.
The Luttra Woman, a bog body from the Early Neolithic period (radiocarbon-dated c. 3928–3651 BC), is discovered near Luttra, Sweden.
The Holocaust: Josef Mengele becomes chief medical officer of the Zigeunerfamilienlager (Romani family camp) at Auschwitz concentration camp.
World War II: The two-day Battle of Porta between the Royal Italian Army and the Greek People's Liberation Army begins.
The Philadelphia Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers of the NFL merge for one season due to player shortages caused by World War II.
The Holocaust and World War II: Jews in the Częstochowa Ghetto in Poland stage an uprising against the Nazis.
World War II: The Allied invasion of Sicily begins, leading to the downfall of Mussolini and forcing Hitler to break off the Battle of Kursk.
World War II: Axis occupation forces violently disperse a massive protest in Athens, killing 22.
World War II: Benito Mussolini is forced out of office by the King (encouraged by the Grand Council of Fascism) and is replaced by Pietro Badoglio.
World War II: 136 Greek civilians are murdered by soldiers of the German 1st Mountain Division in the village of Mousiotitsa, Greece.
World War II: Operation Gomorrah: The Royal Air Force bombs Hamburg, Germany causing a firestorm that kills 42,000 German civilians.
World War II: The Armistice of Cassibile is proclaimed by radio. OB Süd immediately implements plans to disarm the Italian forces.
World War II: The Allies land at Salerno and Taranto, Italy.
World War II: The United States Eighth Air Force loses 60 of 291 B-17 Flying Fortresses during the Second Raid on Schweinfurt.
World War II: The Second Philippine Republic, a puppet state of Japan, is inaugurated with José P. Laurel as its president.
Subhas Chandra Bose forms the Provisional Government of Free India (21 October)
World War II: The Provisional Government of Free India is formally established in Japanese-occupied Singapore.
World War II: The 1st Ukrainian Front liberates Kyiv from German occupation.
Lebanon gains independence from France, nearly two years after it was first announced by the Free French government.
World War II: Tarawa and Makin atolls fall to American forces.
World War II: At the battle of Makin the USS Liscome Bay is torpedoed near Tarawa and sinks, killing 650 men.
World War II: German warship Scharnhorst is sunk off Norway's North Cape after a battle against major Royal Navy forces.
World War II: The Allies commence Operation Shingle, an assault on Anzio and Nettuno, Italy.
World War II: In Bologna, Italy, the Anatomical theatre of the Archiginnasio is completely destroyed in an air-raid.
World War II: American forces land on Kwajalein Atoll and other islands in the Japanese-held Marshall Islands.
The Order of Nakhimov and Order of Ushakov are instituted in USSR as the highest naval awards.
World War II: After the success of Big Week, the USAAF begins a daylight bombing campaign of Berlin.
Greek Civil War: The Political Committee of National Liberation is established in Greece by the National Liberation Front.
German troops massacre 335 Italian civilians in Rome.
World War II: Allied bombers conduct their most severe bombing run on Sofia, Bulgaria.
Rudolf Vrba and Alfréd Wetzler escape from Birkenau death camp.
World War II: Operation Persecution is initiated: Allied forces land in the Hollandia (currently known as Jayapura) area of New Guinea.
World War II: In Greenland, the Allied Sledge Patrol attack the German Bassgeiger weather station.
Georgios Papandreou becomes head of the Greek government-in-exile based in Egypt.
World War II:  Heinrich Kreipe is captured by Allied commandos in occupied Crete.
World War II: Nine German E-boats attack US and UK units during Exercise Tiger, the rehearsal for the Normandy landings, killing 946.
World War II: Battle of Normandy: At Ardenne Abbey, members of the SS Division Hitlerjugend massacre 23 Canadian prisoners of war.
World War II: In Distomo, Boeotia, Greece, 228 men, women and children are massacred by German troops.
World War II: Battle of Carentan: American paratroopers of the 101st Airborne Division secure the town of Carentan, Normandy, France.
World War II: German combat elements, reinforced by the 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division, launch a counterattack on American forces near Carentan.
World War II: After several failed attempts, the British Army abandons Operation Perch, its plan to capture the German-occupied town of Caen.
An F4 tornado tears through the Appalachian Mountains, killing over 100 people in West Virginia, particularly in the town of Shinnston.
World War II: Mogaung is the first place in Burma to be liberated from the Japanese by British Chindits, supported by the Chinese.
The Hartford circus fire, one of America's worst fire disasters, kills approximately 168 people and injures over 700 in Hartford, Connecticut.
World War II: Largest Banzai charge of the Pacific War at the Battle of Saipan.
World War II: Adolf Hitler survives an assassination attempt led by German Army Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg.
World War II: Battle of Guam: American troops land on Guam, starting a battle that will end on August 10.
The Polish Committee of National Liberation publishes its manifesto, starting the period of Communist rule in Poland.
World War II: Operation Spring near Caen is one of the bloodiest days for the First Canadian Army during the war.
World War II: The Warsaw Uprising against the Nazi German occupation breaks out in Warsaw, Poland.
ASNOM: Birth of the Socialist Republic of Macedonia, celebrated as Day of the Republic in North Macedonia.
World War II: Polish insurgents liberate a German labor camp (Gęsiówka) in Warsaw, freeing 348 Jewish prisoners.
IBM dedicates the first program-controlled calculator, the Automatic Sequence Controlled Calculator (known best as the Harvard Mark I).
The United States Forest Service and the Wartime Advertising Council release posters featuring Smokey Bear for the first time.
World War II: The Battle of Guam in the Pacific comes to an effective end.
World War II: German troops begin the pillage and razing of Anogeia in Crete that would continue until September 5.
Freckleton air disaster: A United States Army Air Forces B-24 Liberator bomber crashes into a school in Freckleton, England, killing 61 people.
World War II: Marseille and Toulon are liberated.
World War II:  Slovak National Uprising takes place as 60,000 Slovak troops turn against the Nazis.
The last execution of a Finn in Finland takes place when soldier Olavi Laiho is executed by shooting in Oulu.
World War II: Soviet troops launch the Tallinn Offensive against Germany and pro-independence Estonian units.
World War II: The British submarine HMS Tradewind torpedoes Jun'yō Maru, killing 5,600, mostly slave labourers and POWs.
World War II: Operation Market Garden results in the liberation of Eindhoven.
World War II: The Moscow Armistice between Finland and the Soviet Union is signed, which officially ended the Continuation War.
World War II: Surviving elements of the British 1st Airborne Division withdraw from Arnhem via Oosterbeek.
World War II: Captain Bobbie E. Brown earns a Medal of Honor for his actions during the Battle of Crucifix Hill, just outside Aachen.
World War II: The Soviet Riga Offensive captures the city.
World War II: Germany replaces the Hungarian government after Hungary announces an armistice with the Soviet Union.
A coup is launched against Juan Federico Ponce Vaides, beginning the ten-year Guatemalan Revolution.
World War II: The Soviet Red Army and Yugoslav Partisans liberate Belgrade.
Liquefied natural gas leaks from storage tanks in Cleveland and then explodes, leveling 30 blocks and killing 130 people.
World War II:  American general Douglas MacArthur fulfills his promise to return to the Philippines when he comes ashore during the Battle of Leyte.
World War II: The first kamikaze attack damages HMAS Australia as the Battle of Leyte Gulf begins.
World War II: German forces capture Banská Bystrica during Slovak National Uprising thus bringing it to an end.
World War II: The Royal Air Force sink the German battleship Tirpitz, moored off Tromsø, Norway.
The Jussi Awards, the Finnish film award ceremony, is held for the first time at Restaurant Adlon in Helsinki.
World War II: The Lotta Svärd Movement is disbanded under the terms of the armistice treaty in Finland after the Continuation War.
World War II: The 73rd Bombardment Wing launches the first attack on Tokyo from the Northern Mariana Islands.
World War II: RAF Fauld explosion: An explosion at a Royal Air Force ammunition dump in Staffordshire kills seventy people.
World War II: The Battle of the Bulge begins with the surprise offensive of three German armies through the Ardennes forest.
World War II: The People's Army of Vietnam is formed to resist Japanese occupation of Indochina, now Vietnam.
World War II: George S. Patton's Third Army breaks the encirclement of surrounded U.S. forces at Bastogne, Belgium.
Maurice Richard becomes the first player to score eight points in one game of NHL ice hockey.
World War II: Operation Nordwind, the last major Wehrmacht offensive on the Western Front, begins.
The Soviet Union recognizes the new pro-Soviet Provisional Government of the Republic of Poland.
World War II: Adolf Hitler moves into his underground bunker, the so-called Führerbunker.
The SS-Totenkopfverbände begin the evacuation of the Auschwitz concentration camp as the Red Army closes in.
World War II: Soviet forces liberate the Łódź Ghetto. Of more than 200,000 inhabitants in 1940, fewer than 900 had survived the Nazi occupation.
World War II: The provisional government of Béla Miklós in Hungary agrees to an armistice with the Allies.
World War II: Germany begins the evacuation of 1.8 million people from East Prussia, a task which will take nearly two months.
World War II: Audie Murphy displays valor and bravery in action for which he will later be awarded the Medal of Honor.
World War II: The Soviet 322nd Rifle Division liberates the remaining inmates of Auschwitz-Birkenau.
World War II: Supplies begin to reach the Republic of China over the newly reopened Burma Road.
US Army private Eddie Slovik is executed for desertion, the first such execution of an American soldier since the Civil War.
World War II: The United States and the Philippine Commonwealth begin a month-long battle to retake Manila from Japan.
World War II: The Yalta Conference between the "Big Three" (Churchill, Roosevelt, and Stalin) opens at the Livadia Palace in the Crimea.
World War II: British and Canadian forces commence Operation Veritable to occupy land between the Maas and Rhine rivers.
World War II: Mikhail Devyataev escapes with nine other Soviet POWs from a Nazi concentration camp in Peenemünde, Usedom.
World War II: Battle of the Atlantic: HMS Venturer sinks U-864 off the coast of Fedje, Norway, in a rare instance of submarine-to-submarine combat.
World War II: A force of Allied aircraft unsuccessfully attack a German destroyer in Førdefjorden, Norway.
World War II: American forces land on Corregidor Island in the Philippines.
World War II: US troops reclaim the Philippine island of Corregidor from the Japanese.
World War II: In poor visibility, the RAF mistakenly bombs the Bezuidenhout area of The Hague, Netherlands, killing 511 people.
World War II: The U.S. Army Air Force firebombs Tokyo, and the resulting conflagration kills more than 100,000 people, mostly civilians.
World War II: The Empire of Vietnam, a short-lived Japanese puppet state, is established.
World War II:  The Ludendorff Bridge in Remagen, Germany, collapses, ten days after its capture.
World War II: Soviet forces invade Austria and capture Vienna. Polish and Soviet forces liberate Danzig.
World War II: Sarajevo is liberated from German and Croatian forces by the Yugoslav Partisans.
World War II: German troops kill more than 1,000 political and military prisoners in Gardelegen, Germany.
World War II: Soviet and Bulgarian forces capture Vienna.
World War II: Over 1,000 bombers attack the small island of Heligoland, Germany.
Italian resistance movement: In Turin, despite the harsh repressive measures adopted by Nazi-fascists, a great pre-insurrectional strike begins.
World War II: U.S. troops capture Leipzig, Germany, only to later cede the city to the Soviet Union.
Twenty Jewish children used in medical experiments at Neuengamme are killed in the basement of the Bullenhuser Damm school.
World War II: Soviet forces south of Berlin at Zossen attack the German High Command headquarters.
World War II: Sachsenhausen concentration camp is liberated by soldiers of the Red Army and Polish First Army.
World War II: Benito Mussolini is arrested by Italian partisans in Dongo, while attempting escape disguised as a German soldier.
Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci are shot dead by Walter Audisio, a member of the Italian resistance movement.
World War II: Adolf Hitler marries his longtime partner Eva Braun in a Berlin bunker and designates Admiral Karl Dönitz as his successor.
World War II: The Surrender of Caserta is signed by the commander of German forces in Italy.
World War II: Führerbunker: Adolf Hitler and Eva Braun commit suicide after being married for less than 40 hours.
World War II:  Soviet soldiers raise the first Soviet flag over the Reichstag.  The Victory Banner will be raised the next day.
World War II: The Prague uprising begins as an attempt by the Czech resistance to free the city from German occupation.
World War II: Axis Sally delivers her last propaganda broadcast to Allied troops.
World War II: The Channel Islands are liberated from Nazi occupation.
World War II: Yevgeny Khaldei's photograph Raising a Flag over the Reichstag is published in Ogonyok magazine.
King Haakon VII of Norway returns from exactly five years in exile during World War II.
World War II:  Australian Imperial Forces land in Brunei Bay to liberate Brunei.
William Joyce ("Lord Haw-Haw") is charged with treason for his pro-German propaganda broadcasting during World War II.
The Smoke Tragedy leaves 355 workers dead in the underground copper mine of El Teniente, Chile.
The first Victory Day Parade takes place on Red Square in Moscow, Soviet Union, symbolizing the victory of the Soviet Union over Nazi Germany.
World War II: The USS Indianapolis arrives at Tinian with components and enriched uranium for the Little Boy nuclear bomb.
The Labour Party wins the United Kingdom general election of July 5 by a landslide, removing Winston Churchill from power.
A U.S. Army B-25 bomber crashes into the 79th floor of the Empire State Building killing 14 and injuring 26.
Pierre Laval, the fugitive former leader of Vichy France, surrenders to Allied soldiers in Austria.
World War II:  The Red Army invades Japanese-occupied Manchuria.
August Revolution: Viet Minh led by Ho Chi Minh take power in Hanoi, Vietnam.
The Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces, General Douglas MacArthur, lands at Atsugi Air Force Base.
Communist leader Ho Chi Minh proclaims the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after the end of the Nguyễn dynasty.
World War II and Second Sino-Japanese War: The Empire of Japan formally surrenders to China.
Atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki; Second World War ends; United Nations founded (24 October)
Fifty years of Japanese administration of Taiwan formally ends when the Republic of China assumes control.
The People's Republic of Korea is outlawed in the South, by order of the United States Army Military Government in Korea.
Kurdistan flag day, the flag of Kurdistan is raised for the first time in Mahabad in eastern Kurdistan.
U.S. President Harry S. Truman issues an executive order giving World War II refugees precedence in visa applications under U.S. immigration quotas.
The United States Army Signal Corps successfully conducts Project Diana, bouncing radio waves off the Moon and receiving the reflected signals.
Enver Hoxha, Secretary General of the Communist Party of Albania, declares the People's Republic of Albania with himself as head of state.
General Douglas MacArthur establishes the International Military Tribunal for the Far East in Tokyo to try Japanese war criminals.
The United Nations General Assembly passes its first resolution to establish the United Nations Atomic Energy Commission.
The Democratic Republic of Vietnam introduces the đồng to replace the French Indochinese piastre at par.
The People's Republic of Korea is dissolved in the North and replaced by the communist-controlled Provisional People's Committee of North Korea.
Rudolf Höss, the first commandant of Auschwitz concentration camp, is captured by British troops.
The Soviet Union annexes East Prussia as the Kaliningrad Oblast of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic.
The International Court of Justice holds its inaugural meeting in The Hague, Netherlands.
The League of Nations officially dissolves, giving most of its power to the United Nations.
The U.S. Weather Bureau records that a tornado which struck Timber Lake, South Dakota was 4 miles (6.4 km), among the widest tornadoes on record.
Physicist Louis Slotin is fatally irradiated in a criticality incident during an experiment with the demon core at Los Alamos National Laboratory.
Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, a Socialist, calls for a Direct Action Day against the Portuguese in Goa.
Howard Hughes nearly dies when his XF-11 reconnaissance aircraft prototype crashes in a Beverly Hills neighborhood.
Santa Claus Land, the world's first themed amusement park, opens in Santa Claus, Indiana, United States.
Ordinance No. 46 of the British Military Government constitutes the German Länder (states) of Hanover and Schleswig-Holstein.
The Workers' Party of North Korea, predecessor of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, is founded at a congress held in Pyongyang, North Korea.
The Council of Europe is founded following a speech by Winston Churchill at the University of Zurich.
The first Cannes Film Festival is held, having been delayed for seven years due to World War II.
An American Overseas Airlines Douglas DC-4 crashes near Ernest Harmon Air Force Base in Stephenville, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, killing 39.
France adopts the constitution of the Fourth Republic.
Cabinet Mission; Constituent Assembly meets (9 December)
United Nations Security Council Resolution 13 relating to acceptance of Siam (now Thailand) to the United Nations is adopted.
It's a Wonderful Life premieres at the Globe Theatre in New York to mixed reviews.
An 8.1 Mw earthquake and subsequent tsunami in Nankaidō, Japan, kills over 1,300 people and destroys over 38,000 homes.
KTLA, the first commercial television station west of the Mississippi River, begins operation in Hollywood.
Thomas Goldsmith Jr. files a patent for a "Cathode Ray Tube Amusement Device", the first ever electronic game.
First Indochina War: The French gain complete control of Hanoi after forcing the Viet Minh to withdraw to the mountains.
Thor Heyerdahl and five crew mates set out from Peru on the Kon-Tiki to demonstrate that Peruvian natives could have settled Polynesia.
Pan Am Flight 121 crashes in the Syrian Desert near Mayadin, Syria, killing 15 and injuring 21.
Kenneth Arnold makes the first widely reported UFO sighting near Mount Rainier, Washington.
Referendum held in Sylhet to decide its fate in the Partition of India.
Reports are broadcast that a UFO crash-landed in Roswell, New Mexico in what became known as the Roswell UFO incident.
Prime Minister of the shadow Burmese government, Bogyoke Aung San and eight others are assassinated.
Pakistan gains independence from the British Empire as the Dominion of Pakistan, due to the partition of India.
India becomes independent (15 August); Partition of the subcontinent
India gains independence from British rule after nearly 190 years of British company and crown rule and joins the Commonwealth of Nations.
Flying the Bell X-1 over Muroc Army Air Field in California, Captain Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier in level flight, reaching Mach 1.05.
Meet the Press, the longest running television program in history, makes its debut on NBC Television.
The Soviet Union completes development of the AK-47, one of the first proper assault rifles.
Jerusalem Riots of 1947: Arabs riot in Jerusalem in response to the United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine.
Kentucky Air National Guard pilot Thomas Mantell crashes while in pursuit of a supposed UFO.
The Renville Agreement between the Netherlands and Indonesia is ratified.
Mahatma Gandhi assassinated (30 January)
British South American Airways' Tudor IV Star Tiger disappears over the Bermuda Triangle.
Ceylon (later renamed Sri Lanka) becomes independent within the British Commonwealth.
The Al-Waziri coup briefly ousts the ruling Hamidaddin dynasty of Yemen; Imam Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din is killed.
Arab–Israeli War: The port city of Haifa is captured by Jewish forces.
Igor Stravinsky conducts the premiere of his American ballet, Orpheus at the New York City Center.
Arab–Israeli War: The Kfar Etzion massacre occurs, a day prior to the Israeli Declaration of Independence.
Daniel François Malan is elected as Prime Minister of South Africa. He later goes on to implement Apartheid.
Edvard Beneš resigns as President of Czechoslovakia rather than signing the Ninth-of-May Constitution, making his nation a Communist state.
Columbia Records introduces the long-playing record album in a public demonstration at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in New York City.
Cold War: Start of the Berlin Blockade: The Soviet Union makes overland travel between West Germany and West Berlin impossible.
The United States Congress passes the Displaced Persons Act to allow World War II refugees to immigrate to the United States above quota restrictions.
Cold War: The Tito–Stalin Split results in the expulsion of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia from the Cominform.
Boxer Dick Turpin beats Vince Hawkins at Villa Park in Birmingham to become the first black British boxing champion in the modern era.
Palmiro Togliatti, leader of the Italian Communist Party, is shot and wounded near the Italian Parliament.
Whittaker Chambers accuses Alger Hiss of being a communist and a spy for the Soviet Union.
Kim Il Sung is appointed as premier of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea). This is celebrated annually as its national holiday.
Deputy Prime Minister of India Vallabhbhai Patel orders the Army to move into Hyderabad to integrate it with the Indian Union.
The Indian Army captures the city of Aurangabad as part of Operation Polo.
The Nizam of Hyderabad surrenders his sovereignty over the Hyderabad State and joins the Indian Union.
Margaret Chase Smith of Maine becomes the first woman elected to the United States Senate without completing another senator's term.
A KLM Lockheed L-049 Constellation crashes on approach to Glasgow Prestwick Airport, killing 40.
A deadly smog event begins in Donora, Pennsylvania, eventually killing 20 and sickening thousands.
Ecological disaster in Donora, Pennsylvania.
Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted (10 December)
Arab–Israeli War: The United Nations passes General Assembly Resolution 194, creating a Conciliation Commission to mediate the conflict.
The Finnish Security Police is established to remove communist leadership from its predecessor, the State Police.
Indonesian National Revolution: The Dutch military captures Yogyakarta, the temporary capital of the newly formed Republic of Indonesia.
The DC-3 airliner NC16002 disappears 80 kilometres (50 mi) south of Miami.
United Nations cease-fire takes effect in Kashmir from one minute before midnight. War between India and Pakistan stops accordingly.
Luis Muñoz Marín is inaugurated as the first democratically elected Governor of Puerto Rico.
The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the central bank of the Philippines, is established.
In his State of the Union address, United States President Harry S. Truman unveils his Fair Deal program.
Chinese Civil War: The Communist forces take over Tianjin from the Nationalist government.
These Are My Children, the first television daytime soap opera, is broadcast by the NBC station in Chicago, United States.
Mildred Gillars ("Axis Sally") is convicted of treason.
Hanns Albin Rauter, a chief SS and Police Leader in the Netherlands, is convicted and executed for crimes against humanity.
Cold War: A riot breaks out in Austurvöllur square in Reykjavík, when Iceland joins NATO.
The Dominion of Newfoundland joins the Canadian Confederation and becomes the 10th Province of Canada.
Cold War: Twelve nations sign the North Atlantic Treaty creating the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
The Republic of Ireland Act comes into force, declaring Éire to be a republic and severing Ireland's "association" with the Commonwealth of Nations.
Amethyst incident: The People's Liberation Army attacks HMS Amethyst (F116) travelling to the British embassy in Nanjing during the Chinese Civil War.
Cold War: The Soviet Union lifts its blockade of Berlin.
George Orwell's dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four is published in the United States
Albert II, a rhesus monkey, rides a V-2 rocket to an altitude of 134 km (83 mi), thereby becoming the first mammal and first monkey in space.
The first television western, Hopalong Cassidy, starring William Boyd, is aired on NBC.
The Basketball Association of America and the National Basketball League finalize the merger that would create the National Basketball Association.
In Montana, 12 smokejumper firefighters and a US Forest Service fire guard are killed in the Mann Gulch Fire.
Kemi strike: Two protesters die in the scuffle between the police and the strikers' protest procession in Kemi, Finland.
Soviet atomic bomb project: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb, known as First Lightning or Joe 1, at Semipalatinsk, Kazakhstan.
Paul Robeson performs a second concert in Peekskill, New York eight days after the Peekskill riots.
The Canadian steamship SS Noronic burns in Toronto Harbour with the loss of over 118 lives.
An Air France Lockheed Constellation crashes in the Azores, killing all 48 people on board.
Constituent Assembly adopts the Constitution (26 November)
Chinese Civil War: The Government of the Republic of China moves from Nanjing to Taipei, Taiwan.
Indonesian National Revolution: The Netherlands officially recognizes Indonesian independence. End of the Dutch East Indies.
Constitution of India comes into force (26 January); India becomes a republic
Second Red Scare: US Senator Joseph McCarthy accuses the United States Department of State of being filled with Communists.
The Korean War begins with the invasion of South Korea by North Korea.
Cold War: In Philadelphia, Harry Gold pleads guilty to spying for the Soviet Union by passing secrets from atomic scientist Klaus Fuchs.
Korean War: After four days, the No Gun Ri Massacre ends when the US Army 7th Cavalry Regiment is withdrawn.
Guam is organized as an unincorporated territory of the United States as the President Harry S. Truman signs the Guam Organic Act.
Julien Lahaut, the chairman of the Communist Party of Belgium, is assassinated. The Party newspaper blames royalists and Rexists.
Nino Farina becomes the first Formula One Drivers' champion after winning the 1950 Italian Grand Prix.
Darlington Raceway is the site of the inaugural Southern 500, the first 500-mile NASCAR race.
The Republic of India formally recognised the State of Israel.
Korean War: U.S. Eighth Army and United Nations forces break out of the Pusan Perimeter in southeast Korea.
TV Tupi Difusora, the first television station to broadcast in Brazil, begins transmissions on Channel 3 in São Paulo.
Korean War: An attack by North Korean forces was repelled at the Battle of Nam River.
Korean War: The Battle of Hill 282 is the first US friendly-fire incident on British military personnel since World War II.
Korean War: The Battle of Pyongyang ends in a United Nations victory. Hours later, the Chinese Army begins crossing the border into Korea.
Puerto Rican nationalists Griselio Torresola and Oscar Collazo attempt to assassinate US President Harry S. Truman at Blair House.
General Carlos Delgado Chalbaud, President of Venezuela, is assassinated in Caracas.
Korean War: The Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River ends with a decisive Chinese victory and UN forces are completely expelled from North Korea.
First Five-Year Plan begins; first general election in 1951-52
Korean War: Chinese and North Korean forces capture Seoul for the second time.
National Airlines Flight 83 crashes during landing at Philadelphia International Airport, killing seven passengers and crew.
Nuclear testing at the Nevada Test Site begins with Operation Ranger.
United Nations Security Council Resolution 90 relating to the Korean War is adopted.
Korean War: More than 700 suspected communist sympathizers are massacred by South Korean forces.
The first Pan American Games are officially opened in Buenos Aires by Argentine President Juan Perón.
Remington Rand delivers the first UNIVAC I computer to the United States Census Bureau.
Cold War: Ethel and Julius Rosenberg are sentenced to death for spying for the Soviet Union.
Cold War: A court in Czechoslovakia sentences American journalist William N. Oatis to ten years in prison on charges of espionage.
Vuoristorata, one of the oldest still-operating wooden roller coasters in Europe, is opened at the Linnanmäki amusement park in Helsinki, Finland.
Ferrari take their first Formula One grand prix victory at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone.
King Abdullah I of Jordan is assassinated by a Palestinian while attending Friday prayers in Jerusalem.
Canadian Pacific Air Lines Flight 3505 disappears while flying from Vancouver to Tokyo. The aircraft and its 37 occupants are never found.
Walt Disney's 13th animated film, Alice in Wonderland, premieres in London, England, United Kingdom.
George VI, king of the United Kingdom, has his left lung removed in an operation after a malignant tumour was found.
Mexican chemist Luis E. Miramontes completes the synthesis of norethisterone, the basis of an early oral contraceptive.
The "Johnny Bright incident" occurs during a football game between the Drake Bulldogs and Oklahoma A&M Aggies.
A Miami Airlines Curtiss C-46 Commando crashes in Elizabeth, New Jersey, killing all 58 aboard including dancer Doris Ruby.
The American Civil Rights Congress delivers "We Charge Genocide" to the United Nations.
The EBR-1 in Arco, Idaho becomes the first nuclear power plant to generate electricity. The electricity powered four light bulbs.
Cold War: The Marshall Plan expires after distributing more than US$13.3 billion in foreign aid to rebuild Western Europe.
NBC's long-running morning news program Today debuts, with host Dave Garroway.
Black Saturday in Egypt: rioters burn Cairo's central business district, targeting British and upper-class Egyptian businesses.
Vincent Massey is sworn in as the first Canadian-born Governor General of Canada.
Fulgencio Batista leads a successful coup in Cuba.
Pan Am Flight 526A ditches near San Juan-Isla Grande Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico, after experiencing an engine failure, killing 52 people.
Dwight D. Eisenhower resigns as Supreme Allied Commander of NATO in order to campaign in the 1952 United States presidential election.
The Treaty of San Francisco comes into effect, restoring Japanese sovereignty and ending its state of war with most of the Allies of World War II.
Pan Am Flight 202 crashes into the Amazon basin near Carolina, Maranhão, Brazil, killing 50 people.
A De Havilland Comet makes the first jetliner flight with fare-paying passengers, from London to Johannesburg.
The Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Parliament of India, holds its first sitting.
Catalina affair: A Swedish Douglas DC-3 is shot down by a Soviet MiG-15 fighter.
The SS United States sets sail on her maiden voyage to Southampton. During the voyage, the ship takes the Blue Riband away from the RMS Queen Mary.
The Constitution of Puerto Rico is approved by the United States Congress.
The 7.3 Mw Kern County earthquake strikes Southern California with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing 12 and injuring hundreds.
American experimental composer John Cage's 4’33” premieres at Maverick Concert Hall, played by American pianist David Tudor.
The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation makes its first televised broadcast on the second escape of the Boyd Gang.
The Governor of Kenya Evelyn Baring declares a state of emergency and begins arresting hundreds of suspected leaders of the Mau Mau Uprising.
A Douglas C-124 Globemaster II crashes into Mount Gannet, Alaska, killing all 52 aboard.
The New York Daily News reports the news of Christine Jorgensen, the first notable case of sex reassignment surgery.
A United States Air Force C-124 crashes and burns in Moses Lake, Washington, killing 87 of the 115 people on board.
Andhra State formed; demand for linguistic states grows
Frances P. Bolton and her son, Oliver from Ohio, become the first mother and son to serve simultaneously in the U.S. Congress.
The play Waiting for Godot by Samuel Beckett receives its première in Paris.
Josip Broz Tito is elected the first President of Yugoslavia.
Almost 72 percent of all television sets in the United States are tuned into I Love Lucy to watch Lucy give birth.
Watson and Crick describe the DNA double helix (28 February)
A De Havilland Comet (Canadian Pacific Air Lines) crashes in Karachi, Pakistan, killing 11 people.
CIA director Allen Dulles launches the mind-control program Project MKUltra.
The first U.S. experimental 3D television broadcast shows an episode of Space Patrol on Los Angeles ABC affiliate KECA-TV.
Approximately 7,100 brewery workers in Milwaukee perform a walkout, marking the start of the 1953 Milwaukee brewery strike.
Nuclear weapons testing: At the Nevada Test Site, the United States conducts its first and only nuclear artillery test.
The first public television station in the United States officially begins broadcasting as KUHT from the campus of the University of Houston.
A United States Air Force C-124 crashes and burns near Tachikawa, Japan, killing 129.
The Egyptian revolution of 1952 ends with the overthrow of the Muhammad Ali dynasty and the declaration of the Republic of Egypt.
Cold War: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are executed at Sing Sing, in New York.
Ernesto "Che" Guevara sets out on a trip through Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Panama, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, and El Salvador.
First Indochina War: The French Union withdraws its forces from Operation Camargue against the Viet Minh in central Vietnam.
Cold War: The CIA and MI6 help to overthrow the government of Mohammad Mosaddegh in Iran and reinstate the Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
Ray Bradbury's Fahrenheit 451 is published.
The remaining human inhabitants of the Blasket Islands, County Kerry, Ireland, are evacuated to the mainland.
India establishes its highest civilian awards, the Bharat Ratna and the Padma Vibhushan.
Georgetown–IBM experiment: The first public demonstration of a machine translation system is held in New York at the head office of IBM.
BOAC Flight 781, a de Havilland DH.106 Comet 1, explodes and falls into the Tyrrhenian Sea, killing 35 people.
The Hudson Motor Car Company merges with Nash-Kelvinator Corporation forming the American Motors Corporation.
The first nuclear-powered submarine, the USS Nautilus, is launched in Groton, Connecticut by Mamie Eisenhower, the First Lady of the United States.
Gamal Abdel Nasser seizes power in Egypt.
Red Scare: Witnesses begin testifying and live television coverage of the Army–McCarthy hearings begins.
The first clinical trials of Jonas Salk's polio vaccine begin in Fairfax County, Virginia.
Roger Bannister becomes the first person to run the mile in under four minutes.
First Indochina War: Battle of Mang Yang Pass: Viet Minh troops belonging to the 803rd Regiment ambush G.M. 100 of France in An Khê.
The Obninsk Nuclear Power Plant, the Soviet Union's first nuclear power station, opens in Obninsk, near Moscow.
First Indochina War: The Geneva Conference partitions Vietnam into North Vietnam and South Vietnam.
Radio Pakistan broadcasts the "Qaumī Tarāna", the national anthem of Pakistan for the first time.
The Cruise of the Kings, a royal cruise organised by the Queen Consort of Greece, Frederica of Hanover, departs from Marseille, France.
The People's Liberation Army begins shelling the Republic of China-controlled islands of Quemoy, starting the First Taiwan Strait Crisis.
In a top secret nuclear test, a Soviet Tu-4 bomber drops a 40 kiloton atomic weapon just north of Totskoye village.
Finnish president J. K. Paasikivi becomes the first Western head of state to be awarded the highest honor of the Soviet Union, the Order of Lenin.
The Moomin comics, created by Tove Jansson and Lars Jansson, is published internationally in the London newspaper The Evening News.
AEC Routemaster, the iconic London bus was introduced.
The Cochabamba–Santa Cruz highway connecting western and eastern Bolivia is inaugurated.
Benjamin O. Davis, Jr. becomes the first African-American general in the United States Air Force.
Great Britain defeats France to capture the first ever Rugby League World Cup in Paris in front of around 30,000 spectators.
Cold War: The United States Senate votes 65 to 22 to censure Joseph McCarthy for "conduct that tends to bring the Senate into dishonor and disrepute".
Contralto Marian Anderson becomes the first person of color to perform at the Metropolitan Opera in Giuseppe Verdi's Un ballo in maschera.
A Martin 2-0-2 and Douglas DC-3 collide over Boone County, Kentucky, killing 15 people.
The Air India Kashmir Princess is bombed and crashes in a failed assassination attempt on Zhou Enlai by the Kuomintang.
Twenty-nine nations meet at Bandung, Indonesia, for the first Asian-African Conference.
Cold War: West Germany joins NATO.
Cold War: Eight Communist bloc countries, including the Soviet Union, sign a mutual defense treaty called the Warsaw Pact.
The USSR and Yugoslavia sign the Belgrade declaration and thus normalize relations between the two countries, discontinued since 1948.
Black teenager Emmett Till is lynched in Mississippi for whistling at a white woman, galvanizing the nascent civil rights movement.
An all-white jury in Mississippi finds Roy Bryant and J. W. Milam not guilty in the torture-murder of 14-year-old African American boy Emmett Till.
Ngô Đình Diệm proclaims himself as President of the newly created Republic of Vietnam.
After being destroyed in World War II, the rebuilt Vienna State Opera reopens with a performance of Beethoven's Fidelio.
The Soviet Union launches RDS-37, a 1.6 megaton two stage hydrogen bomb designed by Andrei Sakharov. The bomb was dropped over Semipalatinsk.
Cardiff is proclaimed the capital city of Wales, United Kingdom.
Operation Auca: Five U.S. missionaries are killed by the Waorani of Ecuador shortly after making first contact.
In the United States, Civil Rights Movement leader Martin Luther King Jr.'s home is bombed in retaliation for the Montgomery bus boycott.
In his speech On the Cult of Personality and Its Consequences, Nikita Khrushchev, leader of the Soviet Union, denounces Stalin.
Pakistan becomes the first Islamic republic in the world. This date is now celebrated as Republic Day in Pakistan.
Cuban Revolution: Fidel Castro declares himself at war with Cuban President Fulgencio Batista.
Francoist Spain agrees to surrender its protectorate in Morocco.
SS Ideal X, the world's first successful container ship, leaves Port Newark, New Jersey, for Houston, Texas.
In Operation Redwing, the first United States airborne hydrogen bomb is dropped over Bikini Atoll in the Pacific Ocean.
The Dartmouth workshop is the first conference on artificial intelligence.
A joint resolution of the U.S. Congress is signed by President Dwight D. Eisenhower, authorizing In God We Trust as the U.S. national motto.
The dike around the Dutch polder East Flevoland is closed.
The New York Yankees's Don Larsen pitches the only perfect game in a World Series.
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, leader of India's Untouchable caste, converts to Buddhism along with 385,000 of his followers (see Neo-Buddhism).
States Reorganisation Act: states formed on linguistic lines (1 November); Mysore State enlarged
Morocco, Sudan and Tunisia join the United Nations.
United Nations Security Council Resolution 121 relating to acceptance of Japan to the United Nations is adopted.
Chin Peng, David Marshall and Tunku Abdul Rahman meet in Baling, Malaya to try to resolve the Malayan Emergency situation.
British Prime Minister Sir Anthony Eden resigns from office following his failure to retake the Suez Canal from Egyptian sovereignty.
Kripalu Maharaj is named fifth Jagadguru (world teacher) after giving seven days of speeches before 500 Hindu scholars.
American inventor Walter Frederick Morrison sells the rights to his flying disc to the Wham-O toy company, which later renames it the "Frisbee".
Northeast Airlines Flight 823 crashes on Rikers Island in New York City, killing 20 people and injuring 78 others.
A plane crash in Cebu, Philippines kills Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay and 24 others.
Elections to the Territorial Assembly of the French colony Upper Volta are held. After the elections PDU and MDV form a government.
A Vickers VC.1 Viking crashes while attempting to return to Blackbushe Airport in Yateley, killing 34.
At Malden Island in the Pacific Ocean, Britain tests its first hydrogen bomb in Operation Grapple.
In Roth v. United States, the U.S. Supreme Court rules that obscenity is not protected by the First Amendment.
Hurricane Audrey makes landfall near the Texas–Louisiana border, killing over 400 people, mainly in and around Cameron, Louisiana.
John Lennon and Paul McCartney meet for the first time, as teenagers at Woolton Fete, three years before forming the Beatles.
Rawya Ateya takes her seat in the National Assembly of Egypt, thereby becoming the first female parliamentarian in the Arab world.
The largely autobiographical novel The Ordeal of Gilbert Pinfold by Evelyn Waugh is published.
Heavy rain and a mudslide in Isahaya, western Kyushu, Japan, kills 992.
President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam becomes the first foreign head of state to make a state visit to Australia.
President Eisenhower sends the 101st Airborne Division to Little Rock, Arkansas, to enforce desegregation.
Sputnik 1 launched (4 October)
Project Vanguard: A launchpad explosion of Vanguard TV3 thwarts the first United States attempt to launch a satellite into Earth orbit.
After a general uprising and rioting in the streets, President Marcos Pérez Jiménez leaves Venezuela.
Cold War: Space Race: The Explorer 1, the first successful American satellite, detects the Van Allen radiation belt.
A hydrogen bomb known as the Tybee Bomb is lost by the US Air Force off the coast of Savannah, Georgia, never to be recovered.
The CND peace symbol is displayed in public for the first time in London.
Capital Airlines Flight 67 crashes in Tittabawassee Township, Michigan, near Freeland Tri-City Airport, killing 47.
United Air Lines Flight 736 collides with a United States Air Force fighter jet near Arden, Nevada in what is now Enterprise, Nevada.
During a visit to Caracas, Venezuela, the US Vice President Richard Nixon's car is attacked by anti-American demonstrators.
Capital Airlines Flight 300 collides in mid-air with a United States Air Force Lockheed T-33 over Brunswick, Maryland, killing 12.
United Press International is formed through a merger of the United Press and the International News Service.
Cuban Revolution: Fidel Castro's 26th of July Movement, heavily reinforced by Frank Pais Militia, overwhelm an army post in El Uvero.
Aeronaves de México Flight 111 crashes on approach to Guadalajara International Airport, killing 45.
Benjamin Britten's one-act opera Noye's Fludde premieres at the Aldeburgh Festival.
US President Dwight D. Eisenhower signs the Alaska Statehood Act into law.
In the 14 July Revolution in Iraq, the monarchy is overthrown by popular forces led by Abd al-Karim Qasim, who becomes the nation's new leader.
Vladimir Nabokov's controversial novel Lolita is published in the United States.
Chinese Civil War: The Second Taiwan Strait Crisis begins with the People's Liberation Army's bombardment of Quemoy.
Pan American Airways makes the first commercial flight of the Boeing 707 from New York City to Paris.
John XXIII is elected Pope.
A team of rock climbers led by Warren Harding completes the first ascent of The Nose on El Capitan in Yosemite Valley.
Chad, the Republic of the Congo, and Gabon become autonomous republics within the French Community.
Cuban Revolution: Fulgencio Batista, dictator of Cuba, is overthrown by Fidel Castro's forces.
Luna 1, the first spacecraft to reach the vicinity of the Moon and to orbit the Sun, is launched by the Soviet Union.
Luna 1 becomes the first spacecraft to reach the vicinity of the Moon.
Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 205 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean near Astor Piazzolla International Airport in Mar del Plata, Argentina, killing 51.
The 41-acre (17 ha) Chain Island is listed for sale by the California State Lands Commission, with a minimum bid of $5,226.
The first Melodifestivalen is held at Cirkus in Stockholm, Sweden.
Nine experienced ski hikers in the northern Ural Mountains in the Soviet Union die under mysterious circumstances.
Sixty-five people are killed when American Airlines Flight 320 crashes into the East River on approach to LaGuardia Airport in New York City.
The R-7 Semyorka, the first intercontinental ballistic missile, becomes operational at Plesetsk, USSR.
Fidel Castro becomes Premier of Cuba after dictator Fulgencio Batista was overthrown on January 1.
A Turkish Airlines Vickers Viscount crashes near Gatwick Airport, killing 14; Turkish prime minister Adnan Menderes survives the crash.
Project Vanguard: Vanguard 2: The first weather satellite is launched to measure cloud-cover distribution.
Tibetan uprising: Fearing an abduction attempt by China, thousands of Tibetans surround the Dalai Lama's palace to prevent his removal.
Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, flees Tibet for India.
USS Barbero and the United States Postal Service attempt the delivery of mail via Missile Mail.
Venus occults the star Regulus. This rare event is used to determine the diameter of Venus and the structure of the Venusian atmosphere.
NS Savannah, the first nuclear-powered cargo-passenger ship, is launched as a showcase for Dwight D. Eisenhower's "Atoms for Peace" initiative.
Portugal's state police force PIDE fires upon striking workers in Bissau, Portuguese Guinea, killing over 50 people.
Explorer program: Explorer 6 launches from the Atlantic Missile Range in Cape Canaveral, Florida.
American Airlines Flight 514, a Boeing 707, crashes near the Calverton Executive Airpark in Calverton, New York, killing all five people on board.
TAI Flight 307 crashes during takeoff from Bordeaux–Mérignac Airport in Bordeaux, Nouvelle-Aquitaine, France, killing 55 people.
S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike, Prime Minister of Ceylon, is mortally shot by a Buddhist monk, Talduwe Somarama, and dies the next day.
A Lockheed L-188 Electra crashes in Buffalo, Texas, killing 34 people.
French President Charles de Gaulle declares in a speech in Strasbourg his vision for "Europe, from the Atlantic to the Urals".
The Reserve Bank of Australia, the country's central bank and banknote issuing authority authorized by the 1959 Reserve Bank Act, is established.
Little Joe 1B, a Mercury spacecraft, lifts off from Wallops Island, Virginia, with Miss Sam, a female rhesus monkey, on board.
Avianca Flight 671 crashes at Montego Bay, Jamaica airport, killing 37 people.
The National Football League announces expansion teams for Dallas to start in the 1960 NFL season and Minneapolis-St. Paul for the 1961 NFL season.
British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan speaks of "a wind of change", signalling that his Government is likely to support decolonisation.
A Kyiv-bound Aeroflot airliner crashes on approach to Snilow Airport in Lviv, killing 32 of the 33 people on board.
A New York-bound Alitalia airliner crashes into a cemetery in Shannon, Ireland, shortly after takeoff, killing 34 of the 52 persons on board.
Northwest Airlines Flight 710 explodes and crashes near Cannelton, Indiana, killing 63.
France agrees to grant independence to the Mali Federation, a union of Senegal and French Sudan.
Students in South Korea hold a nationwide pro-democracy protest against president Syngman Rhee, eventually forcing him to resign.
Forced out by the April Revolution, President of South Korea Syngman Rhee resigns after 12 years of dictatorial rule.
More than 20 million viewers watch the first televised royal wedding when Princess Margaret marries Antony Armstrong-Jones at Westminster Abbey.
Theodore Maiman operates the first optical laser (a ruby laser), at Hughes Research Laboratories in Malibu, California.
Following the 1960 Valdivia earthquake, the largest ever recorded earthquake, Cordón Caulle begins to erupt.
In Turkey, a military coup removes President Celâl Bayar and the rest of the democratic government from office.
Trans Australia Airlines Flight 538 crashes near Mackay Airport in Mackay, Queensland, Australia, killing 29.
Charlotte Motor Speedway holds its first NASCAR race, the inaugural World 600.
The United States Food and Drug Administration declares Enovid to be the first officially approved combined oral contraceptive pill in the world.
Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt is injured in an assassination attempt.
Francis Gary Powers is charged with espionage resulting from his flight over the Soviet Union.
Jane Goodall arrives at the Gombe Stream Reserve in present-day Tanzania to begin her study of chimpanzees in the wild.
Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 1-11 ditches off Polillo Island in the Philippines, killing one person and injuring 44.
Sirimavo Bandaranaike is sworn in as prime minister of Ceylon, becoming the world's first democratically elected female head of government.
Islamabad is declared the federal capital of the Government of Pakistan.
Cuban Revolution: Cuba nationalizes American and foreign-owned property in the nation.
South Kasai secedes from the Congo.
Sputnik program: Korabl-Sputnik 2: The Soviet Union launches the satellite with the dogs Belka and Strelka, 40 mice, two rats and a variety of plants.
The Flintstones, the first prime-time animated sitcom, premieres on ABC television.
Penguin Books is found not guilty of obscenity in the trial R v Penguin Books Ltd, the Lady Chatterley's Lover case.
A military coup against President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam is crushed.
Patrice Lumumba is arrested by Mobutu Sese Seko's men on the banks of the Sankuru River, for inciting the army to rebellion.
French forces crack down in a violent clash with protesters in French Algeria during a visit by French president Charles de Gaulle.
Cold War: After a series of economic retaliations against one another, the United States severs diplomatic relations with Cuba.
Throgs Neck Bridge over the East River, linking New York City's boroughs of The Bronx and Queens, opens to road traffic.
Goldsboro B-52 crash: A bomber carrying two H-bombs breaks up in mid-air over North Carolina. The uranium core of one weapon remains lost.
Project Mercury: Mercury-Redstone 2: The chimpanzee Ham travels into outer space.
The Angolan War of Independence and the greater Portuguese Colonial War begin.
Yuri Gagarin is the first human in space (12 April)
Cold War: Failure of the Bay of Pigs Invasion of US-backed Cuban exiles against Cuba.
K-19, the first Soviet nuclear submarine equipped with nuclear missiles, is commissioned.
Project Mercury: Alan Shepard becomes the first American to travel into outer space, on a sub-orbital flight.
Park Chung Hee leads a coup d'état to overthrow the Second Republic of South Korea.
American civil rights movement: Freedom Riders are arrested in Jackson, Mississippi, for "disturbing the peace" after disembarking from their bus.
In Moscow City Court, the Rokotov–Faibishenko show trial begins, despite the Khrushchev Thaw to reverse Stalinist elements in Soviet society.
Marriage of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent to Katharine Worsley at York Minster.
Alaska Airlines Flight 779 crashes near Shemya Air Force Base in Shemya, Alaska, killing six.
Cold War: In a speech John F. Kennedy emphasizes that any attack on Berlin is an attack on NATO.
Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 706 crashes during takeoff from O'Hare International Airport in Chicago, Illinois, killing all 37 people on board.
A Douglas Dakota IV operated by Derby Aviation (later renamed to British Midland International) crashes in Canigou, France, killing 34 people.
The Soviet Navy performs the first armed test of a submarine-launched ballistic missile, launching an R-13 from a Golf-class submarine.
Vietnam War:  United States President John F. Kennedy sends 18,000 military advisors to South Vietnam.
In a nationally broadcast speech, Cuban leader Fidel Castro declares that he is a Marxist–Leninist and that Cuba will adopt Communism.
Goa, Daman and Diu liberated from Portugal (19 December)
India-China war
Pope John XXIII excommunicates Fidel Castro.
Apollo program: NASA announces plans to build the C-5 rocket launch vehicle, then known as the "Advanced Saturn", to carry human beings to the Moon.
Cold War: While tied to its pier in Polyarny, the Soviet submarine B-37 is destroyed when fire breaks out in its torpedo compartment.
Vietnam War: Operation Chopper, the first American combat mission and first American helicopter assault in the war, takes place.
Ranger 3 is launched to study the Moon. The space probe later misses the Moon by 22,000 miles (35,400 km).
French President Charles de Gaulle calls for Algeria to be granted independence.
The Great Sheffield Gale impacts the United Kingdom, killing nine people; the city of Sheffield is devastated, with 150,000 homes damaged.
A Caledonian Airways Douglas DC-7 crashes shortly after takeoff from Cameroon, killing 111 – the worst crash of a DC-7.
A Clockwork Orange, a British dystopian novel by Anthony Burgess, is published.
Arturo Frondizi, the president of Argentina, is overthrown in a military coup by Argentina's armed forces, ending an 11+1⁄2 day constitutional crisis.
The Seattle World's Fair (Century 21 Exposition) opens. It is the first World's Fair in the United States since World War II.
NASA's Ranger 4 spacecraft crashes into the Moon.
Project Mercury: American astronaut Scott Carpenter orbits the Earth three times in the Aurora 7 space capsule.
Adolf Eichmann, former SS officer in Nazi Germany, is hanged in Israel for having committed crimes against humanity, war crimes, and other offenses.
Air France Flight 117 crashes on approach to Pointe-à-Pitre International Airport in Guadeloupe, killing 112 people.
The Late Late Show, the world's longest-running chat show by the same broadcaster, airs on RTÉ One for the first time.
Alitalia Flight 771 crashes in Junnar, Maharashtra, India, killing 94 people.
Ne Win besieges and blows up the Rangoon University Student Union building to crush the Student Movement.
Apartheid: Nelson Mandela is jailed. He would not be released until 1990.
Burundi, Jamaica, Rwanda and Trinidad and Tobago are admitted to the United Nations.
Aeroflot Flight 213 crashes into a mountain near Chersky Airport, killing 32 people.
The People's Democratic Republic of Algeria is formally proclaimed. Ferhat Abbas is elected President of the provisional government.
Project Mercury: US astronaut Wally Schirra, in Sigma 7, is launched from Cape Canaveral for a six-orbit flight.
Der Spiegel publishes an article disclosing the sorry state of the Bundeswehr, leading to accusations of treason.
The Second Vatican Council becomes the first ecumenical council of the Roman Catholic Church in 92 years.
The Pacific Northwest experiences a cyclone the equal of a Category 3 hurricane, with winds above 150 mph. Forty-six people die.
China launches simultaneous offensives in Ladakh and across the McMahon Line, igniting the Sino-Indian War.
Cuban Missile Crisis: Adlai Stevenson shows the United Nations Security Council reconnaissance photographs of Soviet ballistic missiles in Cuba.
The Cuban Missile Crisis ends and Premier Nikita Khrushchev orders the removal of Soviet missiles from Cuba.
President John F. Kennedy dedicates Washington Dulles International Airport, serving the Washington, D.C., region.
Cold War: The West Berlin branch of the Socialist Unity Party of Germany forms a separate party, the Socialist Unity Party of West Berlin.
Prince Rainier III of Monaco revises the principality's constitution, devolving some of his power to advisory and legislative councils.
