Vietnam War: The Viet Cong wins its first major victory, at the Battle of Ap Bac.
Coup d'état in Togo results in the assassination of president Sylvanus Olympio.
The Élysée Treaty of cooperation between France and West Germany is signed by Charles de Gaulle and Konrad Adenauer.
The Guinea-Bissau War of Independence officially begins when PAIGC guerrilla fighters attack the Portuguese Army stationed in Tite.
The regime of Prime Minister of Iraq Abd al-Karim Qasim is overthrown by the Ba'ath Party.
The Dominican Republic receives its first democratically elected president, Juan Bosch, since the end of the dictatorship led by Rafael Trujillo.
Mount Agung erupts on Bali killing more than 1,100 people.
The first election of the Universal House of Justice is held, marking its establishment as the supreme governing institution of the Baháʼí Faith.
The Equal Pay Act of 1963, aimed at abolishing wage disparity based on sex, is signed into law by John F. Kennedy as part of his New Frontier Program.
Buddhist monk Thích Quảng Đức burns himself with gasoline in a busy Saigon intersection to protest the lack of religious freedom in South Vietnam.
The film Cleopatra, starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, is released in US theaters. It was the most expensive film made at the time.
Crown Colony of Sarawak gains self-governance.
An earthquake in Skopje, Yugoslavia (present-day North Macedonia) leaves 1,100 dead.
The Puijo observation tower is opened to the general public at Puijo Hill in Kuopio, Finland.
Civil rights movement: James Meredith becomes the first African American to graduate from the University of Mississippi.
Martin Luther King Jr. gives his "I have a dream" speech (28 August)
March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom: Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. gives his I Have a Dream speech.
Lord Denning releases the UK government's official report on the Profumo affair.
The Arecibo Observatory in Arecibo, Puerto Rico, with the largest radio telescope ever constructed, officially opens.
South Vietnamese President Ngô Đình Diệm is assassinated following a military coup.
The first episode of Doctor Who ("An Unearthly Child") is broadcast by the BBC, which is now the world's longest running science fiction drama.
Instant replay makes its debut during the Army-Navy football game in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.
Kenya declares independence from Great Britain.
The cruise ship Lakonia burns 290 kilometres (180 mi) north of Madeira, Portugal with the loss of 128 lives.
The Central African Federation officially collapses, subsequently becoming Zambia, Malawi and Rhodesia.
The Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland is divided into the independent republics of Zambia and Malawi, and the British-controlled Rhodesia.
Rebels in Zanzibar begin a revolt known as the Zanzibar Revolution and proclaim a republic.
Anti-Muslim riots break out in Calcutta, in response to anti-Hindu riots in East Pakistan. About one hundred people are killed.
The 24th Amendment to the United States Constitution, prohibiting the use of poll taxes in national elections, is ratified.
An unarmed United States Air Force T-39 Sabreliner on a training mission is shot down over Erfurt, East Germany, by a Soviet MiG-19.
In a bloodless coup, General Nguyễn Khánh overthrows General Dương Văn Minh's military junta in South Vietnam.
In Wesberry v. Sanders the Supreme Court of the United States rules that congressional districts have to be approximately equal in population.
Gabonese president Léon M'ba is toppled by a coup and his rival, Jean-Hilaire Aubame, is installed in his place.
At the Academy Awards, Sidney Poitier becomes the first African-American man to win the Best Actor award for the 1963 film Lilies of the Field.
Tanganyika and Zanzibar merge to form the United Republic of Tanzania.
First ascent of Shishapangma, the fourteenth highest mountain in the world and the lowest of the Eight-thousanders.
Discovery of the cosmic microwave background radiation by Robert Woodrow Wilson and Arno Penzias.
The Civil Rights Act of 1964 is approved after surviving an 83-day filibuster in the United States Senate.
Civil rights movement: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act of 1964 meant to prohibit segregation in public places.
Vietnam War: At a rally in Saigon, South Vietnamese Prime Minister Nguyễn Khánh calls for expanding the war into North Vietnam.
Second Gulf of Tonkin Incident: U.S. destroyers USS Maddox and USS Turner Joy mistakenly report coming under attack in the Gulf of Tonkin.
Syncom 3, the first geostationary communication satellite, is launched. Two months later, it would enable live coverage of the 1964 Summer Olympics.
South Vietnamese Generals Lâm Văn Phát and Dương Văn Đức fail in a coup attempt against General Nguyễn Khánh.
The first television adaptation of Charles Addams's "The Addams Family" premieres on ABC Television.
Typhoon Wilda, one of the strongest typhoons to ever strike Japan, makes landfall, causing at least 30 fatalities and sinking at least 64 ships.
Martin Luther King Jr. receives the Nobel Peace Prize for combating racial inequality through nonviolence.
The Soviet Presidium and the Communist Party Central Committee each vote to accept Nikita Khrushchev's "voluntary" request to retire from his offices.
King Saud of Saudi Arabia is deposed by a family coup, and replaced by his half-brother Faisal.
Mariner program: NASA launches the Mariner 4 probe toward Mars.
Vietnam War: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson and his top-ranking advisers meet to discuss plans to bomb North Vietnam.
The first test flight of the SR-71 (Blackbird) takes place at Air Force Plant 42 in Palmdale, California, United States.
India-Pakistan war
South Vietnamese Prime Minister Trần Văn Hương is removed by the military junta of Nguyễn Khánh.
Cosmonaut Alexei Leonov, leaving his spacecraft Voskhod 2 for 12 minutes, becomes the first person to walk in space.
NASA launches Gemini 3, the United States' first two-man space flight (crew: Gus Grissom and John Young).
Vietnam War: A car bomb explodes in front of the United States Embassy, Saigon, killing 22 and wounding 183 others.
My Fair Lady wins Best Picture at the 37th Academy Awards.
Launch of Early Bird, the first commercial communications satellite to be placed in geosynchronous orbit.
The Soviet spacecraft Luna 5 crashes on the Moon.
Vietnam War: American warships begin the first bombardment of National Liberation Front targets within South Vietnam.
Vietnam War: The United States Air Force uses B-52 bombers to attack guerrilla fighters in South Vietnam.
Nguyễn Cao Kỳ becomes Prime Minister of South Vietnam at the head of a military junta; General Nguyễn Văn Thiệu becomes the figurehead chief of state.
Bob Dylan goes electric at the Newport Folk Festival, signaling a major change in folk and rock music.
Vietnam War: The first 4,000 101st Airborne Division paratroopers arrive in Vietnam, landing at Cam Ranh Bay.
U.S. president Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Social Security Act of 1965 into law, establishing Medicare and Medicaid.
The Constitution of the Cook Islands comes into force, giving the Cook Islands self-governing status within New Zealand.
US President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Voting Rights Act of 1965 into law.
Japanese prime minister Eisaku Satō becomes the first post-World War II sitting prime minister to visit Okinawa Prefecture.
Vietnam War: A draft card is burned during an anti-war rally by the Catholic Worker Movement, resulting in the first arrest under a new law.
Pope Paul VI promulgates Nostra aetate, by which the Roman Catholic Church officially recognizes the legitimacy of non-Christian faiths.
Southern Rhodesia's Prime Minister Ian Smith unilaterally declares the colony independent as the unrecognised state of Rhodesia.
Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I simultaneously revoke mutual excommunications that had been in place since 1054.
Tashkent Declaration, a peace agreement between India and Pakistan signed that resolved the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965.
Lyndon B. Johnson states that the United States should stay in South Vietnam until Communist aggression there is ended.
Robert C. Weaver becomes the first African American Cabinet member when he is appointed United States Secretary of Housing and Urban Development.
The First Nigerian Republic, led by Abubakar Tafawa Balewa is overthrown in a military coup d'état.
Indira Gandhi becomes India's first female prime minister.
Air India Flight 101 crashes into Mont Blanc.
The three Beaumont children disappear from a beach in Glenelg, South Australia, resulting in one of the country's largest-ever police investigations.
The Soviet Union launches the unmanned Luna 9 spacecraft as part of the Luna program.
All Nippon Airways Flight 60 plunges into Tokyo Bay, killing 133.
Apollo program: Launch of AS-201, the first flight of the Saturn IB rocket.
A Canadian Pacific Air Lines DC-8-43 explodes on landing at Tokyo International Airport, killing 64 people.
In an interview in the London Evening Standard, the Beatles' John Lennon declares that the band is "more popular than Jesus now".
Off the coast of Spain in the Mediterranean, the DSV Alvin submarine finds a missing American hydrogen bomb.
United Arab Airlines Flight 749 crashes on approach to Cairo International Airport in Cairo, Egypt, killing 30 people.
The Soviet Union launches Luna 10 which later becomes the first space probe to enter orbit around the Moon.
The Labour Party under Harold Wilson wins the 1966 United Kingdom general election.
Rastafari movement: Haile Selassie of Ethiopia visits Jamaica, an event now celebrated as Grounation Day.
American Flyers Airline Flight 280/D crashes on approach to Ardmore Municipal Airport in Ardmore, Oklahoma, killing 83.
The Chinese Communist Party issues the "May 16 Notice", marking the beginning of the Cultural Revolution.
British Guiana gains independence, becoming Guyana.
Surveyor program: Surveyor 1 lands in Oceanus Procellarum on the Moon, becoming the first U.S. spacecraft to soft-land on another world.
Vietnamese Buddhist activist leader Thích Trí Quang was arrested as the military junta of Nguyen Cao Ky crushed the Buddhist Uprising.
France conducts its first nuclear weapon test in the Pacific, on Moruroa Atoll.
Malawi becomes a republic, with Hastings Banda as its first President.
King Mwambutsa IV Bangiriceng of Burundi is deposed by his son Prince Charles Ndizi.
Vietnam War: The United States and South Vietnam begin Operation Hastings to push the North Vietnamese out of the Vietnamese Demilitarized Zone.
England defeats West Germany to win the FIFA World Cup at Wembley Stadium 4–2 after extra time.
Charles Whitman kills 15 people at the University of Texas at Austin before being killed by the police.
The Heron Road Bridge collapses while being built, killing nine workers in the deadliest construction accident in both Ottawa and Ontario.
The Beatles perform their last concert before paying fans at Candlestick Park in San Francisco.
The landmark American science fiction television series Star Trek premieres with its first-aired episode, "The Man Trap".
Vietnam War: the Republic of Korea Army commits the Binh Tai Massacre.
The Black Panther Party is created by Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale.
In response to Fatah raids against Israelis near the West Bank border, Israel launches an attack on the village of As-Samu.
All Nippon Airways Flight 533 crashes into the Seto Inland Sea near Matsuyama Airport in Japan, killing 50 people.
The Temptations release their Greatest Hits album, which goes on to be the Billboard Year-End R&B album of 1967.
Bulgarian TABSO Flight 101 crashes near Bratislava, Czechoslovakia, killing all 82 people on board.
Michel Micombero overthrows the monarchy of Burundi and makes himself the first president.
The first Kwanzaa is celebrated by Maulana Karenga, the chair of Black Studies at California State University, Long Beach.
The Cave of Swallows, the largest known cave shaft in the world, is discovered in Aquismón, San Luis Potosí, Mexico.
Ronald Reagan, past movie actor and future President of the United States, is sworn in as Governor of California.
Cultural Revolution: The Shanghai People's Commune is established following the seizure of power from local city officials by revolutionaries.
Vietnam War: United States Marine Corps and ARVN troops launch "Operation Deckhouse Five" in the Mekong River delta.
Dr. James Bedford becomes the first person to be cryonically preserved with intent of future resuscitation.
Counterculture of the 1960s: The Human Be-In takes place in San Francisco, California's Golden Gate Park, launching the Summer of Love.
The first Super Bowl is played in Los Angeles. The Green Bay Packers defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 35–10.
Between dozens and hundreds of anti-Somocista demonstrators are killed by the Nicaraguan National Guard in Managua.
Diplomatic relations between the Soviet Union and Ivory Coast are established.
Cultural Revolution: The Shanghai People's Commune is formally proclaimed, with Yao Wenyuan and Zhang Chunqiao being appointed as its leaders.
Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his "Beyond Vietnam: A Time to Break Silence" speech in New York City's Riverside Church.
Gnassingbé Eyadéma overthrows Nicolas Grunitzky and installs himself as the new President of Togo, a title he will hold for the next 38 years.
Vietnam War: Boxer Muhammad Ali refuses his induction into the United States Army and is subsequently stripped of his championship and license.
After refusing induction into the United States Army the previous day, Muhammad Ali is stripped of his boxing title.
The Northrop M2-F2 crashes on landing, becoming the inspiration for the novel Cyborg and TV series The Six Million Dollar Man.
The Popular Movement of the Revolution political party is established in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Egypt imposes a blockade and siege of the Red Sea coast of Israel.
Belle de Jour, directed by Luis Buñuel, is released.
The Beatles' album Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band is released.
The U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS John F. Kennedy is launched by Jacqueline Kennedy and her daughter Caroline.
The Nigerian Eastern Region declares independence as the Republic of Biafra, sparking a civil war.
Luis Monge is executed in Colorado's gas chamber, in the last pre-Furman execution in the United States.
Six-Day War: Israeli soldiers enter Jerusalem.
The Six-Day War ends: Israel and Syria agree to a cease-fire.
The United States Supreme Court in Loving v. Virginia declares all U.S. state laws that prohibit interracial marriage to be unconstitutional.
U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson nominates Solicitor-General Thurgood Marshall to become the first black justice on the U.S. Supreme Court.
Mariner program: Mariner 5 is launched towards Venus.
Nigerian Civil War: Nigerian forces invade Biafra, beginning the war.
Vietnam War: Off the coast of North Vietnam the USS Forrestal catches on fire in the worst U.S. naval disaster since World War II, killing 134.
UK Marine Broadcasting Offences Act 1967 declares participation in offshore pirate radio illegal.
Thurgood Marshall is confirmed as the first African American Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
Six-Day War: The Khartoum Resolution is issued at the Arab Summit, and eight countries adopt the "three 'no's against Israel".
Vietnam War: Operation Swift begins when U.S. Marines engage the North Vietnamese in battle in the Que Son Valley.
Thurgood Marshall is sworn in as the first African-American justice of the United States Supreme Court.
Mohammad Reza Pahlavi crowns himself Emperor of Iran.
Carl B. Stokes is elected as Mayor of Cleveland, Ohio, becoming the first African American mayor of a major American city.
US President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Public Broadcasting Act of 1967, establishing the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.
The first pulsar (PSR B1919+21, in the constellation of Vulpecula) is discovered by two astronomers Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish.
Harold Holt, Prime Minister of Australia, disappears while swimming near Portsea, Victoria, and is presumed drowned.
Alexander Dubček comes to power in Czechoslovakia, effectively beginning the "Prague Spring".
Surveyor program: Surveyor 7, the last spacecraft in the Surveyor series, lifts off from Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36A.
Johnny Cash performs live at Folsom State Prison.
Vietnam War, Battle of Khe Sanh: One of the most publicized and controversial battles of the war begins.
Apollo Program: Apollo 5 lifts off carrying the first Lunar module into space.
Operation Igloo White, a US electronic surveillance system to stop communist infiltration into South Vietnam begins installation.
Vietnam War: Tet Offensive launch by forces of the Viet Cong and North Vietnamese Army against South Vietnam, the United States, and their allies.
Canada's three military services, the Royal Canadian Navy, the Canadian Army and the Royal Canadian Air Force, are unified into the Canadian Forces.
The New York Central Railroad and the Pennsylvania Railroad are merged to form Penn Central Transportation.
As a result of nerve gas testing by the U.S. Army Chemical Corps in Skull Valley, Utah, over 6,000 sheep are found dead.
Gold standard: The U.S. Congress repeals the requirement for a gold reserve to back US currency.
Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated by James Earl Ray at a motel in Memphis, Tennessee.
Apollo program: NASA launches Apollo 6.
Two-time Formula One British World Champion Jim Clark dies in an accident during a Formula Two race in Hockenheim.
Vietnam War: North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces attack Australian troops defending Fire Support Base Coral.
James Earl Ray, the man who assassinated Martin Luther King Jr. is arrested at London Heathrow Airport.
Lloyd J. Old identifies the first cell surface antigens that could differentiate among different cell types.
The first International Special Olympics Summer Games are held at Soldier Field in Chicago, with about 1,000 athletes with intellectual disabilities.
Alexandros Panagoulis attempts to assassinate the Greek dictator Colonel Georgios Papadopoulos in Varkiza, Athens.
Cold War: Albania leaves the Warsaw Pact.
A Fairchild F-27 crashes into Moose Mountain while on approach to Lebanon Municipal Airport in Lebanon, New Hampshire, killing 32 people.
Space Race: The Soyuz 3 mission achieves the first Soviet space rendezvous.
Vietnam War: Operation Commando Hunt initiated. The goal is to interdict men and supplies on the Ho Chi Minh trail, through Laos into South Vietnam.
Japan Air Lines Flight 2 accidentally ditches in San Francisco Bay while on approach to San Francisco International Airport. No one is injured.
The Communist Party of the Philippines is established by Jose Maria Sison, breaking away from the Partido Komunista ng Pilipinas-1930.
Ariana Afghan Airlines Flight 701 crashes in Fernhill, West Sussex, UK, while on approach to Gatwick Airport, killing 50 people.
The Venera 5 space probe is launched at 06:28:08 UTC from Baikonur.
USS Enterprise fire: An accidental explosion aboard the USS Enterprise near Hawaii kills 28 people.
Black Panther Party members Bunchy Carter and John Huggins are killed during a meeting in Campbell Hall on the campus of UCLA.
Brazilian Army captain Carlos Lamarca deserts in order to fight against the military dictatorship, taking with him ten machine guns and 63 rifles.
The Beatles' last public performance, on the roof of Apple Records in London. The impromptu concert is broken up by the police.
Apollo program: NASA launches Apollo 9 to test the lunar module.
In Memphis, Tennessee, James Earl Ray pleads guilty to assassinating Martin Luther King Jr. He later unsuccessfully attempts to recant.
Golda Meir becomes the first female Prime Minister of Israel.
The United States begins secretly bombing the Sihanouk Trail in Cambodia, used by communist forces to infiltrate South Vietnam.
Dr. Denton Cooley implants the first temporary artificial heart.
British yachtsman Sir Robin Knox-Johnston wins the Sunday Times Golden Globe Race and completes the first solo non-stop circumnavigation of the world.
Charles de Gaulle resigns as President of France.
Carlos Lamarca leads the first urban guerrilla action against the military dictatorship of Brazil in São Paulo, by robbing two banks.
Vietnam War: The Battle of Dong Ap Bia begins with an assault on Hill 937. It will ultimately become known as Hamburger Hill.
In the aftermath of the 1969 Malaysian general election, Sino-Malay sectarian violence erupts in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Venera program: Venera 5, a Soviet space probe, lands on Venus.
Warren E. Burger is sworn in as Chief Justice of the United States Supreme Court by retiring Chief Justice Earl Warren.
Apollo 11: Neil Armstrong walks on the Moon (20 July)
A cease fire is announced between Honduras and El Salvador, six days after the beginning of the "Football War".
Apollo program: At 02:56 UTC, astronaut Neil Armstrong becomes the first person to walk on the Moon, followed 19 minutes later by Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin.
A day after murdering actress Sharon Tate and four others, members of Charles Manson's cult kill Leno and Rosemary LaBianca.
ISRO founded (15 August)
A coup in Libya brings Muammar Gaddafi to power.
In Chicago, the National Guard is called in as demonstrations continue over the trial of the "Chicago Eight".
Vietnam War: Independent investigative journalist Seymour Hersh breaks the story of the My Lai Massacre.
A Spantax Convair CV-990 Coronado crashes during takeoff from Stockholm Arlanda Airport, killing five people.
Biafra capitulates, ending the Nigerian Civil War.
Nigerian Civil War: Biafran rebels surrender following an unsuccessful 32-month fight for independence from Nigeria.
Vietnam War: Captain Ernest Medina is charged by the U.S. military with My Lai war crimes.
Lon Nol ousts Prince Norodom Sihanouk of Cambodia.
Paul McCartney announces that he is leaving The Beatles for personal and professional reasons.
Apollo Program: Apollo 13 is launched.
Chicano residents in San Diego, California occupy a site under the Coronado Bridge, leading to the creation of Chicano Park.
Vietnam War: US President Richard Nixon formally authorizes American combat troops to take part in the Cambodian campaign.
Vietnam War: A student anti-war strike erupts in response to U.S. and South Vietnamese forces attacking Vietnamese communists in a Cambodian Campaign.
ALM Flight 980 ditches in the Caribbean Sea near Saint Croix, killing 23.
President Richard Nixon appoints Anna Mae Hays and Elizabeth P. Hoisington as the first female United States Army generals.
The Soviet Tupolev Tu-144 becomes the first commercial transport to exceed Mach 2.
The Troubles: The "Falls Curfew" begins in Belfast, Northern Ireland.
Black Tot Day: The last day of the officially sanctioned rum ration in the Royal Navy.
Organized by Mexican American labor union leader César Chávez, the Salad Bowl strike, the largest farm worker strike in U.S. history, begins.
Chicano Moratorium against the Vietnam War, East Los Angeles, California. Police riot kills three people, including journalist Rubén Salazar.
NASA announces the cancellation of two Apollo missions to the Moon, Apollo 15 (the designation is re-used by a later mission), and Apollo 19.
Trans International Airlines Flight 863 crashes during takeoff from John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City, killing all 11 aboard.
A British airliner is hijacked by the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine and flown to Dawson's Field in Jordan.
Michael Eavis hosts the first Glastonbury Festival.
An aircraft carrying the Wichita State University football team, administrators, and supporters crashes in Colorado, killing 31 people.
Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn wins the Nobel Prize in literature.
The Oregon Highway Division attempts to destroy a rotting beached sperm whale with explosives, leading to the now infamous "exploding whale" incident.
Vietnam War: Lieutenant William Calley goes on trial for the My Lai Massacre.
U.S. President Richard Nixon asks the U.S. Congress for $155 million in supplemental aid for the Cambodian government.
First microprocessor, the Intel 4004
The second Ibrox disaster kills 66 fans at a Rangers-Celtic association football match.
The current Emley Moor transmitting station, the tallest free-standing structure in the United Kingdom, begins transmitting UHF broadcasts.
The Singapore Declaration, one of the two most important documents to the uncodified constitution of the Commonwealth of Nations, is issued.
Idi Amin leads a coup deposing Milton Obote and becomes Uganda's president.
Charles Manson and four "Family" members (three of them female) are found guilty of the 1969 Tate–LaBianca murders.
The last of its many UFO sightings is made at Pudasjärvi, Finland.
Idi Amin replaces President Milton Obote as leader of Uganda.
The international Ramsar Convention for the conservation and sustainable utilization of wetlands is signed in Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran.
South Vietnamese ground troops launch an incursion into Laos to try to cut off the Ho Chi Minh trail and stop communist infiltration into the country.
The 6.5–6.7 Mw Sylmar earthquake hits the Greater Los Angeles Area with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing 64 and injuring 2,000.
Satchel Paige becomes the first Negro league player to be voted into the USA's Baseball Hall of Fame.
U.N. Secretary-General U Thant signs United Nations proclamation of the vernal equinox as Earth Day.
Peru: A landslide crashes into Yanawayin Lake, killing 200 people at the mining camp of Chungar.
In Sri Lanka, Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna launches a revolt against the United Front government of Sirimavo Bandaranaike.
Vietnam War: President Richard Nixon announces his decision to quicken the pace of Vietnamization.
Sierra Leone becomes a republic, and Siaka Stevens the president.
Charles Manson is sentenced to death (later commuted to life imprisonment) for conspiracy in the Tate–LaBianca murders.
Bangladesh Liberation War: The Pakistan Army slaughters at least 71 Hindus in Burunga, Sylhet, Bangladesh.
Mariner program: Mariner 9 is launched to map 70% of the surface, and to study temporal changes in the atmosphere and surface, of Mars.
The Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms Division of the U.S. Internal Revenue Service raids the home of Ken Ballew for illegal possession of hand grenades.
Allegheny Airlines Flight 485 crashes on approach to Tweed New Haven Airport in New Haven, Connecticut, killing 28 of 31 aboard.
Vietnam War: The New York Times begins publication of the Pentagon Papers.
Apollo program: Launch of Apollo 15 on the first Apollo "J-Mission", and first use of a Lunar Roving Vehicle.
Apollo program: On Apollo 15, David Scott and James Irwin in the Apollo Lunar Module Falcon land on the Moon with the first Lunar Rover.
An All Nippon Airways Boeing 727 and a Japanese Air Force F-86 collide over Morioka, Iwate, Japan, killing 162.
Apollo program: The Apollo 15 astronauts become the first to ride in a lunar rover.
The four-day Attica Prison riot begins, eventually resulting in 39 dead, most killed by state troopers retaking the prison.
State police and National Guardsmen storm New York's Attica Prison to quell a prison revolt, which claimed 43 lives.
South Vietnamese President Nguyen Van Thieu is re-elected in a one-man election.
British European Airways Flight 706 crashes near Aarsele, Belgium, killing 63.
The People's Republic of China replaces the Republic of China at the United Nations.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo is renamed Zaire.
The United States Atomic Energy Commission tests the largest U.S. underground hydrogen bomb, code-named Cannikin, on Amchitka Island in the Aleutians.
Representatives of the People's Republic of China attend the United Nations, including the United Nations Security Council, for the first time.
Wasfi al-Tal, Prime Minister of Jordan, is assassinated by the Black September unit of the Palestine Liberation Organization.
Purge of Croatian Spring leaders starts in Yugoslavia at the meeting of the League of Communists at the Karađorđevo estate.
Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Fujairah, Sharjah, Dubai, and Umm al-Quwain form the United Arab Emirates.
The Battle of Sylhet is fought between the Pakistani military and the Indian Army.
Bangladesh Liberation War; Bangladesh is born (16 December)
The international aid organization Doctors Without Borders is founded by Bernard Kouchner and a group of journalists in Paris, France.
US President Richard Nixon announces the Space Shuttle program.
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman returns to the newly independent Bangladesh as president after spending over nine months in prison in Pakistan.
Prime Minister Kofi Abrefa Busia and President Edward Akufo-Addo of Ghana are ousted in a bloodless military coup by Colonel Ignatius Kutu Acheampong.
Japanese Sgt. Shoichi Yokoi is found hiding in a Guam jungle, where he had been since the end of World War II.
Pakistan leaves the Commonwealth of Nations in protest of its recognition of breakaway Bangladesh.
Kuala Lumpur becomes a city by a royal charter granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong of Malaysia.
Direct rule is imposed on Northern Ireland by the Government of the United Kingdom under Edward Heath.
Vietnam War: The Easter Offensive begins after North Vietnamese forces cross into the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) of South Vietnam.
Vietnam War: Communist forces overrun the South Vietnamese town of Loc Ninh.
Vietnam War: For the first time since November 1967, American B-52 bombers reportedly begin bombing North Vietnam.
East African Airways Flight 720 crashes during a rejected takeoff from Addis Ababa Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, killing 43.
Apollo program: The Apollo 16 Lunar Module Orion, commanded by John Young and piloted by Charles Duke, lands on the Moon.
Astronauts John Young and Charles Duke fly Apollo 16's Apollo Lunar Module to the Moon's surface, the fifth NASA Apollo Program crewed lunar landing.
Alitalia Flight 112 crashes into Mount Longa near Palermo, Sicily, killing all 115 aboard, making it the deadliest single-aircraft disaster in Italy.
The Ryukyu Islands, under U.S. military governance since their conquest in 1945, revert to Japanese control.
An Antonov An-24 crashes into a kindergarten building in Svetlogorsk, killing 35.
Michelangelo's Pietà in St. Peter's Basilica in Rome is damaged by a vandal, the mentally disturbed Hungarian geologist Laszlo Toth.
Cold War: The United States and the Soviet Union sign the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty.
Staines air disaster: One hundred eighteen people are killed when a BEA H.S. Trident crashes minutes after takeoff from London's Heathrow Airport.
Dhofar Rebellion: British SAS units help the Omani government against Popular Front for the Liberation of Oman rebels in the Battle of Mirbat.
Two Avianca Douglas DC-3 airliners collide over Colombia, killing 38.
Japan establishes diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China after breaking official ties with the Republic of China.
Aeroflot Flight 217 crashes outside Moscow, killing 174.
Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 crashes in the Andes mountains. Twenty-eight survive the crash. All but 16 succumb before rescue on December 23.
The flag of Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, was officially adopted.
Vietnam War: Vietnamization: The United States Army turns over the massive Long Binh military base to South Vietnam.
Apollo 17, the last Apollo Moon mission, is launched. The crew takes the photograph known as The Blue Marble as they leave the Earth.
Apollo 17 becomes the sixth and final Apollo mission to land on the Moon.
Denmark, Ireland and the United Kingdom are admitted into the European Economic Community.
Watergate scandal: The trial of seven men accused of illegal entry into Democratic Party headquarters at Watergate begins.
Major League Baseball owners vote in approval of the American League adopting the designated hitter position.
Vietnam War: Citing progress in peace negotiations, President Richard Nixon announces the suspension of offensive action in North Vietnam.
Amílcar Cabral, leader of the independence movement in Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde, is assassinated in Conakry, Guinea.
A chartered Boeing 707 explodes in flames upon landing at Kano Airport, Nigeria, killing 176.
EgyptAir Flight 741 crashes into the Kyrenia Mountains in Cyprus, killing 37 people.
The American Indian Movement occupies Wounded Knee in protest of the federal government.
Operation Barrel Roll, a covert American bombing campaign in Laos to stop communist infiltration of South Vietnam, ends.
Vietnam War: The last United States combat soldiers leave South Vietnam.
A Lockheed C-141 Starlifter, dubbed the Hanoi Taxi, makes the last flight of Operation Homecoming.
The American League of Major League Baseball begins using the designated hitter.
Invicta International Airlines Flight 435 crashes in a snowstorm on approach to Basel, Switzerland, killing 108 people.
Secretariat wins the 1973 Kentucky Derby in 1:59.4, an as-yet-unbeaten record.
Aeroflot Flight 6551 crashes in Semey, Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic (now Kazakhstan), killing all 63 aboard.
Citing government misconduct, Daniel Ellsberg's charges for his involvement in releasing the Pentagon Papers to The New York Times are dismissed.
Indian Airlines Flight 440 crashes near Palam Airport in Delhi, killing 48.
In Lillehammer, Norway, Mossad agents kill a waiter whom they mistakenly thought was involved in the 1972 Munich Olympics Massacre.
Pan Am Flight 816 crashes after takeoff from Faa'a International Airport in Papeete, French Polynesia, killing 78.
Summer Jam at Watkins Glen: Nearly 600,000 people attend a rock festival at the Watkins Glen International Raceway.
A Delta Air Lines jetliner, flight DL 723, crashes while landing in fog at Logan International Airport, Boston, Massachusetts, killing 89.
Aviaco Flight 118 crashes on approach to A Coruña Airport in A Coruña, Spain, killing all 85 people on the plane and one other one the ground.
Aeroflot Flight A-13 crashes after takeoff from Baku-Bina International Airport in Azerbaijan, killing 56 people and injuring eight.
A 76-hour multinational rescue effort in the Celtic Sea results in the rescue of Roger Mallinson and Roger Chapman.
World Airways Flight 802 crashes into Mount Dutton in King Cove, Alaska, killing six people.
Billie Jean King beats Bobby Riggs in the Battle of the Sexes tennis match at the Houston Astrodome.
Argentine general election: Juan Perón returns to power in Argentina.
The Sydney Opera House is opened by Elizabeth II after 14 years of construction.
Egypt and Israel accept United Nations Security Council Resolution 339.
Mysore State renamed Karnataka (1 November)
Skylab program: NASA launches Skylab 4 with a crew of three astronauts from Cape Canaveral, Florida for an 84-day mission.
U.S. president Richard Nixon signs the Trans-Alaska Pipeline Authorization Act into law, authorizing the construction of the Alaska Pipeline.
Watergate scandal: In Orlando, Florida, U.S. President Richard Nixon tells 400 Associated Press managing editors "I am not a crook."
The Athens Polytechnic uprising against the military regime ends in a bloodshed in the Greek capital.
Thirty passengers are killed in an attack by Palestinian terrorists on Rome's Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport.
The Geneva Conference on the Arab–Israeli conflict opens.
A Royal Air Maroc Sud Aviation Caravelle crashes near Tangier-Boukhalef Airport in Tangier, Morocco, killing 106.
The United States Endangered Species Act is signed into law by President Richard Nixon.
China gains control over all the Paracel Islands after a military engagement between the naval forces of China and South Vietnam.
Pan Am Flight 806 crashes near Pago Pago International Airport in American Samoa, killing 97.
The Symbionese Liberation Army kidnaps Patty Hearst in Berkeley, California.
The crew of Skylab 4, the last mission to visit the American space station Skylab, returns to Earth after 84 days in space.
Robert K. Preston, a disgruntled U.S. Army private, buzzes the White House in a stolen helicopter.
NASA's Mariner 10 becomes the first space probe to fly by Mercury.
The Terracotta Army is discovered in Shaanxi province, China.
Carrie, the first novel by American author Stephen King, is published for the first time with a print run of 30,000 copies.
Pan Am Flight 812 crashes on approach to Ngurah Rai International Airport in Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia, killing all 107 people on board.
Watergate scandal: The  United States House Committee on the Judiciary opens formal and public impeachment hearings against President Richard Nixon.
Josip Broz Tito is elected president for life of Yugoslavia.
India's first nuclear test at Pokhran (18 May)
Northern Ireland's power-sharing Sunningdale Agreement collapses following a general strike by loyalists.
U.S. president Richard Nixon visits the Soviet Union.
Turkish invasion of Cyprus: Forces from Turkey invade Cyprus after a coup d'état, organized by the dictator of Greece, against president Makarios.
Greek Prime Minister Konstantinos Karamanlis forms the country's first civil government after seven years of military rule.
Cyprus dispute: The United Nations Security Council authorizes the UNFICYP to create the "Green Line", dividing Cyprus into two zones.
A bomb explodes in the Italicus Express train at San Benedetto Val di Sambro, Italy, killing 12 people and wounding 22.
Yuk Young-soo, First Lady of South Korea, is killed during an apparent assassination attempt upon President Park Chung Hee.
A Belgrade–Dortmund express train derails at the main train station in Zagreb killing 153 passengers.
Watergate scandal: US President Gerald Ford signs the pardon of Richard Nixon for any crimes Nixon may have committed while in office.
Bangladesh, Grenada and Guinea-Bissau join the United Nations.
Dr. Frank Jobe performs first ulnar collateral ligament replacement surgery (better known as Tommy John surgery) on baseball player Tommy John.
TWA Flight 514, a Boeing 727, crashes northwest of Dulles International Airport, killing all 92 people on board.
Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mohéli vote to become the independent nation of Comoros. Mayotte remains under French administration.
At the opening of a new railway line, a bomb blast at Samastipur, Bihar, India, fatally wounds Lalit Narayan Mishra, Minister of Railways.
The Tasman Bridge in Tasmania, Australia, is struck by the bulk ore carrier Lake Illawarra, killing twelve people.
Turkish Airlines Flight 345 crashes into the Sea of Marmara near Istanbul Yeşilköy Airport, killing 42.
Haicheng earthquake (magnitude 7.3 on the Richter scale) occurs in Haicheng, Liaoning, China.
The Soyuz 17 Soviet spacecraft returns to Earth.
Microsoft is founded as a partnership between Bill Gates and Paul Allen in Albuquerque, New Mexico.
Beirut bus massacre: A confrontation between Phalangist paramilitaries and PLO militia marks the start of the 15-year Lebanese Civil War.
Aryabhata, India's first satellite, launched (19 April)
India's first satellite Aryabhata launched in orbit from Kapustin Yar, Russia.
South Vietnamese forces withdraw from the town of Xuan Loc in the last major battle of the Vietnam War.
General Cao Văn Viên, chief of the South Vietnamese military, departs for the US as the North Vietnamese Army closes in on victory.
Vietnam War: The North Vietnamese Army completes its capture of all parts of South Vietnam-held Trường Sa Islands.
Sony introduces the Betamax videocassette recorder.
Indochina Wars: Democratic Kampuchea naval forces capture the SS Mayaguez.
Junko Tabei from Japan becomes the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
Fifteen West African countries sign the Treaty of Lagos, creating the Economic Community of West African States.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan was founded by Jalal Talabani, Nawshirwan Mustafa, Fuad Masum and others.
British referendum results in continued membership of the European Economic Community, with 67% of votes in favour.
Sony launches Betamax, the first videocassette recorder format.
Mayor of Jaffna and former MP Alfred Duraiappah is shot dead.
The final act of the CSCE meeting is signed in Helsinki, Finland.
A privately chartered Boeing 707 strikes a mountain peak and crashes near Agadir, Morocco, killing 188.
The Pontiac Silverdome opens in Pontiac, Michigan, 30 miles (48 km) northwest of Detroit, Michigan.
Southwest Face expedition members become the first persons to reach the summit of Mount Everest by any of its faces, instead of using a ridge route.
Malév Flight 240 crashes into the Mediterranean Sea while on approach to Beirut International Airport in Beirut, Lebanon, killing 60.
An RAF Avro Vulcan bomber explodes and crashes over Żabbar, Malta after an aborted landing, killing five crew members and one person on the ground.
Juan Carlos is declared King of Spain following the death of Francisco Franco two days earlier.
U.S. President Gerald Ford creates the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in response to the 1970s energy crisis.
Tu-144, the world's first commercial supersonic aircraft, surpassing Mach 2, goes into service.
The Khmer Rouge announce that the new Constitution of Democratic Kampuchea is ratified.
Gerald Ford's would-be assassin, Sara Jane Moore, is sentenced to life in prison.
In Guatemala and Honduras an earthquake kills more than 22,000.
Aeroflot Flight 3739, a Tupolev Tu-104, crashes during takeoff from Irkutsk Airport, killing 24.
In China, the April Fifth Movement leads to the Tiananmen Incident.
Member of Parliament and suspected spy John Stonehouse resigns from the Labour Party after being arrested for faking his own death.
Thirty-seven people are killed when American Airlines Flight 625 crashes at Cyril E. King Airport in Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands.
The 6.5 Mw Friuli earthquake affects Northern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), leaving 900–978 dead and 1,700–2,400 injured.
The Judgment of Paris takes place in France, launching California as a worldwide force in the production of quality wine.
Air France Flight 139 (Tel Aviv-Athens-Paris) is hijacked en route to Paris by the PFLP and redirected to Entebbe, Uganda.
The Angolan court sentences US and UK mercenaries to death sentences and prison terms in the Luanda Trial.
End of South Vietnam; Communist North Vietnam annexes the former South Vietnam to form the unified Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
Viking program: Viking 1 takes the famous Face on Mars photo.
Niki Lauda has a severe accident that almost claims his life at the German Grand Prix at Nürburgring.
Viking program: Viking 2 enters orbit around Mars.
SAETA Flight 011 crashes into the Chimborazo volcano in Ecuador, killing all 59 people on board; the wreckage is not discovered until 2002.
The Soviet Union's robotic probe Luna 24 successfully lands on the Moon.
Viking program: The American Viking 2 spacecraft lands at Utopia Planitia on Mars.
A Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano Boeing 707 crashes after takeoff from El Trompillo Airport in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia, killing 91.
The first electron micrograph of an Ebola virus is taken at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention by Dr. F. A. Murphy.
Burundian president Michel Micombero is deposed in a bloodless military coup d'état by deputy Jean-Baptiste Bagaza.
Fidel Castro becomes President of Cuba, replacing Osvaldo Dorticós Torrado.
Linjeflyg Flight 618 crashes in Kälvesta near Stockholm Bromma Airport in Stockholm, Sweden, killing 22 people.
Capital punishment in the United States resumes after a ten-year hiatus, as convicted murderer Gary Gilmore is executed by firing squad in Utah.
President Gerald Ford pardons Iva Toguri D'Aquino (a.k.a. "Tokyo Rose").
A Chicago Transit Authority elevated train rear-ends another and derails, killing 11 and injuring 180, the worst accident in the agency's history.
A thousand armed soldiers raid Kalakuta Republic, the commune of Nigerian singer Fela Kuti, leading to the death of Funmilayo Anikulapo Kuti.
Morarji Desai becomes the prime minister of India, the first prime minister not to belong to Indian National Congress.
London Transport's Silver Jubilee AEC Routemaster buses are launched.
Annie opens on Broadway.
Optical fiber is first used to carry live telephone traffic.
A Dan-Air Boeing 707 leased to IAS Cargo Airlines crashes on approach to Lusaka International Airport in Lusaka, Zambia, killing six people.
A plane crash at José Martí International Airport in Havana, Cuba, kills 67.
James Earl Ray escapes from Brushy Mountain State Penitentiary in Petros, Tennessee. He is recaptured three days later.
Constitution for the Federation of Earth was adopted by the second session of the World Constituent Assembly, held at Innsbruck, Austria.
The Pinochet dictatorship in Chile organises the youth event of Acto de Chacarillas, a ritualised act reminiscent of Francoist Spain.
Somalia declares war on Ethiopia, starting the Ogaden War.
The Central Intelligence Agency releases documents under the Freedom of Information Act revealing it had engaged in mind-control experiments.
Aeroflot Flight B-2 crashes after takeoff from Vitim Airport in the Sakha Republic, killing 39.
Tandy Corporation announces the TRS-80, one of the world's first mass-produced personal computers.
U.S. President Jimmy Carter signs legislation creating the United States Department of Energy.
Members of the British National Front (NF) clash with anti-NF demonstrators in Lewisham, London, resulting in 214 arrests and at least 111 injuries.
Hijacking of Lufthansa Flight 181 by the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.
A plane carrying the rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd crashes in woodland in Mississippi, United States. Six people, including three band members, are killed.
The Kelly Barnes Dam, located above Toccoa Falls College near Toccoa, Georgia, fails, killing 39.
A Tupolev Tu-154 crashes near Benghazi, Libya, killing 59.
The Budd Company unveils its first SPV-2000 self-propelled railcar in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
The first computer bulletin board system is created (CBBS in Chicago).
Coastal Road massacre: At least 37 are killed and more than 70 are wounded when Fatah hijack an Israeli bus, prompting Israel's Operation Litani.
The first UNIFIL troops arrive in Lebanon for a peacekeeping mission along the Blue Line.
Tbilisi demonstrations: Thousands of Georgians demonstrate against Soviet attempts to change the constitutional status of the Georgian language.
The Ba Chúc massacre begins, which precipitates the Cambodian–Vietnamese War the same year.
The President of Afghanistan, Mohammad Daoud Khan, is overthrown and assassinated in a coup led by pro-communist rebels.
Altaf Hussain founds the student political movement All Pakistan Muhajir Students Organisation (APMSO) in Karachi University.
Garfield's first comic strip, originally published locally as Jon in 1976, goes into nationwide syndication.
Charon, the first of Pluto's satellites to be discovered, was first seen at the United States Naval Observatory by James W. Christy.
Hosts Argentina defeat the Netherlands by a score of 3–1 in the final to win their first ever FIFA World Cup.
The rainbow flag representing gay pride is flown for the first time during the San Francisco Gay Freedom Day Parade.
The 730: Okinawa Prefecture changes its traffic on the right-hand side of the road to the left-hand side.
U.S. President Jimmy Carter declares a federal emergency at Love Canal due to toxic waste that had been disposed of negligently.
One hundred fifty Palestinians in Beirut are killed in a terrorist attack during the second phase of the Lebanese Civil War.
Finnair Flight 405 is hijacked by Aarno Lamminparras in Oulu, Finland.
Aeroflot Flight 1080 crashes after takeoff from Koltsovo International Airport, killing 38.
Australian civilian pilot Frederick Valentich vanishes over the Bass Strait south of Melbourne, after reporting contact with an unidentified aircraft.
The McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet makes its first flight, at the Naval Air Test Center in Maryland, United States.
The Geneva Frequency Plan of 1975 goes into effect, realigning many of Europe's longwave and mediumwave broadcasting frequencies.
In San Francisco, city mayor George Moscone and openly gay city supervisor Harvey Milk are assassinated by former supervisor Dan White.
United Airlines Flight 173 crashes in a residential neighborhood near Portland International Airport, killing 10 people.
Third Indochina War: Cambodian–Vietnamese War: Phnom Penh falls to the advancing Vietnamese troops, driving out Pol Pot and the Khmer Rouge.
Iranian Revolution: The last Iranian Shah flees Iran with his family for good and relocates to Egypt.
Pope John Paul II starts his first official papal visits outside Italy to The Bahamas, Dominican Republic, and Mexico.
Iranian Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini returns to Tehran after nearly 15 years of exile.
The Superliner railcar enters revenue service with Amtrak.
Aeroflot Flight 1691 crashes on approach to Vnukovo International Airport, killing 58.
Quebecair Flight 255 crashes after takeoff from Québec City Jean Lesage International Airport in Quebec City, killing 17.
Red River Valley tornado outbreak: A tornado lands in Wichita Falls, Texas, killing 42 people.
Ugandan dictator Idi Amin is deposed.
Eruption of Mount Marapi: Mount Marapi, a complex volcano on the Indonesian island of Sumatra, erupts. Between 80 and 100 people are killed.
White Night riots in San Francisco following the manslaughter conviction of Dan White for the assassinations of George Moscone and Harvey Milk.
Konstantinos Karamanlis signs the full treaty of the accession of Greece with the European Economic Community.
Downeast Airlines Flight 46 crashes on approach to Knox County Regional Airport in Rockland, Maine, killing 17.
Pope John Paul II starts his first official visit to his native Poland, becoming the first Pope to visit a Communist country.
Bryan Allen wins the second Kremer prize for a man-powered flight across the English Channel in the Gossamer Albatross.
U.S. President Jimmy Carter signs the first directive for secret aid to the opponents of the pro-Soviet regime in Kabul.
U.S. president Jimmy Carter gives his "malaise speech".
The Sandinista rebels overthrow the government of the Somoza family in Nicaragua.
Jay Silverheels, a Mohawk actor, becomes the first Native American to have a star commemorated in the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
A French-organized coup d'état in the Central African Empire overthrows Emperor Bokassa I.
Equatorial Guinean dictator Francisco Macías Nguema is executed by soldiers from Western Sahara.
Swissair Flight 316 crashes at Ellinikon International Airport in Athens, Greece, killing 14.
A coup d'état in El Salvador overthrows President Carlos Humberto Romero and begins the 12 year-long Salvadoran Civil War.
Moshe Dayan resigns from the Israeli government because of strong disagreements with Prime Minister Menachem Begin over policy towards the Arabs.
Park Chung Hee, President of South Korea, is assassinated by Korean CIA head Kim Jae-gyu.
In Bolivia, Colonel Alberto Natusch executes a bloody coup d'état against the constitutional government of Wálter Guevara.
The first line of Bucharest Metro (Line M1) is opened from Timpuri Noi to Semănătoarea in Bucharest, Romania.
Air New Zealand Flight 901, a DC-10 sightseeing flight over Antarctica, crashes into Mount Erebus, killing all 257 people on board.
Coup d'état of December Twelfth occurs in South Korea.
Iran Air Flight 291 crashes in the Alborz Mountains while on approach to Mehrabad International Airport in Tehran, Iran, killing 128 people.
Reports surface that the FBI is targeting allegedly corrupt Congressmen in the Abscam operation.
First winter ascent of Mount Everest by Krzysztof Wielicki and Leszek Cichy.
The government of Suriname is overthrown by a military coup led by Dési Bouterse.
The USS Nautilus is decommissioned and stricken from the Naval Vessel Register.
Nationalist leader Robert Mugabe wins a sweeping election victory to become Zimbabwe's first black prime minister.
A Vostok-2M rocket at Plesetsk Cosmodrome Site 43 explodes during a fueling operation, killing 48 people.
El Salvadorian Archbishop Óscar Romero is assassinated while celebrating Mass in San Salvador.
Beatrix is inaugurated as Queen of the Netherlands following the abdication of Juliana.
Operation Nimrod: The British Special Air Service storms the Iranian embassy in London after a six-day siege.
An F3 tornado hits Kalamazoo County, Michigan. President Jimmy Carter declares it a federal disaster area.
Salvadoran Civil War: The Sumpul River massacre occurs in Chalatenango, El Salvador.
During the Lebanese Civil War, 83 Tiger militants are killed during what will be known as the Safra massacre.
The inaugural 1980 State of Origin game is won by Queensland who defeat New South Wales 20–10 at Lang Park.
A train crash kills 18 people and injures over 170 more in County Cork, Ireland.
Lech Wałęsa leads strikes at the Gdańsk, Poland shipyards.
After weeks of strikes at the Lenin Shipyard in Gdańsk, Poland, the nationwide independent trade union Solidarity is established.
Michael Myers becomes the first member of either chamber of Congress to be expelled since the Civil War.
Pope John Paul II greets the Dalai Lama during a private audience in Vatican City.
The 6th Congress of the Workers' Party ended, having anointed North Korean President Kim Il Sung's son Kim Jong Il as his successor.
Proceedings on the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction conclude.
The Chun Doo-hwan government forcibly arrests and investigates monks and personnel of the Jogye Order.
The NASA space probe Voyager I makes its closest approach to Saturn and takes the first images of its rings.
The 6.9 Mw Irpinia earthquake shakes southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), killing 2,483–4,900, and injuring 7,700–8,934.
Salvadoran Civil War: The FMLN launches its first major offensive, gaining control of most of Morazán and Chalatenango departments.
Pope John Paul II receives a delegation from the Polish trade union Solidarity at the Vatican led by Lech Wałęsa.
President of the Philippines Ferdinand Marcos lifts martial law eight years and five months after declaring it.
Twenty minutes after Ronald Reagan is inaugurated as the 40th President of the United States of America, Iran releases 52 American hostages.
Production of the DeLorean sports car begins in Dunmurry, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.
A plane crash at Pushkin Airport kills 50 people, including 16 members of the Pacific Fleet.
Iran–Iraq War: The Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force mounts an attack on H-3 Airbase and destroys about 50 Iraqi aircraft.
The first launch of a Space Shuttle (Columbia) takes place: The STS-1 mission.
STS-1: The first operational Space Shuttle, Columbia, completes its first test flight.
Dr. Michael R. Harrison of the University of California, San Francisco Medical Center performs the world's first human open fetal surgery.
Bobby Sands dies in the Long Kesh prison hospital (Northern Ireland) after 66 days of hunger-striking, aged 27.
In Riyadh, the Gulf Cooperation Council is created between Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
An EA-6B Prowler crashes on the flight deck of the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, killing 14 crewmen and injuring 45 others.
The Israeli Air Force destroys Iraq's Osiraq nuclear reactor during Operation Opera.
At the Trooping the Colour ceremony in London, a teenager, Marcus Sarjeant, fires six blank shots at Queen Elizabeth II.
The Humber Bridge opens to traffic, connecting Yorkshire and Lincolnshire. It remained the world's longest bridge span for 17 years.
A powerful bomb explodes in Tehran, killing 73 officials of the Islamic Republican Party.
US President Ronald Reagan nominates Sandra Day O'Connor to become the first female member of the Supreme Court of the United States.
As many as 50,000 demonstrators, mostly women and children, take to the streets in Łódź to protest food ration shortages in Communist Poland.
MTV begins broadcasting in the United States and airs its first video, "Video Killed the Radio Star" by The Buggles.
Senegalese opposition parties, under the leadership of Mamadou Dia, launch the Antiimperialist Action Front – Suxxali Reew Mi.
President Ronald Reagan fires 11,359 striking air-traffic controllers who ignored his order for them to return to work.
Gulf of Sidra Incident: United States F-14A Tomcat fighters intercept and shoot down two Libyan Sukhoi Su-22 fighter jets over the Gulf of Sidra.
Silvio Santos launches a new Brazilian television channel in São Paulo, Sistema Brasileiro de Televisão.
Central African President David Dacko is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General André Kolingba.
Belize joins the United Nations.
An Iranian Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules military transport aircraft crashes into a firing range near Kahrizak, Iran, killing 80 people.
The hunger strike at the Maze Prison in Northern Ireland ends after seven months and ten deaths.
Vice President Hosni Mubarak is elected as the President of Egypt, one week after the assassination of Anwar Sadat.
Cold War: The Soviet submarine S-363 runs aground on the east coast of Sweden.
Space Shuttle program: Mission STS-2, utilizing the Space Shuttle Columbia, marks the first time a crewed spacecraft is launched into space twice.
Inex-Adria Aviopromet Flight 1308, a McDonnell Douglas MD-80, crashes in Corsica, killing all 180 people on board.
El Mozote massacre: Armed forces in El Salvador kill an estimated 900 civilians in an anti-guerrilla campaign during the Salvadoran Civil War.
American Brigadier General James L. Dozier is abducted by the Red Brigades in Verona, Italy.
Peruvian Javier Pérez de Cuéllar becomes the first Latin American to hold the title of Secretary-General of the United Nations.
US Army General James L. Dozier is rescued by Italian anti-terrorism forces from captivity by the Red Brigades.
Richard Skrenta writes the first PC virus code, which is 400 lines long and disguised as an Apple boot program called "Elk Cloner".
The Intel 80286 is released, which introduced protected mode memory. The IBM PC/AT and its clones used this CPU.
Hama massacre: The government of Syria attacks the town of Hama.
Japan Air Lines Flight 350 crashes near Haneda Airport in an attempted pilot mass murder-suicide, killing 24 of the 174 people on board.
Syzygy: All nine planets recognized at this time — Mercury to Pluto — align on the same side of the Sun.
Fifteen people are killed when Widerøe Flight 933 crashes into the Barents Sea near Gamvik, Norway.
Guatemala's government, headed by Fernando Romeo Lucas García, is overthrown in a military coup by right-wing General Efraín Ríos Montt.
Space Shuttle program: STS-3 mission is completed with the landing of Columbia at White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico.
Baseball: Rollie Fingers of the Milwaukee Brewers becomes the first pitcher to record 300 saves.
The Bijon Setu massacre occurs in Calcutta, India.
Operation Black Buck: The Royal Air Force attacks the Argentine Air Force during the Falklands War.
Falklands War: The British nuclear submarine HMS Conqueror sinks the Argentine cruiser ARA General Belgrano.
Liberation of Khorramshahr: Iranians recapture the port city of Khorramshahr from the Iraqis during the Iran–Iraq War.
Falklands War: HMS Coventry is sunk by Argentine Air Force A-4 Skyhawks.
Cold War: Spain joins NATO.
Priscilla Presley opens Graceland to the public; the bathroom where Elvis Presley died five years earlier is kept off-limits.
Fahd becomes King of Saudi Arabia upon the death of his brother, Khalid.
Battles of Tumbledown and Wireless Ridge, during the Falklands War.
Falklands War: Argentine forces in the capital Stanley conditionally surrender to British forces ending the war.
Space Shuttle Columbia launched from the Kennedy Space Center on the final research and development flight mission, STS-4.
A failed assassination attempt against Iraqi president Saddam Hussein results in the Dujail Massacre over the next several months.
In one of the first militant attacks by Hezbollah, David S. Dodge, president of the American University of Beirut, is kidnapped.
Spantax Flight 995 crashes at Málaga Airport during a rejected takeoff, killing 50 of the 394 people on board.
Scott Fahlman posts the first documented emoticons :-) and :-( on the Carnegie Mellon University bulletin board system.
Poland bans Solidarity and all other trade unions.
The hull of the Mary Rose is recovered, over four hundred years after her sinking during the battle of the Solent.
During the UEFA Cup match between FC Spartak Moscow and HFC Haarlem, 66 people are crushed to death in the Luzhniki disaster.
The Spanish general election begins fourteen years of rule by the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party.
Channel 4, the British free-to-air public broadcast television channel funded by its commercial activities, starts broadcasting.
Colonel Saye Zerbo, president of the military government of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Colonel Gabriel Yoryan Somé.
Space Shuttle Columbia launches from the Kennedy Space Center on STS-5, the first operational mission of the Space Shuttle program.
USSR: Yuri Andropov becomes the General Secretary of the Communist Party's Central Committee, succeeding Leonid I. Brezhnev.
At the University of Utah, Barney Clark becomes the first person to receive a permanent artificial heart.
In Texas, Charles Brooks Jr., becomes the first person to be executed by lethal injection in the United States.
Turkish Airlines Flight 158 crashes at Ankara Esenboğa Airport in Ankara, Turkey, killing 47 and injuring 20.
The Ash Wednesday bushfires in Victoria and South Australia kill 75.
Bob Hawke is appointed Prime Minister of Australia.
Space Shuttle program: Space Shuttle Challenger makes its maiden voyage into space on STS-6.
During STS-6, astronauts Story Musgrave and Don Peterson perform the first Space Shuttle spacewalk.
Harold Washington is elected as the first black mayor of Chicago.
The West German news magazine Stern begins publishing excerpts from the purported diaries of Adolf Hitler, later revealed to be forgeries.
Pioneer 10 becomes the first man-made object to leave the central Solar System when it passes beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Space Shuttle program: STS-7, astronaut Sally Ride becomes the first American woman in space.
Mona Mahmudnizhad, together with nine other women of the Baháʼí Faith, is sentenced to death and hanged in Shiraz, Iran, over her religious beliefs.
India win the Cricket World Cup at Lord's (25 June)
Cold War: Samantha Smith, a United States schoolgirl, flies to the Soviet Union at the invitation of Secretary General Yuri Andropov.
An attack at Orly Airport in Paris is launched by Armenian militant organisation ASALA, leaving eight people dead and 55 injured.
Nintendo and Sega enter the console market with the respective releases of the Famicom and SG-1000 in Japan.
Gimli Glider: Air Canada Flight 143 runs out of fuel and makes a deadstick landing at Gimli, Manitoba.
Thirteen Sri Lanka Army soldiers are killed after a deadly ambush by the militant Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.
George Brett, playing for the Kansas City Royals against the New York Yankees, has a game-winning home run nullified in the "Pine Tar Incident".
Black July: Thirty-seven Tamil political prisoners at the Welikada high security prison in Colombo are massacred by the fellow Sinhalese prisoners.
Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo, president of the military government of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Captain Thomas Sankara.
Hurricane Alicia hits the Texas coast, killing 21 people and causing over US$1 billion in damage (1983 dollars).
Thirty-eight IRA prisoners, armed with six handguns, hijack a prison meals lorry and smash their way out of the Maze Prison.
Ameritech Mobile Communications launches the first US cellular network in Chicago.
U.S. President Ronald Reagan signs a bill creating Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
Avianca Flight 011: A Boeing 747 crashes near Madrid's Barajas Airport, killing 181.
Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on STS-9, the first mission to carry the European Space Agency's Spacelab module.
Provisional IRA members detonate a car bomb at Harrods Department Store in London. Three police officers and three civilians are killed.
Pope John Paul II visits Mehmet Ali Ağca in Rebibbia's prison and personally forgives him for the 1981 attack on him in St. Peter's Square.
Benjamin Ward is appointed New York City Police Department's first ever African American police commissioner.
In Nigeria, a coup d'état led by Major General Muhammadu Buhari ends the Second Nigerian Republic.
The AT&T Bell System is broken up by the United States Government.
Space Shuttle program: STS-41-B is launched using Space Shuttle Challenger.
Rakesh Sharma becomes the first Indian in space (3 April)
Members of Cameroon's Republican Guard unsuccessfully attempt to overthrow the government headed by Paul Biya.
One hundred and three Korean Martyrs are canonized by Pope John Paul II in Seoul.
Homosexuality is decriminalized in the Australian state of New South Wales.
Virgin Atlantic launches with its first flight from London to Newark.
Salyut 7 cosmonaut Svetlana Savitskaya becomes the first woman to perform a space walk.
Olympic Games: Games of the XXIII Olympiad: The summer Olympics were opened in Los Angeles.
Commercial peat-cutters discover the preserved bog body of a man, called Lindow Man, at Lindow Moss, Cheshire, England.
The Ariane 3 rocket is launched for the first time, carrying the Eutelsat I F-2 and Télécom 1A satellites into geosynchronous transfer orbit.
The Republic of Upper Volta changes its name to Burkina Faso.
STS-41-D: The Space Shuttle Discovery takes off on its maiden voyage.
The popular children's television show Thomas The Tank Engine & Friends, based on The Railway Series by the Reverend Wilbert Awdry, premieres on ITV.
After the assassination of Indira Gandhi, Prime Minister of India on 31 October 1984, by two of her Sikh bodyguards, anti-Sikh riots erupt.
Capital punishment: Velma Barfield becomes the first woman executed in the United States since 1962.
Subway vigilante Bernhard Goetz shoots four would-be muggers on a 2 express train in Manhattan section of New York, United States.
Galaxy Airlines Flight 203 crashes near Reno–Tahoe International Airport in Reno, Nevada, killing 70 people.
A magnitude 8.3 earthquake strikes the Valparaíso Region of Chile, killing 177 and leaving nearly a million people homeless.
The Food and Drug Administration approves a blood test for HIV infection, used since then for screening all blood donations in the United States.
Sudanese President Gaafar Nimeiry is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Field Marshal Abdel Rahman Swar al-Dahab.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-51D to deploy two communications satellites.
Space Shuttle Challenger is launched on STS-51-B.
Ronald Reagan visits the military cemetery at Bitburg and the site of the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, where he makes a speech.
Fifty-six spectators die and more than 200 are injured in the Bradford City stadium fire.
Radio Martí, part of the Voice of America service, begins broadcasting to Cuba.
Bangladesh is hit by a tropical cyclone and storm surge, which kills approximately 10,000 people.
United States–Canada tornado outbreak: Forty-one tornadoes hit Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, and Ontario, leaving 76 dead.
Five member nations of the European Economic Community sign the Schengen Agreement establishing a free travel zone with no border controls.
Members of the Revolutionary Party of Central American Workers, dressed as Salvadoran soldiers, attack the Zona Rosa area of San Salvador.
The Live Aid benefit concert takes place in London and Philadelphia, as well as other venues such as Moscow and Sydney.
Delta Air Lines Flight 191, a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar, crashes at Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport killing 137.
Takao Doi, Mamoru Mohri and Chiaki Mukai are chosen to be Japan's first astronauts.
Hans Tiedge, top counter-spy of West Germany, defects to East Germany.
The wreck of the Titanic is discovered by an American-French expedition led by Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel.
Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Tamil politicians and former MPs M. Alalasundaram and V. Dharmalingam are shot dead.
Super Mario Bros. is released in Japan for the NES, which starts the Super Mario series of platforming games.
Three civilians killed by alleged supporters of the Palestine Liberation Organization in Larnaca yacht killings.
The Space Shuttle Atlantis makes its maiden flight, carrying two DSCS-III Satellites on STS-51-J.
Four men from the Palestine Liberation Front hijack the MS Achille Lauro off the coast of Egypt.
Colombian conflict: leftist guerrillas of the 19th of April Movement seize control of the Palace of Justice in Bogotá.
Space Shuttle program: Atlantis launches on STS-61-B, with Rodolfo Neri Vela becoming the first Mexican astronaut.
Pope John Paul II announces the creation of World Youth Day.
Palestinian guerrillas kill eighteen people inside the airports of Rome, Italy, and Vienna, Austria.
Leabua Jonathan, Prime Minister of Lesotho, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by General Justin Lekhanya.
Conservative protestors attack a mock shanty town that had been erected on the Green at Dartmouth College as part of anti-apartheid protests.
The Voyager 2 space probe makes its closest approach to Uranus.
The National Resistance Movement topples the government of Tito Okello in Uganda.
The Ugandan government of Tito Okello is overthrown by the National Resistance Army, led by Yoweri Museveni.
Space Shuttle program: STS-51-L mission: Space Shuttle Challenger disintegrates after liftoff, killing all seven astronauts on board.
Twenty-eight years of one-family rule end in Haiti, when President Jean-Claude Duvalier flees the Caribbean nation.
The Soviet liner MS Mikhail Lermontov runs aground in the Marlborough Sounds, New Zealand.
China Airlines Flight 2265 crashes into the Pacific Ocean near Penghu Airport in Taiwan, killing all 13 aboard.
The Australia Act 1986 commences, causing Australia to become fully independent from the United Kingdom.
The Soviet Vega 1 begins returning images of Halley's Comet and the first images of its nucleus.
The Loscoe gas explosion leads to new UK laws on landfill gas migration and gas protection on landfill sites.
Mexicana de Aviación Flight 940 crashes into the Sierra Madre Oriental mountain range near the Mexican town of Maravatío, killing 167.
An assembly of Sikhs, known as a Sarbat Khalsa, officially declare independence for a state of Khalistan.
Chernobyl disaster: The City of Chernobyl is evacuated six days after the disaster.
The European Community adopts the European flag.
The Ariane 2 rocket is launched on its maiden flight, carrying Intelsat VA F-14, but the mission ends in failure.
The New Zealand Parliament passes the Homosexual Law Reform Act legalising homosexuality in New Zealand.
Nicholas Daniloff, a correspondent for U.S. News & World Report, is indicted on charges of espionage by the Soviet Union.
Aeroflot Flight 36075 is hijacked at Ufa International Airport.
TASCC, a superconducting cyclotron at the Chalk River Laboratories in Canada, is officially opened.
An explosion occurs at the Cipel-Marco fur factory in Kwai Chung, Hong Kong, killing 14 and injuring 10.
The Phantom of the Opera, eventually the second longest running musical in London, opens at Her Majesty's Theatre.
Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev meet in Iceland to continue discussions about scaling back IRBM arsenals in Europe.
The president of Mozambique and a prominent leader of FRELIMO, along with 33 others, die when their aircraft crashes into the Lebombo Mountains.
USS Rentz, USS Reeves and USS Oldendorf visit Qingdao, China; the first US naval visit to China since 1949.
The flight crew of Japan Airlines Flight 1628 are involved in a UFO sighting incident while flying over Alaska.
Varig Flight 797 crashes near Akouré in the Ivory Coast, resulting in 50 deaths.
Philippine security forces open fire on a crowd of 10,000–15,000 demonstrators at Malacañang Palace, Manila, killing 13.
Mohammed Said Hersi Morgan sends a "letter of death" to Somali President Siad Barre, proposing the genocide of the Isaaq people.
About 20,000 protestors march in a civil rights demonstration in Forsyth County, Georgia, United States.
After the 1986 People Power Revolution, the Philippines enacts a new constitution.
Iran–Contra affair: The Tower Commission rebukes President Ronald Reagan for not controlling his national security staff.
The London Agreement is secretly signed between Israeli Foreign Affairs Minister Shimon Peres and King Hussein of Jordan.
The Tamil Tigers are blamed for a car bomb that detonates in the Sri Lankan capital city of Colombo, killing 106 people.
Iran–Contra affair: Start of Congressional televised hearings in the United States.
LOT Flight 5055 Tadeusz Kościuszko crashes after takeoff in Warsaw, Poland, killing all 183 people on board.
Klaus Barbie goes on trial in Lyon for war crimes committed during World War II.
Fijian Prime Minister Timoci Bavadra is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Lieutenant colonel Sitiveni Rabuka.
An 18-year-old West German pilot, Mathias Rust, evades Soviet Union air defences and lands a private plane in Red Square in Moscow, Russia.
Diane Abbott, Paul Boateng and Bernie Grant are elected as the first black MPs in Great Britain.
Cold War: At the Brandenburg Gate, U.S. President Ronald Reagan publicly challenges Mikhail Gorbachev to tear down the Berlin Wall.
Aeroflot Flight N-528 crashes at Berdiansk Airport in present-day Ukraine, killing eight people.
For the first time in military history, a civilian population is targeted for chemical attack when Iraqi warplanes bomb the Iranian town of Sardasht.
US supertanker SS Bridgeton collides with mines laid by IRGC, causing a 43-square-meter dent in the body of the oil tanker.
Prime Minister of India Rajiv Gandhi and President of Sri Lanka J. R. Jayewardene sign the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord on ethnic issues.
A tornado occurs in Edmonton, Alberta, killing 27 people.
In Moscow, the trial begins for 19-year-old pilot Mathias Rust, who flew his Cessna airplane into Red Square in May.
In a coup d'état in Burundi, President Jean-Baptiste Bagaza is deposed by Major Pierre Buyoya.
Fijian Governor-General Penaia Ganilau is overthrown in a coup d'état led by Lieutenant colonel Sitiveni Rabuka.
Aero Trasporti Italiani Flight 460 crashes near Conca di Crezzo, Italy, killing all 37 people on board.
A coup d'état in Burkina Faso overthrows and kills then President Thomas Sankara.
The United States Navy conducts Operation Nimble Archer, an attack on two Iranian oil platforms in the Persian Gulf.
Black Monday: The Dow Jones Industrial Average falls by 22%, 508 points.
In Tunisia, president Habib Bourguiba is overthrown and replaced by Prime Minister Zine El Abidine Ben Ali.
King's Cross fire: In London, 31 people die in a fire at the city's busiest underground station, King's Cross St Pancras.
The Max Headroom signal hijacking incident takes place, in which a pirate broadcast interrupts television broadcasts in Chicago.
In Zimbabwe, the political parties ZANU and ZAPU reach an agreement that ends the violence in the Matabeleland region known as the Gukurahundi.
Condor Flugdienst Flight 3782 crashes near Seferihisar, Turkey, killing 16 people.
Lee Teng-hui becomes the first native Taiwanese President of the Republic of China.
An Aeroflot Yakovlev Yak-40 crashes at Nizhnevartovsk Airport, killing 27 people.
Doug Williams becomes the first African American quarterback to play in a Super Bowl and leads the Washington Redskins to victory in Super Bowl XXII.
Manuel Noriega is indicted on drug smuggling and money laundering charges.
Sumgait pogrom: The Armenian community in Sumgait, Azerbaijan is targeted in a violent pogrom.
A Colombian Boeing 727 jetliner, Avianca Flight 410, crashes into a mountainside near the Venezuelan border killing 143.
Governor Evan Mecham of Arizona is convicted in his impeachment trial and removed from office.
The Ojhri Camp explosion kills or injures more than 1,000 people in Rawalpindi and Islamabad, Pakistan.
In a United Nations ceremony in Geneva, Switzerland, the Soviet Union signs an agreement pledging to withdraw its troops from Afghanistan.
The USS Samuel B. Roberts strikes a mine in the Persian Gulf during Operation Earnest Will.
The United States launches Operation Praying Mantis against Iranian naval forces in the largest naval battle since World War II.
In Israel John Demjanjuk is sentenced to death for war crimes committed in World War II, although the verdict is later overturned.
All thirty-six passengers and crew are killed when Widerøe Flight 710 crashes into Mt. Torghatten in Brønnøy.
Soviet–Afghan War: After more than eight years of fighting, the Soviet Army begins to withdraw 115,000 troops from Afghanistan.
Margaret Thatcher holds her controversial Sermon on the Mound before the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland.
Pope John Paul II canonizes 117 Vietnamese Martyrs.
Villa Tunari massacre: Bolivian anti-narcotics police kill nine to 12 and injure over a hundred protesting coca-growing peasants.
United States Navy warship USS Vincennes shoots down Iran Air Flight 655 over the Persian Gulf, killing all 290 people aboard.
General Ne Win, effective ruler of Burma since 1962, resigns after pro-democracy protests.
Vietnam Airlines Flight 831 crashes in Khu Khot, Thailand, while on approach to Don Muang International Airport, killing 76.
General Henri Namphy, president of Haiti, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by General Prosper Avril.
Margaret Thatcher delivers the Bruges speech, in which she articulates her opposition to further European integration.
NASA launches STS-26, the first Space Shuttle mission since the Challenger disaster.
A hunter discovers three gray whales trapped under the ice near Alaska; the situation becomes a multinational effort to free the whales.
The Morris worm, the first Internet-distributed computer worm to gain significant mainstream media attention, is launched from MIT.
LOT Polish Airlines Flight 703 crashes in Białobrzegi, Podkarpackie Voivodeship, Poland, killing one person and injuring several more.
Lancang–Gengma earthquakes: At least 730 are killed after two powerful earthquakes rock the China–Myanmar border in Yunnan Province.
The Supreme Soviet of the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic declares that Estonia is "sovereign" but stops short of declaring independence.
In the first open election in more than a decade, voters in Pakistan elect populist candidate Benazir Bhutto to be Prime Minister of Pakistan.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on STS-27, a classified mission for the United States Department of Defense.
A Soviet Air Force Il-76 aircraft crashes while participating in the Armenian earthquake relief, killing 78 people.
Second Gulf of Sidra incident: A pair of Libyan MiG-23 "Floggers" are shot down by a pair of US Navy F-14 Tomcats during an air-to-air confrontation.
Sutton United, a team in the fifth tier of English league football, defeated top-tier Coventry City in one of the biggest upsets in FA Cup history.
Kegworth air disaster: British Midland Flight 92, a Boeing 737-400, crashes into the M1 motorway, killing 47 of the 126 people on board.
