Cold War: Hungary establishes diplomatic relations with South Korea, making it the first Eastern Bloc nation to do so.
The American embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan is closed.
Soviet–Afghan War: The last Soviet armoured column leaves Kabul.
A military coup overthrows Alfredo Stroessner, dictator of Paraguay since 1954.
Independent Air Flight 1851 strikes Pico Alto mountain while on approach to Santa Maria Airport in the Azores, killing all 144 passengers on board.
Air Ontario Flight 1363, a Fokker F-28 Fellowship, crashes at Dryden Regional Airport in Dryden, Ontario, Canada, killing 24.
In Prince William Sound in Alaska, the Exxon Valdez spills 240,000 barrels (38,000 m3) of crude oil after running aground.
A gun turret explodes on the USS Iowa, killing 47 sailors.
Tiananmen Square protests of 1989: In Beijing, around 100,000 students gather in Tiananmen Square to commemorate Chinese reform leader Hu Yaobang.
People's Daily publishes the April 26 Editorial which inflames the nascent Tiananmen Square protests.
The April 27 demonstrations, student-led protests responding to the April 26 Editorial, during the Tiananmen Square protests of 1989.
The Monkseaton shootings occur in Tyne and Wear, England. One is killed and 16 are injured.
Cold War: Hungary begins dismantling its border fence with Austria, which allows a number of East Germans to defect.
Tiananmen Square protests of 1989: The 10-metre high "Goddess of Democracy" statue is unveiled in Tiananmen Square by student demonstrators.
Jiang Zemin succeeds Zhao Ziyang to become the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party after the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre.
On the 600th anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo, Slobodan Milošević delivers the Gazimestan speech at the site of the historic battle.
United Airlines Flight 232 crashes in Sioux City, Iowa, killing 111.
A massacre is carried out by an Indian Peace Keeping Force in Sri Lanka killing 64 ethnic Tamil civilians.
Pakistan is re-admitted to the Commonwealth of Nations after having restored democracy for the first time since 1972.
U.S. Congressman Mickey Leland (D-TX) and 15 others die in a plane crash in Ethiopia.
Leading presidential hopeful Luis Carlos Galán is assassinated near Bogotá in Colombia.
Polish president Wojciech Jaruzelski nominates Solidarity activist Tadeusz Mazowiecki to be the first non-communist prime minister in 42 years.
Singing Revolution: Two million people from Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania stand on the Vilnius–Tallinn road, holding hands.
Colombian drug barons declare "total war" on the Colombian government.
Cubana de Aviación Flight 9046 crashes into a residential area of Havana shortly after takeoff from José Martí International Airport, killing 150.
Varig Flight 254 crashes in the Amazon rainforest near São José do Xingu in Brazil, killing 12.
In Leipzig, East Germany, the first of weekly demonstration for the legalisation of opposition groups and democratic reforms takes place.
Largest anti-Apartheid march in South Africa, led by Desmond Tutu.
An attempted coup d'état against Burkina Faso president Blaise Compaoré is uncovered and foiled.
USAir Flight 5050 crashes into Bowery Bay during a rejected takeoff from LaGuardia Airport, killing two people.
Wayne Gretzky becomes the all-time leading points scorer in the NHL.
The convictions of the Guildford Four are quashed by the Court of Appeal of England and Wales, after they had spent 15 years in prison.
In Honduras, 131 people are killed when a Boeing 727 crashes on approach to Toncontín International Airport near the nation's capital Tegucigalpa.
The first leg of the 1989 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira is held at the Estádio da Luz in Lisbon, Portugal.
China Airlines Flight 204 crashes after takeoff from Hualien Airport in Taiwan, killing all 54 people on board.
Aloha Island Air Flight 1712, a Twin Otter 300, crashed into terrain at night in Hawaii killing all 20 occupants onboard.
Douglas Wilder wins the governor's seat in Virginia, becoming the first elected African American governor in the United States.
David Dinkins becomes the first African American to be elected Mayor of New York City.
Fall of the Berlin Wall (9 November)
NASA launches Space Shuttle Discovery on STS-33, a classified mission for the United States Department of Defense.
Cold War: Velvet Revolution: In the face of protests, the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia announces it will give up its monopoly on political power.
The United States invasion of Panama deposes Manuel Noriega.
German reunification: Berlin's Brandenburg Gate re-opens after nearly 30 years, effectively ending the division of East and West Germany.
United Express Flight 2415 crashes on approach to the Tri-Cities Airport in Pasco, Washington, killing all six people on board.
A magnitude 5.6 earthquake hits Newcastle, New South Wales, Australia, killing 13 people.
United States invasion of Panama: Manuel Noriega, former leader of Panama, surrenders to American forces.
Time Warner is formed by the merger of Time Inc. and Warner Communications.
Douglas Wilder becomes the first elected African American governor as he takes office as Governor of Virginia in Richmond, Virginia.
Exodus of Kashmiri Pandits from the Kashmir Valley in Indian-administered Kashmir due to an insurgency.
Protests in Azerbaijan, part of the Dissolution of the Soviet Union.
Apartheid: F. W. de Klerk announces the unbanning of the African National Congress and promises to release Nelson Mandela.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union: The Central Committee of the Soviet Communist Party agrees to give up its monopoly on power.
American basketball player Hank Gathers dies after collapsing during the semifinals of a West Coast Conference tournament game.
In Haiti, Prosper Avril is ousted eighteen months after seizing power in a coup d'état in September 1988.
Patricio Aylwin is sworn in as the first democratically elected President of Chile since 1970.
Indian intervention in the Sri Lankan Civil War ends with the last ship of Indian Peace Keeping Force leaving Sri Lanka.
The current flag of Hong Kong is adopted for post-colonial Hong Kong during the Third Session of the Seventh National People's Congress.
Customs officers in Middlesbrough, England, seize what they believe to be the barrel of a massive gun on a ship bound for Iraq.
Widerøe Flight 839 crashes after takeoff from Værøy Airport in Norway, killing five people.
Hubble Space Telescope launched (24 April)
The first post-Communist presidential and parliamentary elections are held in Romania.
Croatian Parliament is constituted after the first free, multi-party elections, today celebrated as the National Day of Croatia.
Cold War: George H. W. Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev sign a treaty to end chemical weapon production.
The Lower Ohio Valley tornado outbreak spawns 66 confirmed tornadoes in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, and Ohio, killing 12.
Cold War: Checkpoint Charlie is dismantled in Berlin.
West Germany win the FIFA World Cup final against defending champions Argentina, with Andreas Brehme scoring the game's only goal.
The Jamaat al Muslimeen attempt a coup d'état in Trinidad and Tobago.
Gulf War: The United Nations Security Council orders a global trade embargo against Iraq in response to Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
Saddam Hussein appears on Iraqi state television with a number of Western "guests" (actually hostages) to try to prevent the Gulf War.
Armenia declares its independence from the Soviet Union.
Gulf War: Iraq declares Kuwait to be its newest province.
An F5 tornado strikes the Illinois cities of Plainfield and Joliet, killing 29 people.
Transnistria is unilaterally proclaimed a Soviet republic; the Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev declares the decision null and void.
Batticaloa massacre: Massacre of 184 Tamil civilians by the Sri Lankan Army in Batticaloa District.
The Tampere Hall, the largest concert and congress center in the Nordic countries, is inaugurated in Tampere, Finland.
First Intifada: Israeli police kill 17 Palestinians and wound over 100 near the Dome of the Rock.
Syrian forces attack free areas of Lebanon, removing General Michel Aoun from the presidential palace.
Soviet Union leader Mikhail Gorbachev is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to lessen Cold War tensions and open up his nation.
The Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic declares its sovereignty from the Soviet Union.
British Satellite Broadcasting and Sky Television plc merge to form BSkyB as a result of massive losses.
Rabbi Meir Kahane, founder of the far-right Kach movement, is shot dead after a speech at a New York City hotel.
Fugendake, part of the Mount Unzen volcanic complex, Nagasaki Prefecture, Japan, becomes active again and erupts.
British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher withdraws from the Conservative Party leadership election, confirming the end of her Premiership.
Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on STS-35, carrying the ASTRO-1 spacelab observatory.
Lech Wałęsa is elected President of Poland.
Final independence of Marshall Islands and Federated States of Micronesia after termination of trusteeship.
Economic liberalisation begins under P. V. Narasimha Rao
Sharon Pratt Dixon becomes the first African American woman mayor of a major city and first woman Mayor of the District of Columbia.
Georgian forces enter Tskhinvali, the capital of South Ossetia, Georgia, opening the 1991–92 South Ossetia War.
Roger Lafontant, former leader of the Tonton Macoute in Haiti under François Duvalier, attempts a coup d'état, which ends in his arrest.
Persian Gulf War: An act of the U.S. Congress authorizes the use of American military force to drive Iraq out of Kuwait.
Soviet Union troops attack Lithuanian independence supporters in Vilnius, killing 14 people and wounding around 1,000 others.
Gulf War: Iraq fires a second Scud missile into Israel, causing 15 injuries.
Sudan's government imposes Islamic law nationwide, worsening the civil war between the country's Muslim north and Christian south.
Mohamed Siad Barre is removed from power in Somalia, ending centralized government, and is succeeded by Ali Mahdi.
Gulf War: The Battle of Khafji, the first major ground engagement of the war, as well as its deadliest, begins between Iraq and Saudi Arabia.
The Troubles: The Provisional IRA launches a mortar attack on 10 Downing Street in London, the headquarters of the British government.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Voters in Lithuania vote for independence from the Soviet Union.
Nicaraguan Contras leader Enrique Bermúdez is assassinated in Managua.
The IRA explodes bombs in the early morning at Paddington station and Victoria station in London.
Disbandment of the Warsaw Pact at a meeting of its members in Budapest.
Gulf War: U.S. President George H. W. Bush announces that "Kuwait is liberated".
An amateur video captures the beating of Rodney King by Los Angeles police officers.
1991 Salvadoran legislative election: The Nationalist Republican Alliance wins 39 of the 84 seats in the Legislative Assembly of El Salvador.
An ASA EMB 120 crashes in Brunswick, Georgia, killing all 23 aboard, including Sen. John Tower and astronaut Sonny Carter.
The Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-37 to deploy the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory.
A rare tropical storm develops in the South Atlantic Ocean near Angola, the first to be documented by satellites.
Italian ferry MS Moby Prince collides with an oil tanker in dense fog off Livorno, Italy, killing 140.
Fifty-five tornadoes break out in the central United States. Before the outbreak's end, Andover, Kansas, would record the year's only F5 tornado.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-39, the first unclassified shuttle mission for the United States Department of Defense.
The 7.0 Mw Racha earthquake affects Georgia with a maximum MSK intensity of IX (Destructive), killing 270 people.
Angolan Civil War: The MPLA and UNITA agree to the Bicesse Accords, which are formally signed on May 31 in Lisbon.
A riot breaks out in the Mt. Pleasant section of Washington, D.C. after police shoot a Salvadoran man.
Édith Cresson becomes France's first female Prime Minister.
Former Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi is assassinated by a female suicide bomber near Madras.
Israel conducts Operation Solomon, evacuating Ethiopian Jews to Israel.
Zviad Gamsakhurdia becomes the first elected President of the Republic of Georgia in the post-Soviet era.
Bicesse Accords in Angola lay out a transition to multi-party democracy under the supervision of the United Nations' UNAVEM II peacekeeping mission.
In modern Russia's first democratic election, Boris Yeltsin is elected as the President of Russia.
Sonic the Hedgehog is released in North America on the Sega Genesis platform, beginning the popular video game franchise.
The breakup of Yugoslavia begins when Slovenia and Croatia declare their independence from Yugoslavia.
Two days after it had declared independence, Slovenia is invaded by Yugoslav troops, tanks, and aircraft, starting the Ten-Day War.
Yugoslav Wars: The Brioni Agreement ends the ten-day independence war in Slovenia against the rest of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on STS-43 to deploy the TDRS-5 satellite.
Tim Berners-Lee puts the first website online (6 August)
Takako Doi, chair of the Social Democratic Party, becomes Japan's first female speaker of the House of Representatives.
Ukraine declares itself independent from the Soviet Union.
Libero Grassi, an Italian businessman from Palermo, is killed by the Sicilian Mafia after taking a solitary stand against their extortion demands.
Estonia, North Korea, South Korea, Latvia, Lithuania, the Marshall Islands and Micronesia join the United Nations.
Nadine Gordimer is announced as the winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Croatian War of Independence: Bombing of the Banski Dvori in Zagreb, Croatia.
Upon the expiration of the Brioni Agreement, Croatia and Slovenia sever all official relations with Yugoslavia.
Prof. Anita Hill delivers her televised testimony concerning sexual harassment during the Clarence Thomas Supreme Court nomination.
A 6.8 Mw earthquake strikes the Uttarkashi region of India, killing more than 1,000 people.
Three months after the end of the Ten-Day War, the last soldier of the Yugoslav People's Army leaves the territory of the Republic of Slovenia.
President of the Chechen Republic Dzhokhar Dudayev declares sovereignty of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria from the Russian Federation.
Tropical Storm Thelma causes flash floods in the Philippine city of Ormoc, killing more than 4,900 people.
Magic Johnson announces that he is HIV-positive and retires from the NBA.
Santa Cruz massacre: The Indonesian Army open fire on a crowd of student protesters in Dili, East Timor.
The Republic of Karelia, an autonomous republic of Russia, is formed from the former Karelian ASSR.
Shiite Muslim kidnappers in Lebanon release Anglican Church envoys Terry Waite and Thomas Sutherland.
After an 87-day siege, the Croatian city of Vukovar capitulates to the besieging Yugoslav People's Army and allied Serb paramilitary forces.
Queen lead singer Freddie Mercury announces in a statement that he is HIV-positive. He dies the following day.
Space Shuttle program: Atlantis launches on STS-44.
Cold War: Ukrainian voters overwhelmingly approve a referendum for independence from the Soviet Union.
Yugoslav Wars: In Croatia, forces of the Serb-dominated Yugoslav People's Army (JNA) heaviest bombardment of Dubrovnik during a siege of seven months.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union (26 December)
The Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union meets and formally dissolves the Soviet Union, ending the Cold War.
Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 751 crashes in Gottröra in the Norrtälje Municipality in Sweden, injuring 92.
CommutAir Flight 4821 crashes on approach to Adirondack Regional Airport, in Saranac Lake, New York, killing two people.
President of Georgia Zviad Gamsakhurdia flees the country as a result of the military coup.
The Assembly of the Serb People in Bosnia and Herzegovina proclaims the creation of Republika Srpska, a new state within Yugoslavia.
During a visit to South Korea, Japanese Prime Minister Kiichi Miyazawa apologizes for forcing Korean women into sexual slavery during World War II.
Air Inter Flight 148, an Airbus A320-111, crashes into a mountain near Strasbourg, France, killing 87 of the 96 people on board.
A coup d'état is led by Hugo Chávez against Venezuelan President Carlos Andrés Pérez.
The Maastricht Treaty is signed, leading to the creation of the European Union.
First Nagorno-Karabakh War: Armenian troops massacre more than 20 Azerbaijani civilians during the Capture of Garadaghly.
Israeli Embassy attack in Buenos Aires: Car bomb attack kills 29 and injures 242.
A referendum to end apartheid in South Africa is passed 68.7% to 31.2%.
The USS Missouri, the last active United States Navy battleship, is decommissioned in Long Beach, California.
Peace protesters Suada Dilberovic and Olga Sučić are killed on the Vrbanja Bridge in Sarajevo, becoming the first casualties of the Bosnian War.
Alberto Fujimori, president of Peru, dissolves the Peruvian congress by military force.
A series of gas explosions rip through the streets in Guadalajara, Mexico, killing 206.
Betty Boothroyd becomes the first woman to be elected Speaker of the British House of Commons in its 700-year history.
The Russian Federation and 12 other former Soviet republics become members of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, is proclaimed.
Armenian forces capture Shusha, marking a major turning point in the First Nagorno-Karabakh War.
Westray Mine disaster kills 26 workers in Nova Scotia, Canada.
Li Hongzhi gives the first public lecture on Falun Gong in Changchun, People's Republic of China.
After 30 seasons Johnny Carson hosts his penultimate episode and last featuring guests (Robin Williams and Bette Midler) of The Tonight Show.
The last Thai dictator, General Suchinda Kraprayoon, resigns following pro-democracy protests.
Copa Airlines Flight 201 breaks apart in mid-air and crashes into the Darién Gap in Panama, killing all 47 aboard.
The first World Oceans Day is celebrated, coinciding with the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
GP Express Airlines Flight 861 crashes on approach to Anniston Regional Airport in Anniston, Alabama, killing three.
Space Shuttle Columbia launches on STS-50, the first shuttle mission to carry Extended Duration Orbiter hardware.
A Tupolev Tu-154 crashes during takeoff from Tbilisi International Airport, killing all 24 aboard and four more people on the ground.
Near Medellín, Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar escapes from his luxury prison fearing extradition to the United States.
Abkhazia declares independence from Georgia.
Space Shuttle program: Atlantis is launched on STS-46 to deploy the European Retrievable Carrier and the Tethered Satellite System.
Hurricane Andrew makes landfall in Homestead, Florida as a Category 5 hurricane, causing up to $25 billion (1992 USD) in damages.
NASA launches the Mars Observer. Eleven months later, the probe would fail while preparing for orbital insertion.
The Peekskill meteorite, a 27.7 pounds (12.6 kg) meteorite crashed into a parked car in Peekskill, New York.
The Hoxne Hoard is discovered by metal detectorist Eric Lawes in Hoxne, Suffolk.
The first smartphone, the IBM Simon, is introduced at COMDEX in Las Vegas, Nevada.
China Southern Airlines Flight 3943 crashes on approach to Guilin Qifengling Airport in Guilin, China, killing all 141 people on board.
For the second time in a year, military forces try to overthrow president Carlos Andrés Pérez in Venezuela.
The Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, India, is demolished, leading to widespread riots causing the death of over 1,500 people.
A Dutch DC-10, flight Martinair MP 495, crashes at Faro Airport, Portugal, killing 56.
Dissolution of Czechoslovakia: Czechoslovakia is divided into the Czech Republic and Slovak Republic.
Sri Lankan Civil War: The Sri Lanka Navy kill 35–100 civilians on the Jaffna Lagoon.
In Moscow, Russia, George H. W. Bush and Boris Yeltsin sign the second Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START).
The oil tanker MV Braer runs aground on the coast of the Shetland Islands, spilling 84,700 tons of crude oil.
Indian Border Security Force units kill 55 Kashmiri civilians in Sopore, Jammu and Kashmir, in revenge after militants ambushed a BSF patrol.
Four people are killed when Lufthansa CityLine Flight 5634 crashes on approach to Charles de Gaulle Airport in Roissy-en-France, France.
Bosnian War: The Bosnian Army executes a surprise attack at the village of Kravica in Srebrenica.
Space Shuttle program: Endeavour heads for space for the third time as STS-54 launches from the Kennedy Space Center.
Czech Republic and Slovakia join the United Nations.
Five people are shot outside the CIA Headquarters in Langley, Virginia. Two are killed and three wounded.
An Iran Air Tours Tupolev Tu-154 and an Iranian Air Force Sukhoi Su-24 collide mid-air near Qods, Iran, killing all 133 people on board both aircraft.
Eighteen-year-old Stephen Lawrence is murdered in a racially motivated attack while waiting for a bus in Well Hall, Eltham.
The Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on mission STS-55 to conduct experiments aboard the Spacelab module.
CERN announces World Wide Web protocols will be free.
Sri Lankan President Ranasinghe Premadasa is assassinated in Colombo in a suicide bombing carried out by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.
Eritrea gains its independence from Ethiopia.
Dobrinja mortar attack: Thirteen are killed and 133 wounded when Serb mortar shells are fired at a soccer game in Dobrinja, west of Sarajevo.
Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat wins the first presidential election in Mongolia.
A mob sets fire to the Hotel Madımak in Sivas, Turkey, where an Alevi cultural festival was taking place, killing 37 people.
Great Flood of 1993: Levees near Kaskaskia, Illinois rupture, forcing the entire town to evacuate by barges operated by the Army Corps of Engineers.
China Northwest Airlines Flight 2119 crashes during takeoff from Yinchuan Xihuayuan Airport in Yinchuan, Ningxia, China, killing 55 people.
The Supreme Court of Israel acquits alleged Nazi death camp guard John Demjanjuk of all charges and he is set free.
Ada Deer, a Menominee activist, is sworn in as the head of the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
A Tajikistan Airlines Yakovlev Yak-40 crashes during takeoff from Khorog Airport in Tajikistan, killing 82.
Israeli–Palestinian peace process: The Palestine Liberation Organization officially recognizes Israel as a legitimate state.
The Cambodian monarchy is restored, with Norodom Sihanouk as king.
The 6.2 Mw Latur earthquake shakes Maharashtra, India with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe) killing 9,748 and injuring 30,000.
The flood of '93 ends at St. Louis, Missouri, 103 days after it began, as the Mississippi River falls below flood stage.
At least 60 people die in eastern Papua New Guinea when a series of earthquakes rock the Finisterre Range, triggering massive landslides.
Widerøe Flight 744 crashes in Overhalla Municipality, Norway, killing six people.
China Northern Airlines Flight 6901 crashes on approach to Ürümqi Diwopu International Airport in Ürümqi, China, killing 12 people.
United States House of Representatives passes a resolution to establish the North American Free Trade Agreement.
In Nigeria, General Sani Abacha ousts the government of Ernest Shonekan in a military coup.
In the United States, the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is approved by the House of Representatives.
Space Shuttle program: STS-61: NASA launches the Space Shuttle Endeavour on a mission to repair the Hubble Space Telescope.
Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar is shot and killed by police in Medellín.
Long Island Rail Road shooting: Passenger Colin Ferguson murders six people and injures 19 others on the LIRR in Nassau County, New York.
Baikal Airlines Flight 130 crashes near Mamoney, Irkutsk, Russia, resulting in 125 deaths.
A British Aerospace Jetstream 41 operating as United Express Flight 6291 crashes in Gahanna, Ohio, killing five of the eight people on board.
The Irish Government announces the end of a 15-year broadcasting ban on the IRA and its political arm Sinn Féin.
The spacecraft Clementine by BMDO and NASA is launched.
Space Shuttle program: STS-60 is launched, carrying Sergei Krikalev, the first Russian cosmonaut to fly aboard the Shuttle.
Byron De La Beckwith is convicted of the 1963 murder of civil rights leader Medgar Evers.
Space Shuttle program: The Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on STS-62.
At an election rally in Tijuana, Mexican presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio is assassinated by Mario Aburto Martínez.
The Rwandan genocide begins when the aircraft carrying Rwandan president Juvénal Habyarimana and Burundian president Cyprien Ntaryamira is shot down.
Rwandan genocide: Massacres of Tutsis begin in Kigali, Rwanda, and soldiers kill the civilian Prime Minister Agathe Uwilingiyimana.
South Africa begins its first multiracial election, which is won by Nelson Mandela's African National Congress.
Three-time Formula One champion Ayrton Senna is killed in an accident during the San Marino Grand Prix.
The signing of the Bishkek Protocol between Armenia and Azerbaijan effectively freezes the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.
American teenager Michael P. Fay is caned in Singapore for theft and vandalism.
Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom and French President François Mitterrand officiate at the opening of the Channel Tunnel.
Nelson Mandela becomes President of South Africa (10 May)
The Democratic Republic of Yemen unsuccessfully attempts to secede from the Republic of Yemen; a war breaks out.
China Northwest Airlines Flight 2303 crashes near Xi'an Xianyang International Airport, killing all 160 people on board.
China conducts a nuclear test for DF-31 warhead at Area C (Beishan), Lop Nur, its prominence being due to the Cox Report.
A Boeing B-52 Stratofortress crashes at Fairchild Air Force Base near Spokane, Washington, killing four.
Members of the Aum Shinrikyo cult release sarin gas in Matsumoto, Japan. Seven people are killed, 660 injured.
USAir Flight 1016 crashes near Charlotte Douglas International Airport, killing 37 of the 57 people on board.
Rwandan genocide: Kigali, the Rwandan capital, is captured by the Rwandan Patriotic Front, ending the genocide in the city.
Kim Jong Il begins to assume supreme leadership of North Korea upon the death of his father, Kim Il Sung.
Space Shuttle Columbia is launched on an international science mission.
Alas Chiricanas Flight 00901 is destroyed by a bomb after takeoff from Enrique Adolfo Jiménez Airport in Colón, Panama, killing 21.
Eugene Bullard, the only African American pilot in World War I, is posthumously commissioned as Second Lieutenant in the United States Air Force.
Space Shuttle program: Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-64.
The rest of the Major League Baseball season is canceled because of a strike.
Space Shuttle Endeavour is launched on STS-68.
The United States, under the Clinton administration, returns Haiti's first democratically elected president, Jean-Bertrand Aristide, to the island.
Jordan and Israel sign a peace treaty.
WXYC, the student radio station of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, launches the world's first internet radio broadcast.
First Chechen War: Russian president Boris Yeltsin orders Russian troops into Chechnya.
The First Chechen War: The Russian Ground Forces begin a New Year's storming of Grozny.
The Draupner wave in the North Sea in Norway is detected, confirming the existence of freak waves.
Austria, Finland and Sweden join the EU.
51 people are killed in a plane crash in María La Baja, Colombia.
Astronaut Eileen Collins becomes the first woman to pilot the Space Shuttle as mission STS-63 gets underway from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Ramzi Yousef, the mastermind of the 1993 World Trade Center bombing, is arrested in Islamabad, Pakistan.
The Cenepa War between Peru and Ecuador ends on a ceasefire brokered by the UN.
Selena is murdered by her fan club president Yolanda Saldívar at a Days Inn in Corpus Christi, Texas.
TAROM Flight 371, an Airbus A310-300, crashes near Balotesti, Romania, killing all 60 people on board.
First Chechen War: Russian paramilitary troops begin a massacre of civilians in Samashki, Chechnya.
Alison Hargreaves, a 33-year-old British mother, becomes the first woman to ascend Everest without oxygen or the help of sherpas.
Downed U.S. Air Force pilot Captain Scott O'Grady is rescued by U.S. Marines in Bosnia.
Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-71, the first space shuttle mission to dock with the Russian space station Mir.
In the Bosnian War, under the command of General Ratko Mladić, Serbia begins its attack on the Bosnian town of Srebrenica.
The Navaly church bombing is carried out by the Sri Lanka Air Force killing 125 Tamil civilian refugees.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-70 to deploy the TDRS-7 satellite.
Third Taiwan Strait Crisis: The People's Liberation Army begins firing missiles into the waters north of Taiwan.
The Korean War Veterans Memorial is dedicated in Washington, D.C.
Operation Storm, the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence begins.
Aviateca Flight 901 crashes into the San Vicente volcano in El Salvador, killing all 65 people on board.
In South Carolina, Shannon Faulkner becomes the first female cadet matriculated at The Citadel (she drops out less than a week later).
Bosnian War: NATO launches Operation Deliberate Force against Bosnian Serb forces.
O. J. Simpson murder case: O. J. Simpson is acquitted of the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.
An Amtrak Sunset Limited train is derailed by saboteurs near Palo Verde, Arizona.
Space Shuttle Columbia launches on STS-73.
A commuter train slams into a school bus in Fox River Grove, Illinois, killing seven students.
Mossad agents assassinate Palestinian Islamic Jihad leader Fathi Shaqaqi in his hotel in Malta.
Cleveland Browns relocation controversy: Art Modell announces that he signed a deal that would relocate the Cleveland Browns to Baltimore.
Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-74 to deliver the Mir Docking Module to the Russian space station Mir.
Mozambique becomes the first state to join the Commonwealth of Nations without having been part of the former British Empire.
Nigeria Airways Flight 357 crashes at Kaduna International Airport in Kaduna, Nigeria, killing 11 people and injuring 66.
The Galileo spacecraft arrives at Jupiter, a little more than six years after it was launched by Space Shuttle Atlantis during Mission STS-34.
An Air Saint Martin (now Air Caraïbes) Beechcraft 1900 crashes near the Haitian commune of Belle Anse, killing 20.
American Airlines Flight 965, a Boeing 757, crashes into a mountain 50 km north of Cali, Colombia, killing 159 of the 163 people on board.
The city of Bethlehem passes from Israeli to Palestinian control.
In a military coup, Colonel Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara deposes the first democratically elected president of Niger, Mahamane Ousmane.
President Jacques Chirac announces a "definitive end" to French nuclear weapons testing.
An explosives-filled truck rams into the gates of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka in Colombo, killing at least 86 people and injuring 1,400.
Copernicium is discovered by Sigurd Hofmann, Victor Ninov et al.
A Chicago-bound Amtrak train, the Capitol Limited, collides with a MARC commuter train bound for Washington, D.C., killing 11 people.
In Philadelphia, world champion Garry Kasparov beats the Deep Blue supercomputer in a chess match.
NASA's Discovery Program begins as the NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft lifts off on the first mission ever to orbit and land on an asteroid, 433 Eros.
Taiwan holds its first direct elections and chooses Lee Teng-hui as President.
Two women and four children are killed after an Israeli helicopter fires rockets at an ambulance in Mansouri, Lebanon.
Four people are killed and 75 are injured in a train accident in Jokela, Finland.
Whitewater controversy: President Bill Clinton gives a 41⁄2 hour videotaped testimony for the defense.
The body of former CIA director William Colby is found washed up on a riverbank in southern Maryland, eight days after he disappeared.
Severe thunderstorms and a tornado in Bangladesh kill 600 people.
The ferry MV Bukoba sinks in Tanzanian waters on Lake Victoria, killing nearly 1,000.
The seven Trappist monks of Tibhirine who were abducted on March 27 are killed under uncertain circumstances.
First Chechen War: Russian president Boris Yeltsin meets with Chechen rebels for the first time and negotiates a cease-fire.
The Khobar Towers bombing in Saudi Arabia kills 19 U.S. servicemen.
British Prime Minister John Major announced the Stone of Scone would be returned to Scotland.
A Belgian Air Force C-130 Hercules carrying the Royal Netherlands Army marching band crashes on landing at Eindhoven Airport.
In a military coup in Burundi, Pierre Buyoya deposes Sylvestre Ntibantunganya.
In Atlanta, United States, a pipe bomb explodes at Centennial Olympic Park during the 1996 Summer Olympics.
The remains of a prehistoric man are discovered near Kennewick, Washington. Such remains will be known as the Kennewick Man.
NASA announces that the ALH 84001 meteorite, thought to originate from Mars, contains evidence of primitive life-forms.
Vnukovo Airlines Flight 2801, a Tupolev Tu-154, crashes into a mountain on the Arctic island of Spitsbergen, killing all 141 aboard.
Representatives of 71 nations sign the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty at the United Nations.
Pakistani President Farooq Leghari dismisses the government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and dissolves the National Assembly.
ADC Airlines Flight 086 crashes into the Lagos Lagoon in Epe, Lagos State, Nigeria, killing all 144 people on board.
Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961 is hijacked, then crashes into the Indian Ocean off the coast of Comoros after running out of fuel, killing 125.
Taliban forces retake the strategic Bagram Airfield which solidifies their buffer zone around Kabul, Afghanistan.
Comair Flight 3272 crashes in Raisinville Township in Monroe County, Michigan, killing 29 people.
Yasser Arafat returns to Hebron after more than 30 years and joins celebrations over the handover of the last Israeli-controlled West Bank city.
En route to Lebanon, two Israeli Sikorsky CH-53 troop-transport helicopters collide in mid-air over northern Galilee, Israel, killing 73.
Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, announced (22 February)
Tiger Woods becomes the youngest golfer to win the Masters Tournament.
The Chemical Weapons Convention of 1993 enters into force, outlawing the production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons by its signatories.
The Labour Party wins the 1997 General Election and Tony Blair is elected as Prime Minister.
The 7.3 Mw Qayen earthquake strikes Iran's Khorasan Province killing 1,567 people.
The Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-84 to dock with the Russian space station Mir.
A military coup in Sierra Leone replaces President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah with Major Johnny Paul Koroma.
The 1997 Central Texas tornado outbreak occurs, spawning multiple tornadoes in Central Texas, including the F5 that killed 27 in Jarrell.
The Confederation Bridge opens, linking Prince Edward Island with mainland New Brunswick.
Before fleeing his northern stronghold, Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot orders the killing of his defense chief Son Sen and 11 of Sen's family members.
A jury sentences Timothy McVeigh to death for his part in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.
The National Hockey League approved expansion franchises for Nashville (1998), Atlanta (1999), Columbus (2000), and Minneapolis-Saint Paul (2000).
An uncrewed Progress spacecraft collides with the Russian space station Mir.
Holyfield–Tyson II: Mike Tyson is disqualified in the third round for biting a piece off Evander Holyfield's ear.
The Bank of Thailand floats the baht, triggering the Asian financial crisis.
NASA's Pathfinder space probe lands on the surface of Mars.
The Turkish Armed Forces withdraw from northern Iraq after assisting the Kurdistan Democratic Party in the Iraqi Kurdish Civil War.
An explosion aboard a Brazilian airline TAM Fokker 100 launches engineer Fernando Caldeira de Moura Campos into a 2,400 meters free fall.
The second Blue Water Bridge opens between Port Huron, Michigan and Sarnia, Ontario.
Digital Equipment Corporation files antitrust charges against chipmaker Intel.
About 50 people are killed in the Si Zerrouk massacre in Algeria.
Korean Air Flight 801 crashed at Nimitz Hill, Guam, killing 229 of the 254 people on board.
Space Shuttle Program: The Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-85 from the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida.
Fine Air Flight 101 crashes after takeoff from Miami International Airport, killing five people.
Sixteen people are killed when Formosa Airlines Flight 7601 crashes near Beigan Airport in the Matsu Islands of Taiwan.
At least 98 villagers are killed by the Armed Islamic Group of Algeria GIA in the Rais massacre, Algeria.
Vietnam Airlines Flight 815 (Tupolev Tu-134) crashes on approach into Phnom Penh airport, killing 64.
A German Air Force Tupolev Tu-154 and a United States Air Force Lockheed C-141 Starlifter collide in mid-air near Namibia, killing 33.
NASA launches Space Shuttle Atlantis on STS-86 to the Mir space station.
After a civil war, Denis Sassou Nguesso proclaims himself President of the Republic of the Congo.
The 1997 Asian financial crisis causes a crash in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
Tropical Storm Linda makes landfall in the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, causing more than 3,000 deaths.
In Luxor, Egypt, 62 people are killed by six Islamic militants outside the Temple of Hatshepsut, known as Luxor massacre.
In the Indian state of Bihar, Ranvir Sena attacks the CPI (ML) Party Unity stronghold Lakshmanpur-Bathe, killing 63 lower caste people.
Fourteen-year-old Michael Carneal opens fire at a group of students in Heath High School in West Paducah, Kentucky, killing three and injuring five.
Dennō Senshi Porygon: Over 600 kids in Japan suffer photosensitive epileptic seizures after watching an episode of the Pokémon anime.
Over 100 people are killed in the Sidi-Hamed massacre in Algeria.
Alfredo Ormando sets himself on fire in St. Peter's Square, protesting against homophobia.
In Santa Lucía Cotzumalguapa, Guatemala, thirteen American students on a school trip are attacked and robbed at gunpoint; five were raped.
Clinton–Lewinsky scandal: Matt Drudge breaks the story of the Bill Clinton–Monica Lewinsky affair on his Drudge Report website.
Space Shuttle program: space shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-89 to dock with the Russian space station Mir.
Netscape announces Mozilla, with the intention to release Communicator code as open source.
A suicide attack by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam on Sri Lanka's Temple of the Tooth kills eight and injures 25 others.
Dr. Rüdiger Marmulla performs the first computer-assisted Bone Segment Navigation at the University of Regensburg, Germany.
Netscape releases Mozilla source code under an open source license.
In Japan, the Akashi Kaikyō Bridge opens to traffic, becoming the longest bridge span in the world.
Air France Flight 422 crashes after taking off from El Dorado International Airport in Bogotá, Colombia, killing all 53 people on board.
The European Central Bank is founded in Brussels in order to define and execute the European Union's monetary policy.
Steve Jobs of Apple Inc. unveils the first iMac.
Pokhran-II nuclear tests (11 May)
India conducts three underground atomic tests in Pokhran.
Race riots break out in Jakarta, Indonesia, where shops owned by Indonesians of Chinese descent are looted and women raped.
In Miami, five abortion clinics are attacked by a butyric acid attacker.
A MIAT Mongolian Airlines Harbin Y-12 crashes near Erdenet, Orkhon Province, Mongolia, resulting in 28 deaths.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-91, the final mission of the Shuttle-Mir program.
Propair Flight 420 crashes near Montréal–Mirabel International Airport in Quebec, Canada, killing 11.
In Clinton v. City of New York, the United States Supreme Court decides that the Line Item Veto Act of 1996 is unconstitutional.
Japan launches the Nozomi probe to Mars, joining the United States and Russia as a space exploring nation.
Hong Kong International Airport opens in Chek Lap Kok, Hong Kong, replacing Kai Tak Airport as the city's international airport.
Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Tamil MP S. Shanmuganathan is killed by a claymore mine.
Bombings at United States embassies in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania and Nairobi, Kenya kill approximately 212 people.
HRH Prince Al-Muhtadee Billah is proclaimed the crown prince of Brunei with a Royal Proclamation.
Second Congo War: Loyalist troops backed by Angolan and Zimbabwean forces repulse the RCD and Rwandan offensive on Kinshasa.
Google is founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin, two PhD students at Stanford University.
PauknAir Flight 4101, a British Aerospace 146, crashes near Melilla Airport in Melilla, Spain, killing 38 people.
in Venezuela, Hugo Chávez is victorious in presidential elections.
The European Exchange Rate Mechanism freezes the values of the legacy currencies in the Eurozone, and establishes the value of the euro currency.
Former professional wrestler Jesse Ventura is sworn in as governor of Minnesota, United States.
British Aerospace agrees to acquire the defence subsidiary of the General Electric Company, forming BAE Systems in November 1999.
A 6.0 magnitude earthquake hits western Colombia killing at least 1,000.
Crown Prince Abdullah becomes the King of Jordan on the death of his father, King Hussein.
Alitalia Flight 1553 crashes at Genoa Cristoforo Colombo Airport in Genoa, Italy, killing four.
Gunmen assassinate Paraguay's Vice President Luis María Argaña.
A magnitude 6.8 earthquake in India strikes the Chamoli district in Uttar Pradesh, killing 103.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closes above the 10,000 mark (10,006.78) for the first time, during the height of the dot-com bubble.
Two Libyans suspected of bringing down Pan Am Flight 103 in 1988 are handed over for eventual trial in the Netherlands.
During the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, an American McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle shoots a passenger train, killing between 20 and 60 people.
NATO mistakenly bombs a convoy of ethnic Albanian refugees. Yugoslav officials say 75 people were killed.
A severe hailstorm strikes Sydney, Australia causing A$2.3 billion in insured damages, the most costly natural disaster in Australian history.
Panamanian general election: Mireya Moscoso becomes the first woman to be elected President of Panama.
The first elections to the devolved Scottish Parliament and Welsh Assembly are held.
Mother's Day bus crash kills 22 passengers and injures another 22, including the driver in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States.
Kosovo War: NATO bombs the village of Koriša, killing at least 87 people.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-96, the first shuttle mission to dock with the International Space Station.
In Milan, Italy, after 22 years of restoration work, Leonardo da Vinci's masterpiece The Last Supper is put back on display.
53 people are killed in a stampede at the Nyamiha metro station in Minsk, Belarus.
Kosovo War: NATO suspends its airstrikes after Slobodan Milošević agrees to withdraw Serbian forces from Kosovo.
Days of student protests begin after Iranian police and hardliners attack a student dormitory at the University of Tehran.
ANA Flight 61 is hijacked in Tokyo, Japan by Yuji Nishizawa.
Air Fiji flight 121 crashes while en route to Nadi, Fiji, killing all 17 people on board.
The Gaisal train disaster claims 285 lives in Assam, India.
The Chechnya-based Islamic International Brigade invades neighboring Dagestan.
Russian president Boris Yeltsin fires his prime minister, Sergei Stepashin, and for the fourth time fires his entire cabinet.
Beni Ounif massacre in Algeria: Some 29 people are killed at a false roadblock near the Moroccan border, leading to temporary tensions with Morocco.
In Belgrade, Yugoslavia, tens of thousands of Serbians rally to demand the resignation of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia President Slobodan Milošević.
Kiribati, Nauru and Tonga join the United Nations.
Qantas Flight 1 overruns a runway in Bangkok during a storm, causing minor injuries to some passengers.
The United Kingdom's House of Lords votes to end the right of most hereditary peers to vote in Britain's upper chamber of Parliament.
Honolulu shootings: In the worst mass murder in the history of Hawaii, a gunman shoots at eight people in his workplace, killing seven.
The House of Lords Act is given Royal Assent, restricting membership of the British House of Lords by virtue of a hereditary peerage.
At Texas A&M University, the Aggie Bonfire collapses killing 12 students and injuring 27 others.
The United Kingdom devolves political power in Northern Ireland to the Northern Ireland Executive following the Good Friday Agreement.
SATA Air Açores Flight 530M crashes into Pico da Esperança on São Jorge Island in the Azores, killing 35.
Macau is handed over to China by Portugal.
The Spanish Civil Guard intercepts a van loaded with 950 kg of explosives that ETA intended to use to blow up Torre Picasso in Madrid, Spain.
Cubana de Aviación Flight 1216 overshoots the runway at La Aurora International Airport, killing 18.
The first President of Russia, Boris Yeltsin, resigns from office, leaving Prime Minister Vladimir Putin as the acting President and successor.
Indian Airlines Flight 814 hijacking ends after seven days with the release of 190 survivors at Kandahar Airport, Afghanistan.
Crossair Flight 498, a Saab 340 aircraft, crashes in Niederhasli, Switzerland, after taking off from Zurich Airport, killing 13 people.
A Short 360 aircraft chartered by the Sirte Oil Company crashes off the coast of Brega, Libya, killing 21.
Emery Worldwide Airlines Flight 17 crashes near Sacramento Mather Airport in Rancho Cordova, California, killing all three aboard.
Air Philippines Flight 541 crashes in Samal, Davao del Norte, killing all 131 people on board.
Canonization of Faustina Kowalska in the presence of 200,000 people and the first Divine Mercy Sunday celebrated worldwide.
President Bill Clinton announces that accurate GPS access would no longer be restricted to the United States military.
Second Chechen War: Chechen separatists ambush Russian paramilitary forces in the Republic of Ingushetia.
A fireworks storage depot explodes in a residential neighborhood in Enschede, Netherlands, killing 23 people and injuring 950 others.
The United Nations defines the Blue Line as the border between Israel and Lebanon.
Wuhan Airlines Flight 343 is struck by lightning and crashes into Wuhan's Hanyang District, killing 49 people.
Concorde Air France Flight 4590 crashes outside of Paris shortly after taking off at Charles de Gaulle Airport, killing 113 people.
Gulf Air Flight 072 crashes into the Persian Gulf near Manama, Bahrain, killing 143.
NASA launches Space Shuttle Atlantis on STS-106 to resupply the International Space Station.
Israeli–Palestinian conflict: Twelve-year-old Muhammad al-Durrah is shot and killed on the second day of the Second Intifada.
Israeli-Palestinian conflict: Hezbollah militants capture three Israeli Defense Force soldiers in a cross-border raid.
NASA launches STS-92, the 100th Space Shuttle mission.
A wave of protests forces Robert Guéï to step down as president after the Ivorian presidential election.
Chhattisgarh officially becomes the 26th state of India, formed from sixteen districts of eastern Madhya Pradesh.
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration discovers one of the country's largest LSD labs inside a converted military missile silo in Wamego, Kansas.
Kaprun disaster: One hundred fifty-five skiers and snowboarders die when a cable car catches fire in an alpine tunnel in Kaprun, Austria.
Philippine House Speaker Manny Villar passes the articles of impeachment against Philippine President Joseph Estrada.
Alberto Fujimori is removed from office as president of Peru.
The United States Supreme Court releases its decision in Bush v. Gore.
Downtown Disney opens to the public as part of the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, California.
An earthquake hits El Salvador, killing more than 800.
Wikipedia, a free wiki content encyclopedia, is launched (Wikipedia Day).
Second Congo War: Congolese President Laurent-Désiré Kabila is assassinated by one of his own bodyguards in Kinshasa.
US President Bill Clinton awards former President Theodore Roosevelt a posthumous Medal of Honor for his service in the Spanish–American War.
President of the Philippines Joseph Estrada is ousted in a nonviolent four-day revolution, and is succeeded by Gloria Macapagal Arroyo.
The 7.7 Mw Gujarat earthquake shakes Western India, leaving 13,805–20,023 dead and about 166,800 injured.
Diane Whipple, a lacrosse coach, is killed in a dog attack in San Francisco. The resulting court case clarified the meaning of implied malice murder.
Two Japan Airlines planes nearly collide over Suruga Bay in Japan.
FBI agent Robert Hanssen is arrested for spying for the Soviet Union. He is ultimately convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment.
Loganair Flight 670A crashes while attempting to make a water landing in the Firth of Forth in Scotland.
The Russian Mir space station is disposed of, breaking up in the atmosphere before falling into the southern Pacific Ocean near Fiji.
A Gulfstream III crashes on approach to Aspen/Pitkin County Airport in Aspen, Colorado. All 18 people on board are killed.
The detained crew of a United States EP-3E aircraft that landed in Hainan, China, after a collision with a J-8 fighter, is released.
Series of bombings at Ramna Park in Dhaka during the Bengali New Year celebrations leave 10 people dead and dozens other injured.
Space Shuttle Endeavour is launched on STS-100 carrying the Canadarm2 to the International Space Station.
During a trip to Syria, Pope John Paul II becomes the first pope to enter a mosque.
French Taubira law is enacted, officially recognizing the Atlantic slave trade and slavery as crimes against humanity.
Erik Weihenmayer becomes the first blind person to reach the summit of Mount Everest, in the Himalayas, with Dr. Sherman Bull.
Dolphinarium discotheque massacre: A Hamas suicide bomber kills 21 at a disco in Tel Aviv.
Mamoru Takuma kills eight and injures 15 in a mass stabbing at an elementary school in the Osaka Prefecture of Japan.
Pope John Paul II canonizes Lebanon's first female saint, Saint Rafqa.
Slobodan Milošević is extradited to the ICTY in The Hague to stand trial.
Australian criminal Bradley John Murdoch murders British tourist Peter Falconio and abducts his girlfriend in the Northern Territory.
Megawati Sukarnoputri was sworn in as the first female president of Indonesia following her predecessor's impeachment.
The Bandaranaike Airport attack is carried out by 14 Tamil Tiger commandos, resulting in military and civilian casualties and destroyed aircraft.
Phoolan Devi, a serving Member of Parliament, is assassinated by shooting in New Delhi, India.
Erwadi fire incident: Twenty-eight mentally ill persons tied to a chain are burnt to death at a faith based institution at Erwadi, Tamil Nadu.
Air Transat Flight 236 loses all engine power over the Atlantic Ocean, forcing the pilots to conduct an emergency landing in the Azores.
Four people are killed when Binter Mediterráneo Flight 8261 crashes into the N-340 highway near Málaga Airport.
In Belfast, Protestant loyalists begin a picket of Holy Cross, a Catholic primary school for girls.
Tokyo DisneySea opens to the public as part of the Tokyo Disney Resort in Urayasu, Chiba, Japan.
The New York Stock Exchange reopens for trading after the September 11 attacks, the longest closure since the Great Depression.
First mailing of anthrax letters from Trenton, New Jersey in the 2001 anthrax attacks.
The U.S. invasion of Afghanistan begins with an air assault and covert operations on the ground, starting the longest war in American history.
A twin engine Cessna and a Scandinavian Airlines System jetliner collide in heavy fog during takeoff from Milan, Italy, killing 118 people.
U.S. president George W. Bush announces the establishment of the Office of Homeland Security.
The Polaroid Corporation files for federal bankruptcy protection.
Microsoft releases Windows XP, which becomes one of Microsoft's most successful operating systems.
Turkey, Australia, and Canada agree to commit troops to the invasion of Afghanistan.
Journalists Pierre Billaud, Johanne Sutton and Volker Handloik are killed in Afghanistan during an attack on the convoy they are traveling in.
War in Afghanistan: Taliban forces abandon Kabul, ahead of advancing Afghan Northern Alliance troops.
The Budapest Convention on Cybercrime is signed in Budapest, Hungary.
Israeli–Palestinian conflict: Israeli forces seize the Palestinian freighter Karine A in the Red Sea, finding 50 tons of weapons.
An explosion at a military storage facility in Lagos, Nigeria, kills at least 1,100 people and displaces over 20,000 others.
TAME Flight 120, a Boeing 727-100, crashes in the Andes mountains in southern Colombia, killing 94.
The MPLA government of Angola and UNITA rebels sign a peace treaty ending the Angolan Civil War.
The Ghriba synagogue bombing by al-Qaeda kills 21 in Tunisia.
A suicide bomber blows herself up at the entrance to Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda Market, killing seven people and wounding 104.
Robert Steinhäuser kills 16 at Gutenberg-Gymnasium in Erfurt, Germany, before committing suicide.
Dutch politician Pim Fortuyn is assassinated following a radio interview at the Mediapark in Hilversum.
Antonio Meucci is acknowledged as the first inventor of the telephone by the United States Congress.
Near-Earth asteroid 2002 MN misses the Earth by 75,000 miles (121,000 km), about one-third of the distance between the Earth and the Moon.
The Igandu train disaster in Tanzania kills 281, the worst train accident in African history.
A Boeing 707 crashes near Bangui M'Poko International Airport in Bangui, Central African Republic, killing 28.
French president Jacques Chirac escapes an assassination attempt from Maxime Brunerie during a Bastille Day parade at Champs-Élysées.
American Taliban John Walker Lindh pleads guilty to supplying aid to the enemy and possession of explosives during the commission of a felony.
Nine coal miners trapped in the flooded Quecreek Mine in Somerset County, Pennsylvania, are rescued after 77 hours underground.
Khankala Mi-26 crash: A Russian Mil Mi-26 helicopter carrying troops is hit by a Chechen missile outside Grozny, killing 118 soldiers.
The Oakland Athletics win their 20th consecutive game, an American League record, until the Cleveland Indians surpassed it in 2017.
The Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on STS-112 to continue assembly of the International Space Station.
A bomb attack in a Myyrmanni shopping mall in Vantaa, Finland kills seven.
Top Gear, the revived popular British TV motoring magazine, premieres on BBC.
A Fokker 50 crashes near Luxembourg Airport, killing 20 and injuring three.
Jiang Lijun is detained by Chinese police for signing the Open Letter to the 16th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party.
Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraq agrees to the terms of the UN Security Council Resolution 1441.
Iraq disarmament crisis: United Nations weapons inspectors led by Hans Blix arrive in Iraq.
Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-113 to the International Space Station carrying the Expedition 6 crew and the P1 truss.
Two truck bombs kill 72 and wound 200 at the pro-Moscow headquarters of the Chechen government in Grozny, Chechnya, Russia.
Human Genome Project completed (April)
A suicide bombing at the Tel Aviv central bus station kills 23 people and injures over 100 more.
Turkish Airlines Flight 634 crashes near Diyarbakır Airport, Turkey, killing the entire crew and 70 of the 75 passengers.
Air Midwest Flight 5481 crashes at Charlotte-Douglas Airport, in Charlotte, North Carolina, killing all 21 people on board.
TANS Perú Flight 222 crashes on approach to Chachapoyas Airport in Chachapoyas, Peru, killing 46 people.
North Korea withdraws from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, making it the first state to withdraw from the treaty.
Illinois Governor George Ryan commutes the death sentences of 167 prisoners on Illinois's death row based on the Jon Burge scandal.
208996 Achlys was discovered by Chad Trujillo and Michael E. Brown at Palomar Observatory.
The Space Shuttle Columbia takes off for mission STS-107 which would be its final one. Columbia disintegrated 16 days later on re-entry.
A 7.6 magnitude earthquake strikes the Mexican state of Colima, killing 29 and leaving approximately 10,000 people homeless.
The first selections for the National Recording Registry are announced by the Library of Congress.
The Waterfall rail accident occurs near Waterfall, New South Wales, Australia.
Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated during the reentry of mission STS-107 into the Earth's atmosphere, killing all seven astronauts aboard.
The International Criminal Court holds its inaugural session in The Hague.
Iraq War: U.S. troops capture Baghdad; Saddam Hussein's Ba'athist regime falls two days later.
Ukrainian-Mediterranean Airlines Flight 4230 crashes in the Turkish town of Maçka, killing 75.
The Spirit rover is launched, beginning NASA's Mars Exploration Rover mission.
NASA Opportunity rover, MER-B or Mars Exploration Rover–B, was launched into space aboard a Delta II rocket.
Sudan Airways Flight 139 crashes near Port Sudan Airport during an emergency landing attempt, killing 116 of the 117 people on board.
AOL Time Warner disbands Netscape. The Mozilla Foundation is established on the same day.
A car bomb explodes in the Indonesian capital of Jakarta outside the Marriott Hotel killing 12 and injuring 150.
The Okinawa Urban Monorail is opened in Naha, Okinawa.
A truck-bomb attack on United Nations headquarters in Iraq kills the agency's top envoy Sérgio Vieira de Mello and 21 other employees.
Shmuel HaNavi bus bombing: A suicide attack on a bus in Jerusalem, planned by Hamas, kills 23 Israelis, seven of them children.
In a referendum, Estonia approves joining the European Union.
Bissau-Guinean President Kumba Ialá is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General Veríssimo Correia Seabra.
The 8.3 Mw Hokkaidō earthquake strikes just offshore Hokkaidō, Japan.
Mother Teresa is beatified by Pope John Paul II.
The Sloan Great Wall, once the largest cosmic structures known to humanity, is discovered by students at Princeton University.
Actor Arnold Schwarzenegger's tenure as the governor of California begins.
Rose Revolution: Georgian president Eduard Shevardnadze resigns following weeks of mass protests over flawed elections.
SpaceShipOne, piloted by Brian Binnie, makes its first powered and first supersonic flight.
Stardust successfully flies past Comet Wild 2, collecting samples that are returned to Earth.
Flash Airlines Flight 604 crashes into the Red Sea, resulting in 148 deaths, making it one of the deadliest aviation accidents in Egyptian history.
Spirit, a NASA Mars rover, lands successfully on Mars at 04:35 UTC.
Mikheil Saakashvili is elected President of Georgia following the November 2003 Rose Revolution.
The RMS Queen Mary 2, then the largest ocean liner ever built, is christened by her namesake's granddaughter, Queen Elizabeth II.
The world's largest ocean liner, RMS Queen Mary 2, makes its maiden voyage.
Uzbekistan Airways Flight 1154 crashes while landing at Tashkent International Airport, killing 37.
Hajj pilgrimage stampede: In a stampede at the Hajj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia, 251 people are trampled to death and 244 injured.
Double suicide attack in Erbil on the offices of Iraqi Kurdish political parties by members of Jama'at al-Tawhid wal-Jihad
Swiss tennis player Roger Federer becomes the No. 1 ranked men's singles player, a position he will hold for a record 237 weeks.
Facebook, a mainstream online social networking site, is founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Eduardo Saverin.
Rebels from the Revolutionary Artibonite Resistance Front capture the city of Gonaïves, starting the 2004 Haiti rebellion.
A bombing of a SuperFerry by Abu Sayyaf in the Philippines' worst terrorist attack kills more than 100 passengers.
Shoko Asahara, the leader of the Japanese doomsday cult Aum Shinrikyo, is sentenced to death for masterminding the 1995 Tokyo subway sarin attack.
Madrid train bombings: Simultaneous explosions on rush hour trains in Madrid, Spain kill 191 people.
Unrest in Kosovo: More than 22 are killed and 200 wounded. Thirty-five Serbian Orthodox shrines in Kosovo and two mosques in Serbia are destroyed.
Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia join NATO as full members.
Iraq War in Anbar Province: In Fallujah, Iraq, four American private military contractors working for Blackwater USA, are killed after being ambushed.
Rolandas Paksas becomes the first president of Lithuania to be peacefully removed from office by impeachment.
The Nicoll Highway in Singapore collapses, killing four workers.
Five suicide car bombers target police stations in and around Basra, killing 74 people and wounding 160.
The final Oldsmobile is built in Lansing, Michigan, ending 107 years of vehicle production.
U.S. media release graphic photos of American soldiers committing war crimes against Iraqi prisoners at Abu Ghraib prison.
Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark and Mary Donaldson are married at Copenhagen Cathedral.
The Constitutional Court of South Korea overturns the impeachment of President Roh Moo-hyun.
The Iraqi Governing Council chooses Ayad Allawi, a longtime anti-Saddam Hussein exile, as prime minister of Iraq's interim government.
Cassini–Huygens makes its closest flyby of the Saturn moon Phoebe.
Iraq War: Sovereign power is handed to the interim government of Iraq by the Coalition Provisional Authority, ending the U.S.-led rule of that nation.
Greece beats Portugal in the UEFA Euro 2004 Final and becomes European Champion for first time in its history.
One hundred fifty-six Congolese Tutsi refugees are massacred at the Gatumba refugee camp in Burundi.
Google Inc. has its initial public offering on Nasdaq.
Over 3,000 people die in Haiti after Hurricane Jeanne produces massive flooding and mudslides.
Burt Rutan's Ansari SpaceShipOne performs a successful spaceflight, the first of two required to win the Ansari X Prize.
The first parkrun, then known as the Bushy Park Time Trial, takes place in Bushy Park, London, UK.
Three bombs explode at Taba and Nuweiba in the Sinai Peninsula, Egypt, killing 34.
Thirteen people are killed when Corporate Airlines Flight 5966 crashes in Adair County, Missouri, while on approach to Kirksville Regional Airport.
An express train collides with a stationary car near the village of Ufton Nervet, England, killing seven and injuring 120.
Iraq War: The interim government of Iraq calls for a 60-day state of emergency as U.S. forces storm the insurgent stronghold of Fallujah.
New Zealand Tomb of the Unknown Warrior is dedicated at the National War Memorial, Wellington.
The Orange Revolution begins in Ukraine, resulting from the presidential elections.
The Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, the largest religious building in Georgia, is consecrated.
Pope John Paul II returns the relics of Saint John Chrysostom to the Eastern Orthodox Church.
Blackwater 61 crash: A CASA C-212 Aviocar crashes into the Koh-i-Baba mountain range in Afghanistan, killing six.
The official opening of Taipei 101, the tallest skyscraper at that time in the world, standing at a height of 509 metres (1,670 ft).
Edgar Ray Killen is indicted for the 1964 murders of Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner during the American Civil Rights Movement.
A train collision in Graniteville, South Carolina, United States, releases about 60 tons of chlorine gas.
The Sudan People's Liberation Movement and the Government of Sudan sign the Comprehensive Peace Agreement to end the Second Sudanese Civil War.
Deep Impact launches from Cape Canaveral on a Delta II rocket.
ESA's SMART-1 lunar orbiter discovers elements such as calcium, aluminum, silicon, iron, and other surface elements on the Moon.
In Belmopan, Belize, the unrest over the government's new taxes erupts into riots.
A stampede at the Mandhradevi temple in Maharashtra, India kills at least 258.
The Government of Canada introduces the Civil Marriage Act. This legislation would become law on July 20, 2005, legalizing same-sex marriage.
The Kyoto Protocol comes into force, following its ratification by Russia.
The dwarf planet Makemake is discovered by a team led by astronomer Michael E. Brown at the Palomar Observatory.
Kurdish leader Jalal Talabani becomes Iraqi president; Shiite Arab Ibrahim al-Jaafari is named premier the next day.
Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger is elected to the papacy and becomes Pope Benedict XVI.
Japan's Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi apologizes for Japan's war record.
Kuwait permits women's suffrage in a 35–23 National Assembly vote.
The tallest roller coaster in the world, Kingda Ka opens at Six Flags Great Adventure in Jackson Township, New Jersey.
Vanity Fair reveals that Mark Felt was "Deep Throat".
The jury acquits pop singer Michael Jackson of all charges for allegedly sexually abusing a child in 2003.
Right to Information Act passed (15 June)
American social news and discussion site Reddit is founded in Medford, Massachusetts by Steve Huffman and Alexis Ohanian.
The Deep Impact collider hits the comet Tempel 1.
A series of four explosions occurs on London's transport system, killing 56 people, including four suicide bombers, and injuring over 700 others.
Three bombs explode in the Naama Bay area of Sharm El Sheikh, Egypt, killing 88 people.
Space Shuttle program: STS-114 Mission: Launch of Discovery, NASA's first scheduled flight mission after the Columbia Disaster in 2003.
The Provisional Irish Republican Army calls an end to its thirty-year-long armed campaign against British rule in Northern Ireland.
President of Mauritania Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya is overthrown in a military coup while attending the funeral of King Fahd in Saudi Arabia.
Israel's unilateral disengagement plan to evict all Israelis from the Gaza Strip and from four settlements in the northern West Bank begins.
The Helsinki Agreement between the Free Aceh Movement and the Government of Indonesia is signed, ending almost three decades of fighting.
Hurricane Rita makes landfall in the United States, devastating portions of southwestern Louisiana and extreme southeastern Texas.
The 7.6 Mw Kashmir earthquake leaves 86,000–87,351 people dead, 69,000–75,266 injured, and 2.8 million homeless.
Saddam Hussein goes on trial in Baghdad for crimes against humanity.
Hurricane Wilma becomes the most intense Atlantic hurricane on record with a minimum pressure of 882 mb.
Following a 31-year wait, Australia defeats Uruguay in a penalty shootout to qualify for the 2006 FIFA World Cup.
Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is elected president of Liberia and becomes the first woman to lead an African country.
Ehud Olmert becomes acting Prime Minister of Israel after the incumbent, Ariel Sharon, suffers a second, apparently more serious stroke.
A stampede during the Stoning of the Devil ritual on the last day at the Hajj in Mina, Saudi Arabia, kills at least 362 Muslim pilgrims.
Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is sworn in as Liberia's new president. She becomes Africa's first female elected head of state.
A Slovak Air Force Antonov An-24 crashes near Hejce, Hungary, killing 42.
Mexican professional wrestler Juana Barraza is arrested in connection with the serial killing of at least ten elderly women.
Cyclone Glenda, one of the strongest tropical cyclones in the Australian region makes landfall near Onslow, Western Australia.
Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announces Iran's claim to have successfully enriched uranium.
The United Front for Democratic Change's attack on the Chadian capital of N'Djamena is repelled by the Chadian army
Twin blasts triggered by crude bombs during Asr prayer in the Jama Masjid mosque in Delhi injure 13 people.
The government of Sudan signs an accord with the Sudan Liberation Army.
Mass unrest by the Primeiro Comando da Capital begins in São Paulo (Brazil), leaving at least 150 dead.
Iranian Azeris interpret a cartoon published in an Iranian magazine as insulting, resulting in massive riots throughout the country.
The 6.4 Mw Yogyakarta earthquake shakes central Java with an MSK intensity of VIII (Damaging), leaving more than 5,700 dead and 37,000 injured.
The first Kazakh space satellite, KazSat-1, is launched.
A shootout happens in Spiritwood, Canada, killing two Royal Canadian Mounted Police and wounding a third officer.
Italy win their fourth World Cup title, defeating France 5–3 on penalties following a 1–1 draw after extra time.
Sri Lankan Civil War: Sixty-one schoolgirls killed in Chencholai bombing by Sri Lanka Air Force air strike.
The International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefines the term "planet" such that Pluto is now considered a dwarf planet.
North Korea conducts its first nuclear test.
The House of Commons of Canada approves a motion introduced by Prime Minister Stephen Harper recognizing the Québécois as a nation within Canada.
The law on same-sex marriage comes into force in South Africa, legalizing same-sex marriage for the first time on the African continent.
NASA reveals photographs taken by Mars Global Surveyor suggesting the presence of liquid water on Mars.
Two earthquakes in Hengchun, Taiwan measuring 7.0 and 6.9 on the moment magnitude scale kill two and disrupt telecommunications across Asia.
War in Somalia: The militaries of Somalia's Transitional Federal Government and Ethiopian troops capture Mogadishu unopposed.
The 110th United States Congress convenes, electing Nancy Pelosi as the first female Speaker of the House in U.S. history.
Apple CEO Steve Jobs introduces the original iPhone at a Macworld keynote in San Francisco.
A general strike begins in Guinea in an attempt to get President Lansana Conté to resign.
At least 88 people are killed when two car bombs explode in the Bab Al-Sharqi market in central Baghdad, Iraq.
Microsoft Corporation releases Windows Vista, a major release of the operating system Microsoft Windows and the NT based kernel.
Algiers bombings: Two bombings in Algiers kill 33 people and wound a further 222 others.
Estonian authorities remove the Bronze Soldier, a Soviet Red Army war memorial in Tallinn, amid political controversy with Russia.
Israeli archaeologists discover the tomb of Herod the Great south of Jerusalem.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on STS-117 carrying two truss segments and solar arrays to the International Space Station.
The Charleston Sofa Super Store fire kills nine firefighters in Charleston, South Carolina.
The small town of Elie, Manitoba is hit by Canada's most intense tornado on record.
PMTair Flight 241 crashes in the Dâmrei Mountains in Kampot Province, Cambodia, killing all 22 people on board.
Tony Blair resigns as British Prime Minister, a position he had held since 1997. Chancellor Gordon Brown succeeds him.
The Brazilian Military Police invades the favelas of Complexo do Alemão in an episode which is remembered as the Complexo do Alemão massacre.
Former deputy director of the Chilean secret police Raúl Iturriaga is captured after having been on the run following a conviction for kidnapping.
NASA's Phoenix Mars lander is launched.
At AT&T Park, Barry Bonds hits his 756th career home run to surpass Hank Aaron's 33-year-old record.
Air Moorea Flight 1121 crashes after takeoff from Moorea Airport in French Polynesia, killing all 20 people on board.
An 8.0-magnitude earthquake off the Pacific coast devastates Ica and various regions of Peru, killing 514 and injuring 1,090.
The Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples is adopted by the United Nations General Assembly.
Prelude to the 2008 financial crisis: Northern Rock bank experiences the first bank run in the United Kingdom in 150 years.
Between 30,000 and 100,000 people take part in anti-government protests in Yangon, Burma, the largest in 20 years.
President Roh Moo-hyun of South Korea goes to North Korea for an Inter-Korean summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.
The battle of Mirali begins in which the Pakistan Armed Forces and Taliban militias clash for four days.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average reaches its all-time high of 14,164 points before rapidly declining due to the 2008 financial crisis.
Cristina Fernández de Kirchner becomes the first directly elected female President of Argentina.
The Jokela school shooting in Jokela, Tuusula, Finland, takes place, resulting in the death of nine people.
Elizabeth II becomes the oldest monarch in the history of the United Kingdom, surpassing Queen Victoria, who lived for 81 years and 243 days.
Former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto is assassinated in a shooting incident.
A Let L-410 Turbolet crashes in the Los Roques Archipelago in Venezuela, killing 14 people.
Civic mobilizations in Colombia against FARC, under the name A million voices against the FARC.
Kosovo declares independence from Serbia.
The New York Philharmonic performs in Pyongyang, North Korea; this was the first such event to take place in North Korea.
Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-123, carrying the first component of the Japanese Kibō module to the International Space Station.
Bhutan officially becomes a democracy, with its first ever general election.
Kata Air Transport Flight 007 crashes while attempting an emergency landing at Chișinău International Airport, killing eight.
The Quito Ultratumba nightclub fire in Quito, Ecuador, kills 19 people and injures at least 24 more.
Danica Patrick wins the Indy Japan 300, becoming the first female driver in history to win an Indy car race.
Cyclone Nargis makes landfall in Burma killing over 138,000 people and leaving millions of people homeless.
Chaitén Volcano begins erupting in Chile, forcing the evacuation of more than 4,500 people.
NASA's Phoenix lander touches down in the Green Valley region of Mars to search for environments suitable for water and microbial life.
The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly of Nepal formally declares Nepal a republic, ending the 240-year reign of the Shah dynasty.
TACA Flight 390 overshoots the runway at Toncontín International Airport in Tegucigalpa, Honduras and crashes, killing five people.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-124 carrying the second portion of the Japanese Kibō module to the International Space Station.
East Coast Jets Flight 81 crashes near Owatonna Degner Regional Airport in Owatonna, Minnesota, killing all eight people on board.
The New England Revolution win the 2008 North American SuperLiga final against the Houston Dynamo.
A military junta led by Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz stages a coup d'état in Mauritania, overthrowing president Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi.
The start of the Russo-Georgian War over the territory of South Ossetia.
Russo-Georgian War: Russian units occupy the Georgian city of Gori.
The President of Pakistan, Pervez Musharraf, resigns under threat of impeachment.
A Cessna 208 Caravan crashes in Cabañas, Zacapa, Guatemala, killing 11 people.
A Conviasa Boeing 737 crashes into Illiniza Volcano in Ecuador, killing all three people on board.
Iraq War: The United States Armed Forces transfers control of Anbar Province to the Iraqi Armed Forces.
Delhi, India, is hit by a series of bomb blasts, resulting in 30 deaths and 130 injuries.
Thabo Mbeki resigns as president of South Africa.
Qantas Flight 72 experiences an in-flight upset near Exmouth, Western Australia, Australia, injuring 112.
Asteroid 2008 TC3 impacts the Earth over Sudan, the first time an asteroid impact is detected prior to its entry into Earth's atmosphere.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closes down 733.08 points, or 7.87%, the second worst percentage drop in the Dow's history.
Chandrayaan-1 launched (22 October); finds water molecules on the Moon
A protest movement in Iceland culminates as the 2009 Icelandic financial crisis protests start.
Cyclone Klaus makes landfall near Bordeaux, France, causing 26 deaths as well as extensive disruptions to public transport and power supplies.
Nadya Suleman gives birth to the world's first surviving octuplets.
Soldiers of the Bangladesh Rifles mutiny at their headquarters in Pilkhana, Dhaka, Bangladesh, resulting in 74 deaths, including 57 army officials.
Mass protests begin across Moldova under the belief that results from the parliamentary election are fraudulent.
Zimbabwe officially abandons the Zimbabwean dollar as its official currency.
A fire destroys a homeless hostel and kills at least 22 people in Kamień Pomorski, Poland.
Chrysler files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
An American soldier in Iraq opens fire on a counseling center at Camp Liberty in Baghdad, killing five other US soldiers and wounding three.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on the final mission to service the Hubble Space Telescope.
An Indonesian Air Force Lockheed L-100 Hercules crashes in Magetan Regency, killing 99.
General Motors files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. It is the fourth largest United States bankruptcy in history.
The first of four days of bombings begins on the southern Philippine island group of Mindanao.
Space Shuttle program: Endeavour is launched on STS-127 to complete assembly of the International Space Station's Kibō module.
Aria Air Flight 1525 crashes at Mashhad International Airport, killing 16.
Twenty people are killed in Handlová, Trenčín Region, in the deadliest mining disaster in Slovakia's history.
Right to Education Act passed (26 August)
The G20 summit begins in Pittsburgh with 30 global leaders in attendance.
Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Turkey join in the Turkic Council.
The October 2009 Baghdad bombings kill 155 and wound at least 721.
NASA successfully launches the Ares I-X mission, the only rocket launch for its short-lived Constellation program.
US President Barack Obama signs the Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act.
An Ilyushin Il-76 crashes near the Mir mine after takeoff from Mirny Airport in Yakutia, killing all 11 aboard.
U.S. Army Major Nidal Hasan murders 13 and wounds 32 at Fort Hood, Texas in the deadliest mass shooting at a U.S. military installation.
Space Shuttle program: Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched on mission STS-129 to the International Space Station.
The Maguindanao massacre occurs in Ampatuan, Philippines; 58 opponents of Andal Ampatuan Jr. are kidnapped and killed.
The Avdhela Project, an Aromanian digital library and cultural initiative, is founded in Bucharest, Romania.
The Treaty of Lisbon entered into force in the European Union.
Finnish game developer Rovio Entertainment releases the hit mobile game Angry Birds internationally on iOS.
Iranian election protests: On the Day of Ashura in Tehran, Iran, government security forces fire upon demonstrators.
Forty-three people die in a suicide bombing in Karachi, Pakistan, where Shia Muslims are observing the Day of Ashura.
The Burj Khalifa, the current tallest building in the world, officially opens in Dubai.
