An earthquake in Haiti occurs, killing between 220,000 and 300,000 people and destroying much of the capital Port-au-Prince.
Yemen declares an open war against the terrorist group al-Qaeda.
Rioting begins between Muslim and Christian groups in Jos, Nigeria, results in at least 200 deaths.
Ethiopian Airlines Flight 409 crashes into the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Na'ameh, Lebanon, killing 90.
The 2009 Honduran constitutional crisis ends when Porfirio Lobo Sosa becomes the new President of Honduras.
Apple announces the iPad.
WikiLeaks publishes the first of hundreds of thousands of classified documents disclosed by the soldier now known as Chelsea Manning.
Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-131 to resupply the International Space Station.
Maoist rebels kill 76 CRPF officers in Dantewada district, India.
Merano derailment: A rail accident in South Tyrol kills nine people and injures a further 28.
The Deepwater Horizon drilling rig explodes in the Gulf of Mexico, killing eleven workers and beginning an oil spill that lasted six months.
Faisal Shahzad attempts to detonate a car bomb in Times Square, but the bomb fails to go off.
Mass protests in Greece erupt in response to austerity measures imposed by the government as a result of the Greek government-debt crisis.
In West Bengal, India, the Jnaneswari Express train derailment and subsequent collision kills 148 passengers.
Twelve people are killed and eleven others injured in a spree shooting in Cumbria, England, before the perpetrator takes his own life.
The first FIFA World Cup held on African soil kicks off in South Africa.
At Wimbledon, John Isner of the United States defeats Nicolas Mahut of France, in the longest match in professional tennis history.
The English-Irish boy band One Direction were formed while auditioning for the 2010 series of the British singing competition The X Factor.
An overloaded passenger ferry capsizes on the Kasai River in Bandundu Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, resulting in at least 80 deaths.
Flash floods across a large part of Jammu and Kashmir, India, damages 71 towns and kills at least 255 people.
Operation Iraqi Freedom ends, with the last of the United States brigade combat teams crossing the border to Kuwait.
In San Fernando, Tamaulipas, Mexico, 72 illegal immigrants are killed by Los Zetas and eventually found dead by Mexican authorities.
Henan Airlines Flight 8387 crashes at Yichun Lindu Airport in Yichun, Heilongjiang, China, killing 44 out of the 96 people on board.
The mining accident in Copiapó, Chile ends as all 33 trapped miners arrive at the surface after a record 69 days underground.
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes off Indonesia's Mentawai Islands, triggering a tsunami that kills at least 400 people.
JS Air Flight 201 crashes after takeoff from Jinnah International Airport in Karachi, Pakistan, killing all 21 aboard.
During the Cambodian water festival, a stampede in Koh Pich, Phnom Penh, kills 347 people.
Mohamed Bouazizi sets himself on fire. This act became the catalyst for the Tunisian Revolution and the wider Arab Spring.
A bomb explodes as Coptic Christians in Alexandria, Egypt, leave a new year service, killing 23 people.
At least 35 are killed and 180 injured in a bombing at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport.
Arab Spring: The Yemeni Revolution begins as over 16,000 protestors demonstrate in Sanaa.
Within Ursa Minor, H1504+65, a white dwarf with the hottest known surface temperature in the universe at 200,000 K, was documented.
Arab Spring: Libyan protests against Muammar Gaddafi's regime begin.
Min Aung Hlaing is appointed as the Commander-in-Chief of Myanmar's armed forces.
Georgian Airways Flight 834 crashes at N'djili Airport in Kinshasa, killing 32.
In San Fernando, Tamaulipas, Mexico, over 193 victims of Los Zetas were exhumed from several mass graves.
An explosion in the Minsk Metro, Belarus, kills 15 people and injures 204 others.
Fidel Castro resigns as First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba after holding the title since July 1961.
The wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton takes place at Westminster Abbey in London.
Pope John Paul II is beatified by his successor, Pope Benedict XVI.
An earthquake of magnitude 5.1 hits Lorca, Spain.
The Istanbul Convention is signed in Istanbul, Turkey.
Two bombs explode in the Charsadda District of Pakistan killing 98 people and wounding 140 others.
STS-134 (ISS assembly flight ULF6), launched from the Kennedy Space Center on the 25th and final flight for Space Shuttle Endeavour.
A rare tornado outbreak occurs in New England; a strong EF3 tornado strikes Springfield, Massachusetts, during the event, killing four people.
Space Shuttle Atlantis is launched in the final mission of the U.S. Space Shuttle program.
Mumbai is rocked by three bomb blasts during the evening rush hour, killing 26 and injuring 130.
United Nations Security Council Resolution 1999 is adopted, which admits South Sudan to member status of United Nations.
Noar Linhas Aéreas Flight 4896 crashes in Boa Viagem, Recife, killing all 16 people on board.
Guinean President Alpha Condé survives an attempted assassination and coup d'état at his residence in Conakry.
NASA's Space Shuttle program ends with the landing of Space Shuttle Atlantis on mission STS-135 at NASA's Kennedy Space Center.
Norway attacks: A bomb explodes, targeted at government buildings in central Oslo, followed by a massacre at a youth camp on the island of Utøya.
A high-speed train rear-ends another on a viaduct on the Yongtaiwen railway line in Wenzhou, Zhejiang province, China, resulting in 40 deaths.
A Royal Moroccan Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules crashes near Guelmim Airport in Guelmim, Morocco. All 80 people on board are killed.
A terrorist attack on Israel's Highway 12 near the Egyptian border kills 16 and injures 40.
Mariano Rivera of the New York Yankees surpasses Trevor Hoffman to become Major League Baseball's all-time career saves leader with 602.
The special court in India convicted all 269 accused officials for atrocity on Dalits and 17 for rape in the Vachathi case.
Iraq War: President Barack Obama announces that the withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq will be complete by the end of the year.
Mario Draghi succeeds Jean-Claude Trichet and becomes the third president of the European Central Bank.
A helicopter crash just outside Mexico City kills seven, including Francisco Blake Mora the Secretary of the Interior of Mexico.
Silvio Berlusconi tenders his resignation as Prime Minister of Italy, effective November 16, due in large part to the Euro area crisis.
NASA succeeds in putting the first of two Gravity Recovery and Interior Laboratory satellites in orbit around the Moon.
Twenty-six people are killed and 63 wounded when a suicide bomber blows himself up at a police station in Damascus.
A hot air balloon crashes near Carterton, New Zealand, killing all 11 people on board.
A bombing at Jamrud in Pakistan, kills at least 30 people and injures 78 others.
The ferry MV Rabaul Queen sinks off the coast of Papua New Guinea near the Finschhafen District, with an estimated 146–165 dead.
A train derails in Burlington, Ontario, Canada killing at least three people and injuring 45.
A series of explosions is reported at a munitions dump in Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of the Congo, killing at least 250 people.
A U.S. soldier kills 16 civilians in the Panjwayi District of Afghanistan near Kandahar.
Azawad declares itself independent from the Republic of Mali.
Two trains are involved in a head-on collision near Sloterdijk, Amsterdam, in the Netherlands, killing one person and injuring 116 others.
At least four explosions hit the Ukrainian city of Dnipropetrovsk with at least 27 people injured.
An overloaded ferry capsizes on the Brahmaputra River in India killing at least 108 people. At least 150 more are missing and presumed dead.
Forty-nine dismembered bodies are discovered by Mexican authorities on Mexican Federal Highway 40.
The SpaceX Dragon 1 becomes the first commercial spacecraft to successfully rendezvous and berth with the International Space Station.
The Arkankergen massacre in Kazakhstan's Alakol District kills 15 people.
Former Liberian president Charles Taylor is sentenced to 50 years in prison for his role in atrocities committed during the Sierra Leone Civil War.
A series of bombings across Iraq, including Baghdad, Hillah and Kirkuk, kills at least 93 people and wounds over 300 others.
Paraguayan President Fernando Lugo is removed from office by impeachment and succeeded by Federico Franco.
Ashton Eaton breaks the decathlon world record at the United States Olympic Trials.
Death of Lonesome George, the last known individual of Chelonoidis nigra abingdonii, a subspecies of the Galápagos tortoise.
Higgs boson discovery announced at CERN (4 July)
The discovery of particles consistent with the Higgs boson at the Large Hadron Collider is announced at CERN.
At least 172 people are killed in a flash flood in the Krasnodar Krai region of Russia.
Syrian civil war: The People's Protection Units (YPG) capture the city of Kobanî without resistance, starting the Rojava conflict in Northeast Syria.
Syrian civil war: The People's Protection Units (YPG) capture the cities of Amuda and Efrîn without resistance.
James Holmes opened fire at a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado, killing 12 and injuring 70 others.
Syrian civil war: The People's Protection Units (YPG) capture the city of Girkê Legê.
A train fire kills 32 passengers and injures 27 on the Tamil Nadu Express in Andhra Pradesh, India.
Michael Phelps breaks the record set in 1964 by Larisa Latynina for the most medals won at the Olympics.
NASA's Curiosity rover lands on the surface of Mars.
Shannon Eastin becomes the first woman to officiate an NFL game.
Anders Behring Breivik, perpetrator of the 2011 Norway attacks, is sentenced to 21 years of preventive detention.
The Indian space agency puts into orbit its heaviest foreign satellite yet, in a streak of 21 consecutive successful PSLV launches.
A bomb explosion kills eight people and injures 110 more in Lebanon.
Microsoft made a public release of Windows 8 and made it available on new PCs.
A fuel tank truck crashes and explodes in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, killing 26 people and injuring 135.
Tammy Baldwin becomes the first openly gay politician to be elected to the United States Senate.
A strong earthquake with the magnitude 6.8 hits northern Burma, killing at least 26 people.
At least 50 schoolchildren are killed in an accident at a railway crossing near Manfalut, Egypt.
Pope Tawadros II of Alexandria becomes the 118th Pope of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria.
At least 125 people are killed and up to 200 injured in bombings in the Alawite village of Aqrab, Syria.
North Korea successfully launches its first satellite, Kwangmyŏngsŏng-3 Unit 2.
China opens the world's longest high-speed rail route, which links Beijing and Guangzhou.
At least 60 people are killed and 200 injured in a stampede after celebrations at Félix Houphouët-Boigny Stadium in Abidjan, Ivory Coast.
A gunman kills eight people in a house-to-house rampage in Kawit, Cavite, Philippines.
More than 100 people are killed and 270 injured in several bomb blasts in the Quetta area of Pakistan.
One French soldier and 17 militants are killed in a failed attempt to free a French hostage in Bulo Marer, Somalia.
A train carrying Egyptian Army recruits derails near Giza, Greater Cairo, killing 19 and injuring 120 others.
Former cyclist Lance Armstrong confesses to his doping in an airing of Oprah's Next Chapter.
Two hundred and forty-two people die in a nightclub fire in the Brazilian city of Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul.
SCAT Airlines Flight 760 crashes near the Kazakh city of Almaty, killing 21 people.
Naro-1 becomes the first carrier rocket launched by South Korea.
A bomb blast at a market in Hazara Town, Quetta, Pakistan kills more than 80 people and injures 190 others.
Armed robbers steal a haul of diamonds worth $50 million during a raid at Brussels Airport in Belgium.
A hot air balloon crashes near Luxor, Egypt, killing 19 people.
A bomb blast in Karachi, Pakistan, kills at least 48 people and injured 200 others in a predominantly Shia Muslim area.
At least 36 people are killed when a 16-floor building collapses in the commercial capital Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
Two suicide bombers kill three Chadian soldiers and injure dozens of civilians at a market in Kidal, Mali.
Salam Fayyad resigns as Prime Minister of the Palestinian National Authority following an ongoing dispute with President Mahmoud Abbas.
Lion Air Flight 904 crashes on approach to Ngurah Rai International Airport in Denpasar, Indonesia, injuring 40 people.
A 6.6-magnitude earthquake strikes Lushan County, Ya'an, in China's Sichuan province, killing at least 193 people and injuring thousands.
A powerful explosion occurs in an office building in Prague, believed to have been caused by natural gas, and injures 43 people.
Willem-Alexander is inaugurated as King of the Netherlands following the abdication of Beatrix.
Fifty-two people are killed in a bombing in Reyhanlı, Turkey.
An upsurge in violence in Iraq leaves more than 389 people dead over three days.
An EF5 tornado strikes the Oklahoma City suburb of Moore, killing 24 people and injuring 377 others.
The asteroid 1998 QE2 and its moon make their closest approach to Earth for the next two centuries.
Nik Wallenda becomes the first man to successfully walk across the Grand Canyon on a tight rope.
A magnitude 6.1 earthquake strikes Aceh, Indonesia, killing at least 42 people and injuring 420 others.
A De Havilland Otter air taxi crashes in Soldotna, Alaska, killing ten people.
Typhoon Soulik kills at least nine people and affects more than 160 million in East China and Taiwan.
Dedication of the statue of Rachel Carson, a sculpture of the environmentalist, in Woods Hole, Massachusetts.
Seventeen government soldiers are killed in an attack by FARC revolutionaries in the Colombian department of Arauca.
Syrian civil war: The Battle of Ras al-Ayn ends with the expulsion of Islamist forces from the city by the People's Protection Units (YPG).
Dingxi earthquakes: A series of earthquakes in Dingxi, China, kills at least 89 people and injures more than 500 others.
Two passenger trains collide in the Swiss municipality of Granges-près-Marnand near Lausanne injuring 25 people.
Gunmen open fire at a Sunni mosque in the city of Quetta killing at least ten people and injuring 30.
Egypt declares a state of emergency as security forces kill hundreds of demonstrators supporting former president Mohamed Morsi.
UPS Airlines Flight 1354 crashes short of the runway at Birmingham–Shuttlesworth International Airport, killing both crew members on board.
A riot at the Palmasola prison complex in Santa Cruz, Bolivia kills 31 people.
A VIA Rail train crashes into a double-decker bus at a train station in Ottawa, Canada, killing six people and injuring 35 others.
A 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes southern Pakistan, killing at least 327 people.
Over 42 people are killed by members of Boko Haram at the College of Agriculture in Nigeria.
At least 360 migrants are killed when their boat sinks near the Italian island of Lampedusa.
A migrant boat sinks in the Channel of Sicily, with at least 359 people drowning.
A stampede occurs in India during the Hindu festival Navratri, killing 115 and injuring more than 110.
The 7.2 Mw Bohol earthquake strikes the Philippines. At least 215 were killed.
One hundred and five people are injured in a train crash in Buenos Aires.
Five people are killed and 38 are injured after a car crashes into barriers at Tiananmen Square in China.
Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) launched (5 November)
NASA launches the MAVEN probe to Mars.
Iran signs an interim agreement with the P5+1 countries, limiting its nuclear program in exchange for reduced sanctions.
A bus falls from an elevated highway in Manila, capital of the Philippines, killing at least 18 people with 20 injured.
An Irkut-Avia Antonov An-12 crashes on approach to Irkutsk Northwest Airport, killing all nine people on board.
A launch of the communication satellite GSAT-14 aboard the GSLV MK.II D5 marks the first successful flight of an Indian cryogenic engine.
An explosion at a Mitsubishi Materials chemical plant in Yokkaichi, Japan, kills at least five people and injures 17 others.
A bomb attack on an army convoy in the city of Bannu kills at least 26 Pakistani soldiers and injures 38 others.
Rojava conflict: The Jazira Canton declares its autonomy from the Syrian Arab Republic.
Rojava conflict: The Kobanî Canton declares its autonomy from the Syrian Arab Republic.
Rojava conflict: The Afrin Canton declares its autonomy from the Syrian Arab Republic.
A school shooting in Moscow, Russia leaves two people dead and one wounded.
A hotel fire in Medina, Saudi Arabia, kills 15 Egyptian pilgrims with 130 others injured.
The first same-sex marriages in England and Wales are performed.
Three people are killed in a shooting in Overland Park, Kansas.
Two bombs detonate at a bus station in Nyanya, Nigeria, killing at least 88 people and injuring hundreds. Boko Haram claims responsibility.
A bomb blast in Ürümqi, China kills three people and injures 79 others.
Two mudslides in Badakhshan, Afghanistan, leave up to 2,500 people missing.
Fifteen people are killed and 46 injured in Kinshasa, DRC, in a stampede caused by tear gas being thrown into soccer stands by police officers.
An explosion at an underground coal mine in southwest Turkey kills 301 miners.
Twelve people are killed in two explosions in the Gikomba market area of Nairobi, Kenya.
Random killings occur on the Bannan Line of the Taipei MRT, killing four and injuring 24.
A 6.4 magnitude earthquake occurs in the Aegean Sea between Greece and Turkey, injuring 324 people.
At least three people are killed in a shooting at Brussels' Jewish Museum of Belgium.
Narendra Modi takes oath as the 15th Prime Minister of India.
Telangana officially becomes the 29th state of India, formed from ten districts of northwestern Andhra Pradesh.
At least fourteen people are killed when a Gas Authority of India Limited pipeline explodes in the East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh, India.
Israel launches an offensive on Gaza amid rising tensions following the kidnapping and murder of three Israeli teenagers.
Germany wins the FIFA World Cup, defeating Argentina in the final 1–0 after extra time.
A magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes the San Francisco Bay Area; it is the largest in that area since 1989.
Mangalyaan enters Mars orbit on its first try (24 September)
The Mars Orbiter Mission makes India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit, and the first nation in the world to do so in its first attempt.
The Philae lander, deployed from the European Space Agency's Rosetta probe, reaches the surface of Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko.
While playing with a toy gun in Cleveland, 12-year-old African American Tamir Rice is killed by a white police officer.
The annual furry convention Midwest FurFest is targeted in an unsolved chlorine gas attack.
Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan militants attack an Army Public School in Peshawar, Pakistan, killing 150 people, 132 of them schoolchildren.
Indonesia AirAsia Flight 8501 crashes into the Karimata Strait en route from Surabaya to Singapore, killing all 162 people aboard.
Boko Haram militants destroy the entire town of Baga in north-east Nigeria, starting the Baga massacre and killing as many as 2,000 people.
A car bomb explodes outside a police college in the Yemeni capital Sanaa with at least 38 people reported dead and more than 63 injured.
A mass poisoning at a funeral in Mozambique involving beer that was contaminated with Burkholderia gladioli leaves 75 dead and over 230 people ill.
Government raids kill 143 Boko Haram fighters in Kolofata, Cameroon.
The Swiss National Bank abandons the cap on the Swiss franc's value relative to the euro, causing turmoil in international financial markets.
An aircraft crashes at Los Llanos Air Base in Albacete, Spain, killing 11 people and injuring 21 others.
Eighteen people are killed and 78 injured in a stampede at a Mardi Gras parade in Haiti.
At least 310 people are killed in avalanches in northeastern Afghanistan.
Germanwings Flight 9525 crashes in the French Alps in an apparent pilot mass murder-suicide, killing all 150 people on board.
Ten people are killed in a bomb attack on a convoy carrying food supplies to a United Nations compound in Garowe in the Somali region of Puntland.
A ship carrying 458 people capsizes in the Yangtze river in China's Hubei province, killing 442 people.
The Afghan National Assembly building is attacked by gunmen after a suicide bombing. All six of the gunmen are killed and 18 people are injured.
Chile claims its first title in international football by defeating Argentina in the 2015 Copa América final.
NASA's New Horizons probe performs the first flyby of Pluto, and thus completes the initial survey of the Solar System.
The United States and Cuba resume full diplomatic relations after five decades.
NASA announces discovery of Kepler-452b by the Kepler space telescope.
Seven people are killed and many injured after gunmen attack an Indian police station in Punjab.
The first piece of suspected debris from Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 is discovered on Réunion Island.
A suicide bomb attack kills at least 15 people at a mosque in the Saudi city of Abha.
The U.S. Embassy in Havana, Cuba re-opens after 54 years of being closed when Cuba–United States relations were broken off.
North Korea moves its clock back half an hour to introduce Pyongyang Time, 81⁄2 hours ahead of UTC.
LIGO detects gravitational waves (14 September)
The first observation of gravitational waves is made, announced by the LIGO and Virgo collaborations on 11 February 2016.
At least 1,100 people are killed and another 934 wounded after a stampede during the Hajj in Saudi Arabia.
Forty-two people are killed and 33 go missing in the Kunduz hospital airstrike in Afghanistan.
A 7.5 magnitude earthquake strikes in the Hindu Kush mountain range in South Asia, killing 399 people and leaving 2,536 people injured.
Rona Ambrose takes over after Stephen Harper as the Leader of the Conservative Party of Canada.
Two suicide bombers detonate explosives in Bourj el-Barajneh, Beirut, killing 43 people and injuring over 200 others.
An explosion on a bus carrying Tunisian Presidential Guard personnel in Tunisia's capital Tunis leaves at least 14 people dead.
San Bernardino attack: Syed Rizwan Farook and Tashfeen Malik kill 14 people and wound 22 at the Inland Regional Center in San Bernardino, California.
Venezuelan parliamentary election: For the first time in 17 years, the United Socialist Party of Venezuela loses its majority in parliament.
The JAXA probe Akatsuki successfully enters orbit around Venus five years after the first attempt.
The Paris Agreement relating to United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is adopted.
A violent EF-4 tornado hits Garland, Texas, killing nine and injuring almost 500 others.
In response to the execution of Nimr al-Nimr, Iran ends its diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia.
Ten people are killed and 15 wounded in a bombing near the Blue Mosque in Istanbul.
President Barack Obama announces the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, an agreement intended to limit Iran's nuclear program.
New Zealand politician Steven Joyce is hit by a flung rubber dildo in a Waitangi Day protest.
Two passenger trains collide in the German town of Bad Aibling in the state of Bavaria. Twelve people die and 85 others are injured.
Military vehicles explode outside a Turkish Armed Forces barracks in Ankara, Turkey, killing at least 29 people and injuring 61 others.
Three people are killed and fourteen others injured in a series of shootings in the small Kansas cities of Newton and Hesston.
NASA astronaut Scott Kelly and Roscosmos cosmonaut Mikhail Kornienko return to Earth after a yearlong mission at the International Space Station.
An earthquake of 6.6 magnitude strikes 39 km west-southwest of Ashkasham, impacting India, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Srinagar and Pakistan.
The Paris Agreement is signed, an agreement to help fight global warming.
One hundred and ten people are killed in an ISIL bombing in Baghdad.
Barack Obama is the first president of the United States to visit Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park and meet Hibakusha.
Brexit:  The United Kingdom votes in a referendum to leave the European Union, by 52% to 48%.
Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron resigns, and is succeeded by Theresa May.
An earthquake strikes Central Italy with a magnitude of 6.2, with aftershocks felt as far as Rome and Florence. Around 300 people are killed.
The U.S. and China, together responsible for 40% of the world's carbon emissions, both formally ratify the Paris global climate agreement.
NASA launches OSIRIS-REx, its first asteroid sample return mission. The probe visited 101955 Bennu and returned with samples in September 2023.
Eleven days after the Uri attack, the Indian Army conducts "surgical strikes" against suspected militants in Pakistani-administered Kashmir.
Ethiopian protests break out during a festival in the Oromia region, killing dozens of people.
In the wake of Hurricane Matthew, the death toll rises to over 800.
The Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army launches its first attack on Myanmar security forces along the Bangladesh–Myanmar border.
The Maldives announces its decision to withdraw from the Commonwealth of Nations.
The Chicago Cubs defeat the Cleveland Indians in the World Series, ending the longest Major League Baseball championship drought at 108 years.
Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces launch an offensive to capture the ISIL-held city of Raqqa.
LaMia Flight 2933 crashes near Medellín, Colombia, killing 71 of 77 people on board, including members of the Brazilian football club Chapecoense
Thirty-six people die in a fire at a converted Oakland, California, warehouse serving as an artist collective.
Aerosucre Flight 157 crashes during takeoff from Germán Olano Airport in Puerto Carreño, Colombia, killing five people.
Five people are killed and six others injured in a mass shooting at Fort Lauderdale–Hollywood International Airport in Broward County, Florida.
The search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 is announced to be suspended.
A gunman opens fire at the Islamic Cultural Centre of Quebec City, killing six people and wounding 19 others in a spree shooting.
ISRO launches 104 satellites on one rocket (15 February)
Syria conducts an air strike on Khan Shaykhun using chemical weapons, killing 89 civilians.
U.S. President Donald Trump orders the 2017 Shayrat missile strike against Syria in retaliation for the Khan Shaykhun chemical attack.
Andrew Scheer takes over after Rona Ambrose as the leader of the Conservative Party of Canada.

A Myanmar Air Force Shaanxi Y-8 crashes into the Andaman Sea near Dawei, Myanmar, killing all 122 aboard.
A series of terrorist attacks take place in Pakistan, resulting in 96 deaths and wounding 200 others.
Nawaz Sharif was disqualified from office for life by Supreme Court of Pakistan after finding him guilty of corruption charges.
The National Space Agency of Taiwan successfully launches the observation satellite Formosat-5 into space.
Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) declare victory in the Raqqa campaign.
Catalonia declares independence from Spain.
Devin Patrick Kelley kills 26 and injures 22 in a church in Sutherland Springs, Texas.
Shamshad TV is attacked by gunmen and suicide bombers, with a security guard killed and 20 people wounded; ISIS claims responsibility for the attack.
A terrorist attack on a Mosque in Al-Rawda, North Sinai, Egypt kills 311 people and injures 128.
Donald Trump's administration officially announces the recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.
A false emergency alert warning of an impending missile strike in Hawaii causes widespread panic in the state.
Myanmar police open fire on a group of ethnic Rakhine protesters, killing seven and wounding twelve.
The China–United States trade war begins when President Donald Trump places tariffs on Chinese solar panels and washing machines.
Former doctor Larry Nassar is sentenced up to 175 years in prison after being found guilty of using his position to sexually abuse female gymnasts.
Winter Olympics: Opening ceremony is performed in Pyeongchang County in South Korea.
Iran Aseman Airlines Flight 3704 crashes in the Dena sub-range in the Zagros Mountains of Iran, Resulting in 66 Deaths

Students across the United States stage the March for Our Lives demanding gun control in response to the Stoneman Douglas High School shooting.
The Israeli Army kills 17 Palestinians and wounds 1,400 in Gaza during Land Day protests.
Syria launches the Douma chemical attack during the Eastern Ghouta offensive of the Syrian Civil War.
An Ilyushin Il-76 owned and operated by the Algerian Air Force crashes near Boufarik, Algeria, killing 257.
King Mswati III of Swaziland announces that his country's name will change to Eswatini.
The Panmunjom Declaration is signed between North and South Korea, officially declaring their intentions to end the Korean conflict.
The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) becomes enforceable in the European Union.
United States President Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un of North Korea hold the first meeting between leaders of their two countries in Singapore.
France win their second World Cup title, defeating Croatia 4–2.
The Knesset passes the controversial Nationality Bill, which defines the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people.
Australian Wendy Tuck becomes the first female skipper to win the Clipper Round the World Yacht Race.
The collapse of the Ponte Morandi bridge in Genoa, Italy, left 16 people injured and 43 people killed.
At least 161 people die after a ferry capsizes close to the pier on Ukara Island in Lake Victoria, Tanzania.
Bill Cosby is sentenced to three to ten years in prison for aggravated sexual assault.
The Washington Post journalist Jamal Khashoggi is assassinated in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey.
Soyuz MS-10, launching an intended crew for the ISS, suffers an in-flight abort. The crew lands safely.
13-year-old American girl, Jayme Closs, is kidnapped from her Barron, Wisconsin home after her parents were both murdered.
A passenger train derails in Yilan County, Taiwan, killing 18 people and injuring 187.
A gunman opens fire on a Pittsburgh synagogue killing eleven and injuring six, including four police officers.
The Oulu Police informed the public about the first offence of the much larger child sexual exploitation in Oulu, Finland.
The 2018–2019 United States federal government shutdown, the second-longest shutdown of the U.S. federal government in history, begins.
Chang'e 4 makes the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon, deploying the Yutu-2 lunar rover.
A fire in an escape room in Koszalin, Poland, kills five teenagers through carbon monoxide poisoning.
Muhammad V of Kelantan resigns as the Yang di-Pertuan Agong of Malaysia, becoming the first monarch to do so.
A Saha Airlines Boeing 707 crashes at Fath Air Base near Karaj in Alborz Province, Iran, killing 15 people.
Somali militants attack the DusitD2 hotel in Nairobi, Kenya killing at least 21 people and injuring 19.
Pope Francis becomes the first Pope in history to visit and perform papal mass in the Arabian Peninsula during his visit to Abu Dhabi.
Indian Air Force fighter-jets target Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist training camps in Balakot, Pakistan.
A redacted version of the Mueller report is released to the United States Congress and the public.
Eight bombs explode at churches, hotels, and other locations in Sri Lanka on Easter Sunday, killing at least 269.
Naruhito ascends to the throne of Japan succeeding his father Akihito, beginning the Reiwa period.
Twenty-two students die in a fire in Surat (India).
A shooting occurs inside a municipal building at Virginia Beach, Virginia, leaving 13 people dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.
The United States defeated the Netherlands 2–0 at the 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup final in Lyon, France.
A GippsAero GA8 Airvan crashes in Umeå, Sweden, killing all nine aboard.
Soyuz MS-13 is launched to the International Space Station on the 50th anniversary of the Apollo 11 moon landing.
Chandrayaan-2 launched (22 July)
Boris Johnson becomes Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after defeating Jeremy Hunt in a leadership contest, succeeding Theresa May.
Hurricane Dorian, a category 5 hurricane, devastates the Bahamas, killing at least five.
Yemen's Houthi rebels claim responsibility for an attack on Saudi Arabian oil facilities.
Twenty people die on the first of two days of rioting in Papua and West Papua over an alleged racist incident.
About 200 Extinction Rebellion activists block the gates of Leinster House (parliament) in the Republic of Ireland.
Kenyan Brigid Kosgei sets a new world record for a woman runner with a time of 2:14:04 at the 2019 Chicago Marathon.
The first known case of COVID-19 is traced to a 55-year-old man who had visited a market in Wuhan, Hubei Province, China.
The outbreak of coronavirus infection begins in Wuhan.
Bek Air Flight 2100 crashes during takeoff from Almaty International Airport in Almaty, Kazakhstan, killing 13.
The 6.4Mw 2019–20 Puerto Rico earthquakes kill four and injure nine in southern Puerto Rico.
COVID-19 pandemic in Hubei: Municipal health officials in Wuhan announce the first recorded death from COVID-19.
Taal Volcano in the Philippines erupts and kills 39 people.
The Thai Ministry of Public Health confirms the first case of COVID-19 outside China.
A plinth breaks between Coral Edge and Riviera in Singapore, Coral Edge closes one platform.
The World Health Organization declares the COVID-19 pandemic to be a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
The United Kingdom's membership within the European Union ceases in accordance with Article 50, after 47 years of being a member state.
The COVID-19 pandemic causes all casinos in Macau to be closed down for 15 days.
United States President Donald Trump is acquitted by the United States Senate in his first impeachment trial.
Pegasus Airlines Flight 2193 overshoots the runway at Sabiha Gökçen International Airport and crashes, killing three people and injuring 179.
The World Health Organization (WHO) declares the COVID-19 virus epidemic a pandemic.
Prime Minister Boris Johnson puts the United Kingdom into its first national lockdown in response to COVID-19.
COVID-19 pandemic: China ends its lockdown in Wuhan.
A killing spree in Nova Scotia, Canada, leaves 22 people and the perpetrator dead, making it the deadliest rampage in the country's history.
For the first time in history, oil prices drop below zero, an effect of the 2020 Russia-Saudi Arabia oil price war.
The COVID-19 recession causes the U.S. unemployment rate to hit 14.9 percent, its worst rate since the Great Depression.
After a five-day search, the body of American actress and singer Naya Rivera is recovered from Lake Piru in California, where she had drowned.
NASA's Mars 2020 mission is launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
Beirut Port explosion: At least 220 people are killed and over 5,000 are wounded when 2,700 tons of ammonium nitrate explodes in Beirut, Lebanon.
Derecho in Iowa becomes the most costly thunderstorm disaster in U.S. history.
Erin O'Toole is elected leader of the Conservative Party of Canada.
Pope Benedict XVI becomes the longest-lived pope, 93 years, four months, 16 days, surpassing Pope Leo XIII, who died in 1903.
Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: Azerbaijan twice targets the Church of the Holy Savior Ghazanchetsots of Shusha.
In Vienna's Innere Stadt district, an ISIL sympathizer shoots and kills four people and injures 23 more, before being shot and killed by the police.

The Utah monolith, built sometime in 2016 is discovered by state biologists of the Utah Division of Wildlife Resources.
Over seven hundred civilians are massacred by the Ethiopian National Defense Force and Eritrean Army in Aksum, Ethiopia.
Cannabis is removed from the list of most dangerous drugs of the international drug control treaty by the UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs.
Twenty-three people are killed in what is described as a police ″massacre″ in La Vega, Caracas, Venezuela.
Protesters and farmers storm the Red Fort near Delhi, clashing with police. One protester is killed and more than 80 police officers are injured.
A nitrogen leak at a poultry food processing facility in Gainesville, Georgia kills six and injures at least ten.
A coup d'état in Myanmar removes Aung San Suu Kyi from power and restores military rule.
Perseverance, a Mars rover designed to explore Jezero crater on Mars, as part of NASA's Mars 2020 mission, lands successfully.
A total of 279 female students aged between 10 and 17 are kidnapped by bandits in the Zamfara kidnapping in Zamfara State, Nigeria.
US President Joe Biden signs the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan into law.
The ship Ever Given is dislodged from the Suez Canal.
Indonesian Navy submarine KRI Nanggala (402) sinks in the Bali Sea during a military drill, killing all 53 on board.
China successfully lands Zhurong, the country's first Mars rover.
Ten people are killed in a shooting at a VTA rail yard in San Jose, California, United States.
An Antonov An-26 operating as Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Air Flight 251 crashes on approach to Palana Airport, killing all 28 aboard.
Haitian crisis: Haitian President Jovenel Moïse is assassinated in his residence in the capital of Port-au-Prince.
American businessman Jeff Bezos flies to space aboard New Shepard NS-16 operated by his private spaceflight company Blue Origin.
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake strikes southwestern Haiti, killing at least 2,248 people and causing a humanitarian crisis.
The Cumbre Vieja volcano, on the island of La Palma in the Canary Islands, erupts. The eruption lasts for almost three months, ending on December 13.
Eight people are killed in an airplane crash near Milan, Italy.
The Los Angeles Superior Court formally ends the 14-year conservatorship to pop singer Britney Spears.
Three people are killed when a 14-year-old opens fire on civilians at a Texaco convenience store in Garland, Texas.
Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev dismisses Prime Minister Asqar Mamin and declares state of emergency over the 2022 Kazakh unrest.
Sue Gray, a senior civil servant in the United Kingdom, publishes an initial version of her report on the Downing Street Partygate controversy.
Russian invasion of Ukraine: The Russian warship Moskva is struck by two anti-ship missiles and sinks into the Black Sea.
The Burmese military executes at least 37 villagers during the Mon Taing Pin massacre in Sagaing, Myanmar.
Ten people are killed in a mass shooting in Buffalo, New York.
Russo-Ukrainian war: Russia claims full control of the Ukrainian city of Mariupol after a nearly three-month siege.
A mass shooting occurs at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, United States, resulting in the deaths of 21 people, including 19 children.
Former Japanese prime minister Shinzo Abe is shot and killed with an improvised firearm due to resentment against the Unification Church.
Catastrophic floods devastate Eastern Kentucky, resulting in 45 fatalities and causing damage to thousands of homes and businesses.
Ten people are killed and 15 are injured in  a stabbing spree in 13 locations on the James Smith Cree Nation and in Weldon, Saskatchewan.
The state funeral of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom is held at Westminster Abbey, London.
A strong earthquake kills 2 and injures over 30 in Mexico's state of Michoacán.
Svante Pääbo is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
Ales Bialiatski, along with two organisations, Memorial and Center for Civil Liberties, are awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
Ten people are killed and eight are injured in an explosion at a petrol station in Creeslough, Ireland.
A peace agreement is signed between the Ethiopian government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, ending the Tigray War.
Russo-Ukrainian War: Ukrainian armed forces enter the city of Kherson following a successful two-month southern counteroffensive.
A Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress and a Bell P-63 Kingcobra collide in mid-air over Dallas Executive Airport during an airshow, killing six.
A mass stabbing occurs in Moscow, Idaho in which four University of Idaho students are killed in off-campus housing.
Artemis Program: NASA launches Artemis 1 on the first flight of the Space Launch System, the start of the program's future missions to the moon.
A shooting at a Walmart in Chesapeake, Virginia leaves seven workers dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.
A landslide occurs at a camp at an organic farm near the town of Batang Kali in Selangor, Malaysia, trapping 92 people and killing 31.
A Vega C rocket carrying two Pléiades Neo satellites fails after liftoff.
Supporters of former Brazil president Jair Bolsonaro storm the Brazilian Congress.
A shooting at a synagogue in Neve Yaakov, East Jerusalem, kills seven people and injures three others.
An attack on the Azerbaijani embassy in Pasdaran, Tehran, kills one person and injures three others.
Protests begin in the United States after police beat and kill Tyre Nichols.
The Burmese military kills at least 30 villagers, including 3 Buddhist monks, during the Pinlaung massacre in Shan State, Myanmar.
An EF4 tornado strikes the towns of Rolling Fork and Silver City, Mississippi, causing mass destruction.
Donald Trump becomes the first former United States president to be indicted by a grand jury.
Finland becomes a member of NATO after Turkey accepts its membership request.
A mass shooting occurs at the Old National Bank in Louisville, Kentucky, that leaves five victims dead and eight wounded.
During the Pazigyi massacre, an airstrike conducted by the Myanmar Air Force kills at least 100 villagers in Pazigyi, Sagaing Region.
The house of Jack Teixeira is raided in an investigation into leaked Pentagon documents; he is arrested on the same day.
The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (JUICE) is launched by the European Space Agency.
The World Health Organization declares the end of the COVID-19 pandemic as a global health emergency.
The May 9 riots following the arrest of Imran Khan in Pakistan.
Russo-Ukrainian war: The Kakhovka Dam is destroyed.
At least 100 people are killed when a wedding boat capsizes on the Niger River in Kwara State, Nigeria.
Three people are killed and another three injured in an early morning stabbing and van ramming attack in Nottingham, England.
The Wagner Group led by Yevgeny Prigozhin launches an insurrection against the Russian government.
Former US President Donald Trump is indicted for his role in the January 6 United States Capitol attack, his third indictment in 2023.
Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole (23 August)
Gabonese coup d'état: After Ali Bongo Ondimba's reelection, a military coup ousts him, ending 56 years of Bongo family rule in Gabon.
A magnitude 6.9 earthquake strikes Morocco, killing nearly 3,000 people and damaging historic sites in Marrakesh.
NASA's OSIRIS-REx capsule containing samples from the asteroid 101955 Bennu successfully lands back on Earth.
Wab Kinew is elected to be the first First Nations Premier of a Canadian province in the 2023 Manitoba general election

António Costa resigns as Prime Minister of Portugal following news of an investigation in a corruption scandal implicating members of his cabinet.
Hibiscus Rising, commemorating David Oluwale, is unveiled in Leeds.

Disney's copyright protection on Steamboat Willie and the original Mickey Mouse expires as they enter the public domain.
Two aircraft collide on a runway at Haneda Airport in Tokyo, killing 5 and injuring 18.
Queen Margrethe II abdicates as Queen of Denmark and is succeeded by her son, Frederik X.
The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's probe lands on the moon, making Japan the 5th country to land a spacecraft on the moon.
Ram Mandir is inaugurated by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh after 500 years of dispute.
Northwestern Air Flight 738 crashes after takeoff from Fort Smith Airport, Northwest Territories, Canada, killing six people.
An Ilyushin Il-76 crashes in Russia's Korochansky District, killing all 74 people on board.
Pakistan election offices are hit by twin bombings, killing at least 24 people a day before general elections.
Start/Middle of the May 2024 Solar Storms, the most powerful set of geomagnetic storms since the 2003 Halloween solar storms.
Prime Minister of Slovakia Robert Fico is shot and critically injured while meeting with supporters at an event in Handlová.
A stabbing spree on the Green line of the Taichung MRT injures four people, including the perpetrator.
The launch of SpaceX Starship integrated flight test 4 (IFT-4)
A plane crash in Malawi leaves 10 people dead, including the country's Vice President Saulos Chilima.
A fire in a residential building in Mangaf, Kuwait City kills at least 50 people.
A stampede during a religious event in Uttar Pradesh, India, leaves at least 121 people dead and 150 others injured.

A series of landslides occurs in Kerala, India, causing over 420 fatalities.
Voepass Linhas Aéreas Flight 2283 crashes near Vinhedo, São Paulo, killing all 62 people on board.
Israel strikes Al-Tabaeen school in eastern Gaza City, killing at least 80 Palestinians.
At least 129 inmates are killed and 59 more injured in an attempted prison break at Makala Prison in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
A 14-year-old gunman kills four people and injures seven in a mass shooting at Apalachee High School near Winder, Georgia.
Israel launches airstrikes against Hezbollah targets in Lebanon, killing more than 490 people.
Bengali, Assamese, Marathi, Pali and Prakrit are accorded the Classical language status by the Government of India
Thick of It, a single by British Internet personality and rapper KSI featuring Trippie Redd, is released.
Syrian rebel groups led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham launch a ground offensive into Syria.
Battle of Damascus (2024): Syrian opposition forces enter the Rif Dimashq Governorate, reaching within 20 km of the capital Damascus.
The Abundant Life Christian School shooting in Madison, Wisconsin, United States, takes place, resulting in the death of three people.
Six people are killed and over 200 are injured when an anti-Islam activist drives a car into a crowd at a Christmas market in Magdeburg, Germany.
Fourteen people are killed and 57 others injured during a vehicle-ramming and shooting attack in New Orleans, Louisiana.
Justin Trudeau announces his resignation as leader of the Liberal Party of Canada and Prime Minister of Canada after nine years in office.
A series of wildfires ravage the Greater Los Angeles area, resulting in at least 16 deaths and 13,401 structures destroyed.
A fire at the Grand Kartal Hotel in the Kartalkaya ski resort in Bolu Province, Turkey, results in 78 people dead and 51 injured.
A chartered Beechcraft 1900 crashes near the Unity oilfield in South Sudan, killing 20 people.
Med Jets Flight 056 crashes near Roosevelt Mall in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, killing 8 people and injuring 23.
Ten people are killed in a mass shooting at an adult education centre in Örebro, Sweden.
Rory McIlroy wins the Masters Tournament, becoming just the sixth person to complete the Grand Slam in golf.
A car ramming attack at a Lapu-Lapu Day festival kills 11 people and injures at least 30 in Vancouver, Canada.
A devastating EF4 tornado kills nineteen people in Southeast Kentucky, hitting the towns of Somerset and London.
65 people are injured when a car rams into a crowd on Water Street, near Liverpool F.C.'s Premier League trophy parade.
Eleven people are killed, including the perpetrator, and eleven others are injured, in a mass shooting at a secondary school in Graz, Austria.
The United States conducts airstrikes on three Iranian nuclear sites in Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan.
The Oasis Live '25 tour begins in Principality Stadium, Cardiff, ending a 16-year hiatus.
Angara Airlines Flight 2311 crashes on approach to Tynda Airport, killing all 48 people on board.
US president Donald Trump meets with Russian president Vladimir Putin in Alaska, the first such summit since the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.
Balçova police station shooting: Four people, including the perpetrator are killed an attack on a police station in Turkey.
Six people are killed when Israel carries out an airstrike on Doha in a failed attempt to decapitate the Hamas leadership.
2 people are killed and at least 4 others injured in an attack on a synagogue in Manchester, UK, during Yom Kippur.
A coup d'état successfully overthrows Malagasy president Andry Rajoelina.
Pieces of the French Crown Jewels are successfully stolen during a heist on the Louvre Museum in Paris..
Canadian ostrich cull: The Government of Canada kills 314 ostriches after H5N8 is detected in an ostrich farm in Edgewood, BC.
British racing driver Lando Norris wins the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025 with McLaren.
Israel recognises Somaliland as an independent state, becoming the first country to do so.
An estimated €30 million were stolen from a Sparkasse bank in Gelsenkirchen, Germany.
Unrest in the form of mass protests erupt across Iran, the largest uprising in the country since the Iranian Revolution.
Thirty-two people are killed when a crane falls onto a passenger train in Sikhio district, Thailand.
Indonesia Air Transport ATR 42 crashed near Mount Bulusaraung in South Sulawesi, after losing contact en route to Makassar.
At least 70 people are killed and 10 others missing after major landslides in West Java, Indonesia.
The Rubaya mine collapse at Rubaya mines in DR Congo causes at least 400 deaths and injured several others.
Islamist militants massacred at least 162 while injuring and kidnapping dozens in two villages in Kwara State, Nigeria.
The government of Pakistan declares "open war" against the Taliban in Afghanistan, initiating the 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan War.
Bam Adebayo of the Miami Heat recorded the second-highest scoring game in NBA history with 83 Points.
Seven people are killed and fourteen others are injured in a mass shooting in Kyiv, Ukraine
A suicide bombing targeting a shuttle train in Quetta, Balochistan, killed at least 48 people and injured 98 others.
South African-American businessman Elon Musk becomes the first US$ trillionaire with the initial public offering of SpaceX.
